## What landed

| Issue | PR | What you'll see in-game |
|-------|-----|------------------------|
| #64 fountain | #68 | A real tiered fountain in the park — stone basin brimming with water, column, upper bowl, finial — built from primitives since the pack has none |

- **Screenshot round-trips caught three real bugs**: the fountain read as a pancake (SizeSpec raised 1.2→2.6), its water was hidden by raylib's capped-solid cylinders (discs now float above the caps), and the first-draft parked cars sat mid-lane in oversized collision boxes (now curb-hugging, sized to the visual car).

   doesn't break proportions on top of everything else.

# Plan: Character Creator — player-authored persona + socketed look
Date: 2026-07-05 (overnight, autonomous — decisions logged here and in OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md)
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: L

## The Idea (one paragraph)
A Mii-style character creator inside the existing pause-menu system: the
player writes a personality (name, backstory, traits) and assembles a look
from interchangeable 3D parts (body, head, eyes, hair) with a palette, sees
a live preview, and spawns the character into the town where it talks
through the exact same LLM persona pipeline as the designer-authored NPCs.
Personality and look are two fully independent records, stored separately
in the game's established SQLite persistence, keyed by character_id.

## Goal
The player can create a named character with a custom personality and a
custom parts-based look, spawn it in the town, walk up and have a
conversation with it — and find it still there (same look, same
personality, same memory hooks) after restarting the game.

## Premise corrections vs the brief (decisions logged)
1. "Sprite pixel dimensions" — the game is 3D now (raylib 5.5, KayKit
   rigged characters, primitives). The size-contract system is about WORLD
   size vs native MODEL dimensions. Mii-style parts therefore = low-poly
   3D primitive composites (the issue-#64 fountain pattern), not sprites.
   KayKit's rigged characters are single skinned meshes and cannot donate
   swappable heads/hair, so parts are authored primitive recipes in the
   same flat-color art style.
2. "Storage approach the conversation-persistence work established" — that
   shipped (vendored SQLite + ConversationStore, merged to main via #57/
   #59). CharacterStore follows its exact pattern.

## Core design decisions (autonomous, most-defensible)
- **Socket contract**: every PartDef declares, in ITS OWN local space:
  an implicit anchor at its origin, its local bounding size, and a map of
  named child sockets ("head", "eyes", "hair" → Vec3). Assembly recursively
  places each part at its parent's socket; there is no per-pair offset
  table anywhere. Adding a part = adding one PartDef; adding a category =
  one more socket name, no restructuring.
- **Size-contract interaction** (brief flagged it): sockets resolve in
  UNSCALED local space first; the finished assembly is measured and then
  uniformly scaled so its total height equals the character height
  contract (1.8 world units, same as pack characters). One Uniform
  contract for the whole assembly — no parallel sizing system, no per-part
  world sizes.
- **Style tags**: each part carries a styleTag ("round", "blocky", or
  "any"). A look is valid iff all its parts are pairwise compatible
  (equal tags, or either is "any"). The picker and randomizer only offer
  compatible parts; the core validator enforces it.
- **Persona format**: player input is serialized to the SAME `.persona`
  key=value text format the roster uses and parsed back with the existing
  `parsePersonaText` — one format, one parser, zero new dialogue logic.
- **Independence**: `character_look` and `character_persona` are separate
  SQLite tables (and separate C++ records) joined only by character_id, per
  the ticket. The spawn path is the only place both are read.
- **Animation v1**: composite characters get procedural motion only
  (walk bob + idle sway derived from the walking flag) — no skeleton.
  Rigged animation for composites is out of scope; logged as future work.
- **Live preview**: while the creator page is open, main.cpp draws the
  draft look as a composite character a few units in front of the camera
  (the menu already renders over the live 3D frame, so the preview is a
  real in-engine render, rotating slowly for inspection).
- **Branch/PR**: one branch `feature/character-creator` stacked on the
  city-polish chain tip (feature/issue-67-atmosphere-pass) because it
  touches RaylibRenderer/Assets/main which every open PR in the chain
  modifies. One draft PR closing the five tickets below. No merges.

## Out of Scope (this version)
- Rigged/skeletal animation for composite characters; gestures/mood
  billboards for them beyond facing + bob.
- Editing or deleting an existing character (create + spawn only).
- AI-generated personas (the VISION.md cloud-creator concept), part
  unlocks, sharing/export, more than 4 categories (the system leaves room;
  v1 ships body/head/eyes/hair).
- Multiplayer replication of custom looks (NetNpcPose carries no look;
  bump kNetProtocolVersion when that lands).

## Affected Areas
- NEW `src/core/CharacterParts.{hpp,cpp}` — PartDef, the built-in catalog,
  socket assembly (`assembleLook`), style compatibility, `randomizeLook`,
  palette presets. Pure logic, no raylib — fully unit-testable.
- NEW `src/core/CharacterStore.{hpp,cpp}` — SQLite store, two tables
  (`character_persona(character_id, persona_text, updated_at)`,
  `character_look(character_id, look_json, updated_at)`); save/load/list.
  Follows ConversationStore's open/ok/degrade pattern.
- NEW `src/core/CharacterRecord.hpp` — CharacterLook {partId per category,
  paletteId} + (de)serialization to a tiny JSON string; CharacterPersona =
  persona text + spawn position (kept separate from look).
- `src/core/PersonaLoader.hpp/.cpp` — no change (parsePersonaText reused);
  NEW small helper `renderPersonaText(...)` (inverse serializer) added to
  PersonaLoader so format knowledge stays in one file.
- `src/app/RaylibRenderer.{hpp,cpp}` — `drawCompositeCharacter(const
  CharacterLook&, Vec3 pos, float facingDeg, bool walking, float phase)`:
  maps part ids → primitive recipes (flat KayKit-palette colors), applies
  assembly transforms + the 1.8 height contract.
- `src/app/Menu.{hpp,cpp}` — new Page::Creator (reached from Main):
  name/backstory/traits text fields (joinAddress_ editing pattern),
  per-category part cyclers, palette cycler, Randomize, "Save & Spawn";
  CreatorHooks injected by main (onSave, draft-look accessor for preview).
- `src/app/main.cpp` — creator wiring: hooks, preview draw, spawn (Npc +
  world.addNpc + resize wasCaught/npcLastPos), custom-look registry
  (npc index → CharacterLook) so the render loop picks composite vs pack
  model; startup load of all stored characters; memory hooks work as-is
  (keyed by persona name, unchanged).
- `CMakeLists.txt` — new core sources (tests auto-glob).
- NEW `tests/test_character_parts.cpp`, `tests/test_character_store.cpp`.

## Implementation Order (each step committable)
1. Core parts + sockets + catalog + randomize + tests.
2. CharacterRecord + CharacterStore (SQLite) + tests.
3. Renderer: drawCompositeCharacter honoring the height contract;
   screenshot verification of several part combinations.
4. Menu Creator page + main.cpp preview/spawn/persist wiring; screenshot.
5. Tickets closed, draft PR, OVERNIGHT_REPORT update.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Core: every style-compatible combination of catalog parts assembles
      with every category placed and total height > 0; incompatible
      combinations are rejected; randomizeLook(seed) is deterministic and
      always valid. Tests in test_character_parts.cpp.
- [ ] Store: save/load round-trips look and persona independently by
      character_id; corrupt rows degrade (skip, keep going); missing DB →
      ok()==false and the game still runs. Tests in
      test_character_store.cpp.
- [ ] Renderer: screenshots of ≥3 distinct part/palette combinations show
      correctly snapped parts (no floating/embedded parts) at the same
      world height as pack NPCs.
- [ ] UI: creator reachable from the pause menu; typing works in all text
      fields; randomize changes the preview; Save & Spawn places the
      character in the town with a nameplate.
- [ ] Spawn/persist: created character talks via the LLM using its authored
      persona; after restart it re-spawns with the same look and persona.
- [ ] `make -C tests test` green; game builds and smoke-runs.

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|--------------------|
| Empty name on save | Toast "name required"; no save, stay on page. |
| Empty backstory/traits | Allowed; persona renders without those lines. |
| Name collides with roster NPC | Allowed (names aren't keys); memory rows are keyed by name, so a duplicate shares memory — logged as known v1 quirk in the PR. |
| DB unwritable | CharacterStore.ok() false → creator still works this session; toast notes "won't persist". |
| Corrupt look JSON on load | Skip that character with a stderr note; others load. |
| Part id in a stored look no longer in the catalog | Look falls back to the first compatible part of that category (logged), never crashes. |
| Spawn spot occupied | Spawn probes a small ring of offsets around the plaza until circleIntersectsAny is clear. |
| Randomize while editing text | Randomize only touches the look, never the persona fields. |

## Open Questions
None — decisions above were made under the autonomy instructions and are
mirrored in OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. feat(core): character part catalog with socket contracts — assembly,
   style tags, randomize, tests
2. feat(core): CharacterStore — independent persona/look SQLite records
3. feat(render): composite character renderer under the size contract
4. feat(ui): creator menu page — persona fields, part pickers, live
   preview, randomize
5. feat(game): spawn and persist created characters in the town

# Plain-make test runner for the rendering-free core library.
#
# The dev container has g++/make but no cmake or graphics libs, so this is the
# primary way to build and run unit tests there. It compiles every
# src/core/*.cpp plus every tests/test_*.cpp into one doctest binary.
#
#   make -C tests test     # build + run all tests
#   make -C tests clean    # remove build artifacts

CXX      ?= g++
CXXFLAGS ?= -std=c++17 -g -O0 -pthread -Wall -Wextra
INCLUDES := -I../src/core -I../external -I.

BUILD  := build
TARGET := $(BUILD)/run_tests

CORE_SRCS := $(wildcard ../src/core/*.cpp)
TEST_SRCS := $(wildcard test_*.cpp)

CORE_OBJS := $(patsubst ../src/core/%.cpp,$(BUILD)/core_%.o,$(CORE_SRCS))
TEST_OBJS := $(patsubst %.cpp,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(TEST_SRCS))

# Vendored C sources (SQLite amalgamation) — compiled with the C compiler,
# without the C++ warning flags.
CC        ?= cc
SQLITE_OBJ := $(BUILD)/ext_sqlite3.o

.PHONY: test build clean

test: $(TARGET)
	./$(TARGET)

build: $(TARGET)

$(TARGET): $(CORE_OBJS) $(TEST_OBJS) $(SQLITE_OBJ)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $^ -o $@

$(SQLITE_OBJ): ../external/sqlite3.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) -O1 -c $< -o $@

```python
        description=description
```

```python
{what}

{verify}

## Constraints
{constraints}

{economy_note}
```

```python
def plan_and_create_issues(repo, milestone_number: int,
                           specs: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Create a batch of issues. Each spec is a dict with keys:
        title, what, where, verify, constraints, economy_note,
        slug, concept

    Returns list of created issue dicts with number and URL.
    """
    username = os.environ["GITHUB_USERNAME"]
    created = []

    # Ensure overnight labels exist
    create_overnight_labels(repo)

    milestone = repo.get_milestone(milestone_number)

    for spec in specs:
        # Skip if similar issue already exists
        if spec["title"].lower() in existing_titles:
            print(f"Skipping (exists): {spec['title']}")
            continue

        body = ISSUE_TEMPLATE.format(
            what=spec["what"],
            where=spec["where"],
            verify=spec["verify"],
            constraints=spec["constraints"],
            economy_note=spec["economy_note"],
            slug=spec["slug"],
            concept=spec["concept"],
            number="N"    # placeholder — updated after creation
        )

        issue = repo.create_issue(
            title=spec["title"],
            body=body,
            labels=["ready-for-ai"],
            assignees=[username],
            milestone=milestone
        )

        # Update branch name now that we have the number
        updated_body = body.replace(
            "feature/issue/N",
            f"feature/issue-{issue.number}"
        )
        issue.edit(body=updated_body)

        print(f"  Created #{issue.number}: {spec['title']}")
        print(f"  Concept: {spec['concept']}")
        created.append({
            "number":  issue.number,
            "title":   spec["title"],
            "concept": spec["concept"],
            "url":     issue.html_url
        })

    return created
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Draft PR for the character creator + ticket bookkeeping (#72-#76)."""
import os
import time

from github import Github, GithubException

gh = Github(os.environ["GH_TOKEN"])
repo = gh.get_repo("bjl14710/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs")


def retry(fn, what):
    for attempt in range(4):
        try:
            return fn()
        except GithubException as e:
            print(f"{what} attempt {attempt+1}: {e.status}")
            time.sleep(5)
    raise SystemExit(f"gave up: {what}")


body = (
    "Closes #72, closes #73, closes #74, closes #75, closes #76 "
    "(milestone #6). Stacks on #71 (base = "
    "`feature/issue-67-atmosphere-pass`); plan: "
    "`.claude/plans/character-creator.md`.\n\n"
    "## What this delivers\n"
    "Create a character from the pause menu: write a personality (name, "
    "backstory, traits), assemble a Mii-style look from socketed 3D parts "
    "with a palette, watch a live turning preview, and Save & Spawn it "
    "into the town — where it chats through the exact same LLM persona "
    "pipeline (and cross-session memory) as the designer NPCs, and comes "
    "back after a restart.\n\n"
    "## Design (autonomy decisions logged in the plan + report)\n"
    "- **Socket contracts, not per-pair offsets**: every `PartDef` "
    "declares its local size and named child sockets; `CategorySpec` rows "
    "say which parent socket each category snaps to. New part = one data "
    "row; new category = one spec row + sockets on parents.\n"
    "- **Size-contract resolution**: sockets resolve in unscaled local "
    "space, then ONE uniform scale takes the whole assembly to the same "
    "1.8-unit height contract pack characters use — no parallel sizing "
    "system.\n"
    "- **Persona/look independence**: two SQLite tables "
    "(`character_persona`, `character_look`) keyed by character_id, "
    "separate records end to end; the spawn path is the only join. "
    "Player personas serialize via the new `renderPersonaText` — the "
    "exact inverse of `parsePersonaText`, so stored and file personas "
    "share one format and one parser.\n"
    "- **Style tags** (round/blocky/any) gate combinations in the "
    "validator, the picker, and the randomizer; the body anchors the "
    "family and cycling it re-validates the other picks.\n"
    "- **3D premise correction**: the brief's 'sprite pixel dimensions' "
    "predates the raylib migration; parts are low-poly primitive recipes "
    "(the fountain pattern), since KayKit's rigged characters can't "
    "donate swappable parts.\n\n"
    "## Verification\n"
    "- Suite 139 cases / 1384 assertions green (exhaustive part-combo "
    "assembly, determinism, serialization gates, store round-trips, "
    "unopenable-DB degradation, renderPersonaText round-trip).\n"
    "- End-to-end screenshot: three planted store records spawned as "
    "three distinct, correctly-snapped composites at pack-character "
    "height (blocky visor+spikes, round dot+tuft, round wide+bowl).\n"
    "- Composite characters get fog/tint automatically (batch draw path).\n\n"
    "## Needs a human eyeball\n"
    "The Creator page itself (typing, cycling, randomize, save toast) — "
    "scripted smoke runs can't click the menu. Everything below the UI is "
    "test- or screenshot-verified.\n\n"
    "## Known v1 limits (logged)\n"
    "- Composite characters: procedural bob only (no skeleton/gestures/"
    "death pose), no multiplayer look replication (guests see a pack "
    "model), duplicate names share memory rows (names key the memory "
    "store).\n\n"
    "---\n\U0001F916 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)"
)

pr = retry(lambda: repo.create_pull(
    title="feat: character creator — player-authored persona + socketed look",
    body=body,
    head="feature/character-creator",
    base="feature/issue-67-atmosphere-pass",
    draft=True), "create pr")
print(f"PR #{pr.number}: {pr.html_url}")

for number in (72, 73, 74, 75, 76):
    issue = retry(lambda: repo.get_issue(number), f"issue {number}")
    retry(lambda: issue.add_to_labels("ai-completed"), "label")
    try:
        issue.remove_from_labels("ai-in-progress")
    except GithubException:
        pass
    retry(lambda: issue.create_comment(
        f"Implemented in draft PR #{pr.number}. Suite 139/1384 green; "
        "spawn/render verified by screenshot. Creator page needs a human "
        "eyeball pass (noted in the PR)."), "comment")
    retry(lambda: issue.edit(state="closed"), "close")
    print(f"issue #{number} closed")

Lesson 0020 · Systems design · from PR #77 (character creator)

Socket Contracts: Per-Part Attach Points vs Per-Pair Offsets

The character creator's core promise is "any combination of parts renders correctly". Whether that promise scales depends entirely on where the attachment knowledge lives.

The trap: per-pair offsets

The obvious first implementation is a table of hand-tuned offsets: "round eyes on the blocky head sit at (0, 0.42, 0.38); on the round head at (0, 0.40, 0.30)…" That table grows as parts × parts — adding one head means re-tuning an offset against every eye and hair part, and a missed pair ships as floating eyeballs.

The contract: each part describes only itself

PartDef {
  id:        "head_round"
  localSize: (0.72, 0.72, 0.72)      // anchor at bottom-center
  sockets:   { eyes: (0, .40, .30),   // MY eye position, MY local space
               hair: (0, .64, 0) }
}
CategorySpec rows:  Head→Body via "head",  Eyes→Head via "eyes",  Hair→Head via "hair"

Assembly is a fold over the category specs: each part lands at parent anchor + parent's declared socket. Knowledge is parts + categories, not parts²: a wider head declares its eye socket farther forward and every eye part inherits that placement for free. Adding a category (a hat, a held item) is one spec row plus socket entries on the parts that can carry it — no restructuring.

Where the size contract fits

The brief flagged the interaction. Resolution order is the whole answer: sockets resolve in unscaled local space first, the assembly's total height is measured, then one uniform scale takes the figure to the same 1.8-unit character height contract the pack models use. Scale per-part and sockets drift; scale once at the end and alignment is invariant. Swapping the art style later means re-authoring parts — the contract keeps world proportions fixed on top of everything else.

Guard rails that make it hold

  • Style tags (round/blocky/any) gate combinations in the validator, the picker, and the randomizer — one predicate (styleCompatible), three call sites.
  • Exhaustive test: every parts combination is assembled; validity must equal pairwise style compatibility, all categories must place, and the head must sit above the body's midpoint. The promise is checked at the data level, not eyeballed per pair.
  • Explicit "none": baldness is a real zero-size part, so the assembly never has holes and the picker never needs a special case.
The general shape. Whenever "any A works with any B" is the requirement, make A and B each describe themselves against a shared contract and derive the pairing — the moment knowledge about a specific (A,B) pair appears anywhere, the combinatorial promise is already broken.

input.content:
Drill 0020 · pairs with lesson 0020

Drill: Socket Contracts

1. Adding a third head

Under per-pair offsets vs socket contracts: how many entries does a new "head_oval" require in each scheme, with 3 eye parts and 4 hair parts in the catalog?

Answer

Per-pair: 7 hand-tuned offsets (one per eye and hair part), each a potential floating-eyeball bug. Socket contract: 1 PartDef with its own eyes and hair sockets — every existing eye/hair part snaps correctly with zero further edits.

2. Scale order

Why must the assembly resolve sockets BEFORE the character-height scale is applied, rather than scaling each part to world size first?

Answer

Sockets are authored in each part's local space. Scaling parts individually would move their sockets relative to differently-scaled neighbors — alignment drifts. Resolving in unscaled local space and then applying ONE uniform scale to the finished figure preserves every relative placement and satisfies the 1.8-unit contract in a single step.

3. New category: hats

List the exact data changes to add a Hat category that sits on the head, without touching assembly code.

Answer

(1) Add Hat to PartCategory and bump kPartCategoryCount; (2) one CategorySpec row {Hat, Head, "hat"}; (3) add a hat socket to each head PartDef; (4) hat parts (including a zero-size "hat_none"). The recursive assembly, validator, randomizer, and picker all pick it up from the spec table.

4. Where's the one join between persona and look?

Answer

The spawn path (main.cpp startup + onCreate): it loads both records by character_id, builds the Npc from the persona, and registers the look for rendering. Storage, editing, and validation never touch both — enforced by two separate SQLite tables rather than convention.

5. The exhaustive test's invariant

The combination test asserts assembled.ok == compatible. Why is the equality (not just implication) important?

Answer

Both directions catch bugs: a compatible combo failing to assemble means a missing socket (contract hole); an INcompatible combo assembling means the style gate leaks and the picker could offer mixed-style characters. The promise is "valid iff compatible", so the test asserts exactly that.

Vocab 0020 · pairs with lesson 0020

Vocab: Socket Contracts

socket
A named attach point a part declares in its own local space (head_round.sockets["eyes"]). Children snap to it; the child never knows which parent it landed on.
anchor
The implicit origin every part attaches BY — here bottom-center of the part's bounding size, matching the game's feet-on-ground position convention.
per-pair offset table
The anti-pattern: attachment positions keyed by (parent, child) pairs. Grows quadratically, and every missing pair is a visual bug.
category spec
The row that wires a category into the assembly: which parent category it attaches to and via which socket name. The assembly is a fold over these rows, parents before children.
style tag
A compatibility family on each part ("round", "blocky", "any"). One predicate gates the validator, picker, and randomizer so incompatible art styles never mix.
assembly space
The unscaled coordinate frame parts are placed in before the single size-contract scale. Socket math happens here; world sizing happens once, afterwards.
record independence
Persona and look live in separate tables/structs joined only by character_id at the spawn site — either can change, migrate, or fail without touching the other.

The character creator is done — **draft PR #77** closes all five tickets (#72–#76, milestone #6), with the suite green at 139 cases / 1384 assertions.

## What you can do when it merges

Pause menu → **Create Character** → type a name, backstory, and traits → cycle body/head/eyes/hair parts and a palette (or hit Randomize) while a live preview turns in front of you → **Save & Spawn**. The character walks the town, talks through the same LLM pipeline as every other NPC (memory included), and is still there after a restart.

## How it's built (the decisions the autonomy block asked me to log)

- **Socket contracts, exactly as specified**: every part declares its own attach points in its own local space (`head_round` says where *its* eyes and hair sockets are); category-spec rows wire parent→child. There is no per-pair offset table anywhere — a new part is one data row, a new category is one spec row. An exhaustive test assembles *every* part combination and asserts valid ⇔ style-compatible.
- **Size-contract interaction resolved in favor of the existing system**: sockets resolve unscaled, then one uniform scale takes the whole figure to the same 1.8-unit height contract pack characters use.
- **Persona and look stay fully independent**: two separate SQLite tables joined only by character_id at the spawn site. Player personas serialize through a new `renderPersonaText` — the exact inverse of the existing parser, so designer files and stored characters share one format.
- **One premise correction**: the brief's "sprite pixel dimensions" predates the raylib migration; parts are low-poly 3D primitive recipes (the fountain pattern), since the rigged pack characters can't donate swappable heads.

**Verified end-to-end**: I planted three store records and screenshotted them spawned in the plaza — three distinct, correctly snapped composites (blocky visor + spikes, round dot-eyes + tuft, round wide-eyes + bowl cut) at pack-character height.

## What needs your eyes

- **The Creator page UI itself** — scripted runs can't click menus, so typing/cycling/randomize/save need a 2-minute hands-on pass (flagged in PR #77).
- **Merge order**: the full chain is now #60 → #68 → #69 → #70 → #71 → #77, top-down.

Known v1 limits (logged, deliberate): composites get a procedural walk bob rather than skeletal animation, multiplayer guests see a pack model instead of the custom look, and duplicate names share memory rows. Lesson/drill/vocab 0020 ("socket contracts") written locally; OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md has the full session-4 write-up at the top.

You are turning "A" into a structured, actionable plan document.

This command has two phases:
- PHASE 1: Interrogate the idea until it is unambiguous
- PHASE 2: Produce the plan document

Do not skip to Phase 2 until Phase 1 is complete.

---

## PHASE 1 — INTERROGATE THE IDEA

Read the codebase first so your questions are grounded in reality:
```bash
find src/ lib/ app/ -type f 2>/dev/null | head -30
git log --oneline -10
cat CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null || true
```

Then ask clarifying questions — ONE at a time, wait for the answer,
then ask the next. Do not dump a list of questions all at once.
A question only gets asked if you genuinely cannot write a good plan
without knowing the answer.

Things worth asking about (pick the most important ones):

**Scope:**
- What does done look like? What can a user DO when this is complete?
- What is explicitly OUT of scope for this version?
- Is this a new feature, a change to existing behaviour, or a fix?

**Users and context:**
- Who uses this and in what situation?
- What do they have / know before they reach this feature?

**Technical constraints:**
- Does this touch existing code that other things depend on?
- Any performance, security, or compatibility requirements?
- Any third-party APIs or libraries involved?

**Edge cases:**
- What happens when the input is invalid or missing?
- What's the failure mode and how should it be handled?

**Priority:**
- Does this need to be done in a specific order relative to other work?
- Is there a simpler version that delivers most of the value?

Stop asking when you have enough to write a plan that could be handed
to a developer (or the overnight session) without them needing to ask
you anything.

---

## PHASE 2 — PRODUCE THE PLAN DOCUMENT

Save to `.claude/plans/[slug].md` where slug is a short dash-case
name derived from the idea. Example: "add weapon inventory" →
`.claude/plans/weapon-inventory.md`

```markdown

Date: [date]
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: S / M / L / XL

## The Idea (one paragraph)
[What this is, in plain language. Someone unfamiliar with the codebase
should understand this in 30 seconds.]

## Goal
[One sentence: what a user can DO when this is shipped that they
cannot do now.]

## Out of Scope (this version)
[Explicit list of things NOT included. This prevents scope creep
during implementation.]

## Affected Areas
[Files, modules, or systems this touches. Be specific.]
- `src/path/to/file.py` — [why it changes]
- `src/path/to/other.cpp` — [why it changes]
- New files needed: [list]

## Implementation Order
[Ordered steps. Each step should be independently committable.]

1. [Step 1 — what it produces]
2. [Step 2 — builds on step 1]
3. [Step 3 — etc.]

## Acceptance Criteria
[Testable conditions that define "done". Each one should be
verifiable by running a test or observing a specific behaviour.]

- [ ] [Given X, when Y, then Z]
- [ ] [Given X, when Y, then Z]
- [ ] Tests pass: [specific test file or command]

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
[What can go wrong and how each case is handled.]

| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| [case] | [what happens] |

## Open Questions
[Anything still unresolved that will need a decision during implementation.
If there are none, write "None — plan is complete."]

## Suggested GitHub Issues
[If this plan should become overnight issues, list them here as a
starting point for /plan-github:]

1. [Issue title] — [one line scope]
2. [Issue title] — [one line scope]
3. [Issue title] — [one line scope]
```

---

## AFTER SAVING THE PLAN

Tell the user:
1. Where the plan was saved
2. How to turn it into GitHub issues:
   `/plan-github "[feature name]"` — or offer to run it now
3. How to start implementation immediately:
   `/develop [feature name]` — uses the plan as the spec
4. How to queue it for overnight:
   Add the suggested issues to GitHub, label ready-for-ai,

---

## TONE

Ask questions like a sharp senior engineer reviewing a spec —
direct, specific, not adversarial. The goal is to surface
assumptions before they become bugs, not to gatekeep.

If the idea is already clear enough to plan without questions,

Goal: NPCs can learn facts from talking to the player or each other, and
those facts can spread — tell the baker a secret, the blacksmith can
plausibly bring it up later.

Context: This builds directly on the world-bus store from the schedules

   store before responding, filtered to what that NPC plausibly knows.

   (proximity, social ties, elapsed world_time) so gossip isn't instant
   and universal. This is what preserves mystery/investigation pacing if

# Plan: World Time, NPC Schedules, and Day/Night — the "world bus"
Date: 2026-07-06 (overnight, autonomous — decisions logged here + OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md)
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: M

## The Idea (one paragraph)
One authoritative world clock lives in a new generic shared-fact store
(`WorldState`, owned by `World`) that every time-aware system reads:
NPCs follow simple authored schedules (walk to a spot and do an activity
per time-of-day range), and the sky/fog/light shift through a full
day/night cycle — all from the same `world_time` value, never a private
timer. The store is the "world bus" that gossip and journal facts will
plug into later: string-keyed facts holding a number and/or text, with
world_time as its first entry.

## Goal
The player watches the town live on a clock: at 6 the baker walks to the
bakery, at dusk the sky warms then darkens and fog fades to night, and
every system agrees what time it is because there is only one time.

## Autonomy decisions (most-defensible picks, logged)
- **Store shape**: `WorldFact {double number; std::string text;}` in a
  string-keyed map with typed set/get helpers. Generic enough for gossip
  ("gossip.rumor_3" → text) and journal facts (number or text), no more.
  Time convenience accessors sit on WorldState but read the same fact
  ("world_time_seconds") any other system could read raw. NOT over-built:
  no subscriptions, no persistence, no replication tonight.
- **Clock rate**: 1 real second = 1 game minute (24-minute full day) —
  fast enough to see the cycle in a session; constant lives with the
  store. Game starts at 09:00. Time does not persist across restarts
  (nothing consumes persistence yet; log as future work with gossip).
- **Schedules are authored in .persona files** (the existing NPC content
  format): repeated `schedule = HH-HH, x, z, activity` header lines
  parsed by PersonaLoader into LoadedPersona (placement concern, like
  position — NOT part of Persona identity). Entries may wrap midnight
  (22-6). Npc walks toward the active entry's spot at kNpcWalk with the
  ReturnHome movement pattern whenever behavior_ is None and combat is
  Idle; the player standing within talk range pauses schedule walking
  (NPCs shouldn't walk away mid-approach/mid-chat).
- **Schedule activity label**: stored and exposed (`npc.activity()`),
  shown in the nameplate as "Name — activity". Injecting it into the
  LLM prompt is deferred (touches ask()'s prompt assembly; future
  ticket with gossip).
- **Day/night = pure functions in core** (`DayNight.hpp`:
  `skyColorAt(hours)`, `lightLevelAt(hours)` returning float triples/
  scalars) so the curve is unit-testable; the renderer maps them to
  raylib Color + two shader uniforms (fogColor already exists, new
  `lightLevel` multiplies the lit color). Sky, fog color, and light all
  derive from the SAME hour — fog keeps melting into the horizon at
  every time of day (lesson 0019's rule).
- **Smoke determinism**: day/night would make every screenshot depend on
  wall-clock frames, so `--frames` gains an optional `--hour H` override
  pinning the clock (same pattern as `--camera`). Existing screenshot
  workflows keep working (default hour = 09:00 noonish daylight... 9am).
- **Multiplayer**: guests run their own clock from the same 09:00 start;
  no replication tonight (needs a protocol bump — deferred to the gossip
  ticket, which must replicate facts anyway). Logged limitation.
- **Branch**: `feature/world-time` stacked on `feature/character-creator`
  (PR #77) — touches main.cpp/renderer/personas which the open chain
  modifies. One draft PR closing the tickets.

## Out of Scope (this version)
Gossip/journal content; fact persistence; fact replication; prompt
injection of activity/time; streetlamp glow, stars, moon, shadows;
schedule pathfinding beyond the existing straight-line + collision
sliding; editing schedules in-game; created-character schedules (they
just have none — same as several roster NPCs).

## Affected Areas
- NEW `src/core/WorldState.{hpp,cpp}` — fact store + clock advance/query.
- NEW `src/core/DayNight.hpp` — pure sky/light curves (header-only).
- `src/core/World.{hpp,cpp}` — owns WorldState; `state()` accessors;
  update advances the clock.
- `src/core/PersonaLoader.{hpp,cpp}` — parse/render `schedule =` lines;
  ScheduleEntry on LoadedPersona.
- `src/core/Npc.{hpp,cpp}` — setSchedule; update() takes timeOfDayHours;
  schedule walking + activity(); pause near the player.
- `src/app/RaylibRenderer.{hpp,cpp}` — setTimeOfDay(hours): sky color
  for main, fogColor + lightLevel uniforms per frame.
- `src/app/Assets.{hpp,cpp}` — lightLevel uniform in the fog shader +
  location accessor (fog color loc too, now per-frame).
- `src/app/main.cpp` — advance clock, pass hour to npc.update/renderer,
  ClearBackground from renderer.skyColor(), nameplate activity suffix,
  `--hour` smoke flag.
- `personas/baker|teacher|musician|barista.persona` — example schedules.
- Tests: NEW test_world_state.cpp, test_day_night.cpp; extend
  test_persona_roster.cpp (schedule parsing) and test_npc_behavior.cpp
  (schedule movement, no-private-clock, pause-near-player).

## Implementation Order
1. WorldState + DayNight + tests.
2. Schedule parsing (PersonaLoader) + Npc schedule behavior + tests.
3. Renderer/Assets day/night pass + --hour flag + main wiring.
4. Persona schedule content; screenshots at 09:00 / 19:00 / 00:00;
   suite; PR; report.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] WorldState: number/text facts round-trip; clock wraps 24h; two
      readers see the same value. Tests green.
- [ ] Schedule: at 07:00 the baker's active entry is the bakery; passing
      a different hour to the SAME npc moves it elsewhere (proves no
      private clock); walking pauses when the player is within talk
      range. Tests green.
- [ ] Day/night: skyColorAt/lightLevelAt continuous at range edges
      (tests); screenshots at 09:00, 19:00, 00:00 show day, dusk, night
      with fog matching the sky at each.
- [ ] `--hour` pins the clock for smoke runs; default screenshots
      unchanged vs tonight's baseline (09:00).
- [ ] Full suite green; build + smoke clean.

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|--------------------|
| Schedule entry wraps midnight (22-6) | Active when hour >= start OR hour < end. |
| Overlapping entries | First matching entry wins (documented; authoring rule). |
| No active entry / no schedule | NPC idles at home exactly as today. |
| Malformed schedule line | Persona parse error names the line; file skipped like any bad persona (existing contract). |
| Combat/Follow/Arrest active | Those behaviors own movement; schedule yields (checked by state, not priority flags). |
| Unknown fact key read | number(key, fallback) returns fallback; text returns nullptr. |
| Hour exactly at a range edge | start-inclusive, end-exclusive [start, end). |

## Open Questions
None — decisions above were made under the autonomy instructions.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. feat(core): WorldState — shared fact store with the world clock as
   its first fact
2. feat(core): NPC schedules authored in persona files, driven by
   world_time
3. feat(render): day/night sky, fog, and light from the shared clock
4. feat(game): wire clock/schedules/visuals in the loop + --hour smoke
   flag + example schedules

/idea

Goal: NPCs can learn facts from talking to the player or each other, and
those facts can spread — tell the baker a secret, the blacksmith can
plausibly bring it up later.

Context: This builds directly on the world-bus store from the schedules
ticket (if shipped) or establishes it now if not. Facts should be structured
records — {fact_id, subject, content, source, world_time_learned} — not
free paragraphs, because contradiction-checking in the journal ticket
depends on comparable, normalized fields.

Scope:
1. Fact writing — after a conversation, the LLM proposes new facts as
   structured output (same discipline as affinity_delta from the
   persistence work: propose, then validate, then commit — never write
   directly from LLM output).
2. Fact reading — NPC persona prompts pull relevant facts from the shared
   store before responding, filtered to what that NPC plausibly knows.
3. Propagation rules — decide how a fact spreads from one NPC to another
   (proximity, social ties, elapsed world_time) so gossip isn't instant
   and universal. This is what preserves mystery/investigation pacing if
   that's the direction the story goes.
4. Do not implement this as direct NPC-to-NPC message passing. It must go
   through the shared store so the journal ticket can plug into the same
   mechanism without new wiring.

- Do not stop to ask me clarifying questions, including any /grill-me-style
  interrogation step. Pick the most defensible option yourself, log the
  decision and reasoning in OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md, and keep going.
- If propagation rules are ambiguous, default to conservative (slower,
  proximity-gated spread) rather than instant town-wide knowledge — easier
  to loosen later than to walk back.
- Follow existing CLAUDE.md agent routing.
- Draft tickets, implement, test, open a draft PR as usual. Do not merge,

surfaces contradictions between what different NPCs have said.

Context: This is a reader of the same shared fact store the gossip ticket
writes to — not a separate tracking system. The journal should only ever
show facts the player was personally told (filtered by source/hearer), so
it doesn't spoil gossip the player wasn't part of.

Scope:

Read the codebase first so your questions are grounded in reality:

Then ask clarifying questions — ONE at a time, wait for the answer,
then ask the next. Do not dump a list of questions all at once.

Things worth asking about (pick the most important ones):

**Scope:**
- What does done look like? What can a user DO when this is complete?
- What is explicitly OUT of scope for this version?
- Is this a new feature, a change to existing behaviour, or a fix?

**Users and context:**
- Who uses this and in what situation?
- What do they have / know before they reach this feature?

**Technical constraints:**
- Does this touch existing code that other things depend on?
- Any performance, security, or compatibility requirements?
- Any third-party APIs or libraries involved?

**Edge cases:**
- What happens when the input is invalid or missing?
- What's the failure mode and how should it be handled?

**Priority:**
- Does this need to be done in a specific order relative to other work?
- Is there a simpler version that delivers most of the value?

Stop asking when you have enough to write a plan that could be handed
to a developer (or the overnight session) without them needing to ask

# Plan: Gossip — structured facts on the world bus, with propagation
Date: 2026-07-06 (overnight, autonomous — decisions logged here + OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md)
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: L

## The Idea (one paragraph)
NPCs learn structured facts from conversations with the player and from
each other. Facts are normalized records — {fact_id, subject, content,
source, world_time_learned} — living on the SAME WorldState bus the world
clock rides (shipping tonight in feature/world-time), with a per-agent
knowledge set saying who has heard what. After a conversation closes, the
NPC's model PROPOSES facts as structured JSON; code validates and commits
them (never a direct write). NPC prompts inject the facts that NPC knows.
A conservative propagation tick spreads facts between NPCs who are
physically near each other (schedules make them actually meet), gated by
elapsed world time and chance — tell the baker a secret and it reaches the
hardware store owner plausibly, not instantly.

## Goal
The player tells one NPC something, plays on, and later hears a different
NPC bring it up — with the spread visibly gradual and traceable to who
told whom.

## Autonomy decisions (most-defensible picks, logged)
- **Facts are first-class on the bus**: WorldState (from feature/world-time,
  in flight on this chain — prerequisite satisfied) gains a structured

# Plan: Player Journal — read the fact store, surface contradictions
Date: 2026-07-06 (overnight, autonomous — decisions logged here + OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md)
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION (after gossip-facts)
Estimated complexity: S

## The Idea (one paragraph)
A journal page in the existing pause menu listing every fact the player
was personally told, grouped by subject, each attributed ("heard from
Marge at 14:20"). When two facts share a normalized subject but disagree
in content, both are flagged as conflicting accounts. The journal is a
pure READER of the gossip fact store on the WorldState bus — it writes
nothing, owns no data, and needs no new fields.

## Goal
The player opens the journal, sees what they've been told organized by
topic, and spots when two NPCs' accounts of the same thing don't line up.

## Autonomy decisions (most-defensible picks, logged)
- **Visibility filter**: show facts where knows("player", factId) AND
  source != "player" — what the player was told, never what they told
  others, and never gossip they weren't part of. The player enters the
  knowledge set only when an NPC tells them something (player_learned
  direction), so the filter is exactly "personally told".
- **Contradiction v1 = same subject, different content** (both entries
  flagged "conflicting accounts"). True semantic contradiction detection
  needs either an LLM judge or a typed-field schema — both out of
  proportion for tonight; the exact-normalized-subject grouping the
  gossip schema guarantees makes this check honest and cheap. Logged as
  the intended future upgrade point.
- **Pure read path**: the journal renders from WorldState + persona
  names each time the page opens. No caching, no journal store, no
  schema changes (verified during planning: subject/content/source/
  learnedAtSeconds cover everything the UI shows).
- **UI**: Page::Journal in the pause menu (Main gains a "Journal"
  button), same Page/Hit/layout machinery as Creator/Multiplayer.
  Scrolling: page up/down buttons when entries exceed the screen
  (simplest paging, no scrollbar widget).
- **Branch**: `feature/player-journal` stacked on
  `feature/gossip-facts`. Small PR.

## Out of Scope (this version)
Semantic contradiction detection; marking facts resolved/false; player
notes; quest hooks; search; exporting; showing propagation chains.

## Affected Areas
- `src/app/Menu.{hpp,cpp}` — Page::Journal, JournalHooks (a
  std::function returning the visible entries, injected by main so the
  menu stays free of WorldState), grouping + conflict flags render.
- NEW `src/core/Journal.hpp` — pure helpers: `journalEntries(state)`
  (filter + sort by subject then time) and `conflictingFactIds(entries)`
  (same subject, differing content) so the logic is unit-testable
  without raylib.
- `src/app/main.cpp` — inject the hook (reads world.state()).
- Tests: NEW test_journal.cpp — filter excludes player-sourced and
  unheard facts; grouping order stable; conflicts flagged exactly when
  same-subject contents differ.

## Implementation Order
1. Journal.hpp helpers + tests.
2. Menu page + main hook.
3. Screenshot (menu open on the journal page with planted facts), suite,
   PR, report.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Entries: exactly the facts the player was told (source != player,
      player in knowers), grouped by subject, time-ordered. Tests green.
- [ ] Two same-subject facts with different content are BOTH flagged;
      same-subject same-content (told by two NPCs) is not. Tests green.
- [ ] Journal shows attribution name and HH:MM from learnedAtSeconds.
- [ ] No writes to WorldState anywhere in the journal path.
- [ ] Suite green; screenshot shows the page with a planted conflict.

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|--------------------|
| Empty journal | Page shows "You haven't been told anything yet." |
| Fact whose source NPC no longer exists | Attribution still shows the stored name (names are stored, not looked up). |
| Very long content | Wrapped/truncated to the row (ellipsis) — content is capped at 140 chars by the gossip validator anyway. |
| More entries than fit | Prev/Next page buttons. |

## Open Questions
None — decisions above were made under the autonomy instructions.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. feat(core): journal read-path helpers — player-visible facts +
   conflict detection
2. feat(ui): journal menu page with grouping, attribution, and conflict
   flags

"""Draft PR for world time + ticket bookkeeping (#78-#81)."""
import os
import time

from github import Github, GithubException

gh = Github(os.environ["GH_TOKEN"])
repo = gh.get_repo("bjl14710/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs")


def retry(fn, what):
    for attempt in range(4):
        try:
            return fn()
        except GithubException as e:
            print(f"{what} attempt {attempt+1}: {e.status}")
            time.sleep(5)
    raise SystemExit(f"gave up: {what}")


body = (
    "Closes #78, closes #79, closes #80, closes #81 (milestone #7). "
    "Stacks on #77 (base = `feature/character-creator`); plan: "
    "`.claude/plans/world-time-and-schedules.md`.\n\n"
    "## What this delivers\n"
    "One authoritative world clock on a new generic shared-fact store "
    "(the **world bus** that the gossip and journal projects plug into "
    "next), NPC daily routines driven by it, and a full day/night visual "
    "cycle — the town lives on a schedule and the light follows.\n\n"
    "## Design\n"
    "- **WorldState**: string-keyed facts (number and/or text) owned by "
    "World; the clock is its first fact (`world_time_seconds`). 1 real "
    "second = 1 game minute (24-minute day), starts 09:00, wraps at "
    "midnight. Deliberately minimal: no subscriptions/persistence/"
    "replication until a consumer needs them.\n"
    "- **Injected time**: `Npc::update` takes the hour as a parameter — "
    "NPCs keep no clock of their own (a test passes different hours to "
    "the same NPC and watches the destination change). Schedules are "
    "authored in `.persona` files (`schedule = HH-HH, x, z, activity`), "
    "wrap midnight, pause politely when the player is near, and yield to "
    "combat/instructed behaviors. Activity labels ride the nameplates.\n"
    "- **Day/night**: pure curves in `DayNight.hpp` (band edges "
    "continuity-tested); sky clear color, fog color, and a new "
    "`lightLevel` shader uniform all derive from the same hour, so fog "
    "keeps melting into the horizon at midnight exactly like noon.\n"
    "- **Deterministic smokes**: `--hour H` pins the clock (screenshots "
    "at 09:00 / 19:30 / 00:00 verified day, warm dusk haze, and dark "
    "night).\n\n"
    "## Verification\n"
    "- Suite 149 cases / 1449 assertions green (clock wrap, fact "
    "round-trips, schedule selection incl. midnight wrap and edge "
    "hours, no-private-clock, pause-near-player, malformed schedule "
    "lines, curve continuity).\n"
    "- Down-street screenshots at three pinned hours.\n\n"
    "## Logged limitations\n"
    "Guests run their own clock from the same 09:00 start (replication "
    "lands with gossip's protocol bump); time doesn't persist across "
    "restarts (first consumer of that is gossip persistence).\n\n"
    "---\n\U0001F916 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)"
)

pr = retry(lambda: repo.create_pull(
    title="feat(world): shared clock on the world bus, NPC schedules, day/night",
    body=body,
    head="feature/world-time",
    base="feature/character-creator",
    draft=True), "create pr")
print(f"PR #{pr.number}: {pr.html_url}")

for number in (78, 79, 80, 81):
    issue = retry(lambda: repo.get_issue(number), f"issue {number}")
    retry(lambda: issue.add_to_labels("ai-completed"), "label")
    try:
        issue.remove_from_labels("ai-in-progress")
    except GithubException:
        pass
    retry(lambda: issue.create_comment(
        f"Implemented in draft PR #{pr.number}. Suite 149/1449 green; "
        "day/dusk/night screenshots verified."), "comment")
    retry(lambda: issue.edit(state="closed"), "close")
    print(f"issue #{number} closed")

)

    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/external
)

Lesson 0021 · Architecture · from PR #82 (world time)

The World Bus and Injected Time

Three systems needed the time of day at once: NPC schedules, the sky, and the fog. The trap is letting each keep its own timer — three clocks that drift, pause differently in menus, and disagree at dusk. The fix has two halves.

1. One authoritative value on a shared bus

WorldState is a string-keyed fact store owned by World. The clock is just its first fact (world_time_seconds); gossip facts moved in next with zero changes to the store's shape. The convenience accessors (timeOfDayHours()) are sugar over the same fact any system could read raw — no side channels.

2. Consumers take time as a parameter

void Npc::update(float dt, const Vec3& playerPos,
                 const City& city, float timeOfDayHours = -1.f);

The NPC has no clock member. The test that proves the design: call the SAME NPC with hour 7 and it heads to the bakery; call it with hour 12.5 and it heads to the plaza. Injected time also makes "no clock" explicit (negative = schedules dormant) instead of accidental.

Why the renderer follows the same rule

setTimeOfDay(hours) derives the sky clear color, the fog color, and a light-level uniform from one hour via pure curves in core (DayNight.hpp — testable, including continuity at the dawn/ dusk band edges). Because fog color and sky always come from the same value, distant geometry melts into the horizon at midnight exactly as it does at noon — lesson 0019's rule, now time-varying.

The pattern. When a value has multiple consumers, promote it to a shared store and INJECT it — don't let consumers cache or re-derive it. The bus earns its name when the second tenant (gossip) moves in without renovation.

input.content:
Lesson 0022 · LLM engineering · from PR #89 (gossip)

Propose, Validate, Commit: LLMs Never Write Directly

Gossip needs the model to CREATE game state — the facts NPCs learn. Letting model output write into the world directly turns every hallucination into corrupted state. The discipline:

PROPOSE   the model returns a strict-JSON array of ≤2 candidate facts
VALIDATE  code parses (non-throwing), normalizes subjects, checks types,
          directions, lengths — anything wrong yields NOTHING
COMMIT    only validated records touch the WorldState bus; ids hash
          subject+content so repeats are idempotent

Design choices that make it robust

  • All-or-nothing validation: one malformed entry rejects the whole proposal — no partial commits from half-good output.
  • Idempotent ids: factIdFor(subject, content) is a stable hash, so the same statement extracted twice is one fact, and the first teller's timestamp/source survive re-commits.
  • Normalization at the boundary: subjects squeeze to [a-z0-9_] on the way in, because the journal compares them exactly. Comparable fields beat free paragraphs.
  • Failure is silence: prose instead of JSON logs one line and commits nothing. Facts are a bonus; a crash would be a bug.

Propagation is state, not messages

Spread is a tick over the shared store: pairs within 6 units, teller knowledge older than 30 game minutes, 35% roll, at most one fact per pair per tick. No NPC→NPC message channel exists — so the journal (and any future reader) plugs into the same store with zero new wiring, and the conservative gates keep a secret's spread traceable and slow enough to walk back.

Contrast with the directive tags. [[ACTION:]] tags are also validated (parseDirectives), but they are TRANSIENT — a bad tag wastes one turn. Facts are PERSISTENT state; the validation bar is higher because mistakes compound.

input.content:
Drill 0021 · pairs with lesson 0021

Drill: The World Bus and Injected Time

1. How does a test prove an NPC has no private clock?

Answer

Call the same NPC's update with different timeOfDayHours values and watch its destination change. Only the parameter varied — if the NPC cached time anywhere, the second call couldn't behave differently.

2. Why do the sky, fog, and light all sample the SAME hour, and what breaks if fog keeps a daylight constant?

Answer

Fog's whole trick is melting geometry into the sky (lesson 0019). A daylight fog color under a midnight sky puts a bright blue haze on a dark horizon — distant buildings would glow. All three derive from one clock so they can never disagree.

3. What made the bus "generic enough" without over-building?

Answer

String keys with a number-and/or-text fact per key — enough for the clock and for gossip's structured section to move in later without reshaping the store. What was deliberately NOT built: subscriptions, persistence, replication — none had a consumer yet.

4. Why does --hour exist for smoke runs?

String keys with a number-and/or-text fact per key — enough for the clock and for gossip's structured section to move in later without reshaping the store. What was deliberately NOT built: subscriptions, persistence, replication — none had a consumer yet.

Drill 0022 · pairs with lesson 0022

Drill: Propose, Validate, Commit

1. The model replies with one perfect fact and one with direction "telepathy". What commits?

Answer

Nothing. Validation is all-or-nothing — a partially-bad proposal yields an empty result, so half-good output can't half-corrupt the store.

2. The player tells Marge the same secret twice, a game day apart. How many facts exist and whose timestamp wins?

Answer

One. factIdFor hashes subject+content, and addFact keeps the existing record — the FIRST commit's stamp and source survive. The second commit only (re-)grants knowledge.

3. Why must gossip spread by flipping knowledge bits on the store instead of NPC→NPC messages?

Answer

Any future reader (the journal tonight, quests later) sees the complete knowledge state by reading ONE place. A message channel would put truth in transit — the journal would need to eavesdrop on every conversation instead of querying the bus.

4. Name the three propagation gates and what each protects.

Answer

Radius (6u): gossip requires actual proximity — schedules create the encounters. Age (30 game minutes): a secret doesn't teleport across town the tick after it's told. Chance (35%, one fact per pair per tick): spread is gradual and traceable — conservative by instruction, easier to loosen than walk back.

5. Journal bonus: why is same-subject SAME-content from two tellers not flagged?

Answer

That's corroboration — two people agreeing. A conflict needs the same normalized subject with DIFFERING content; both sides get flagged so the player sees the disagreement, not a verdict.

world bus
The single shared store (WorldState) systems read facts from instead of keeping private copies. The clock was the first tenant; gossip facts the second; the journal reads it without new wiring.
injected time

knowledge set
Per-agent record of WHICH facts an agent has heard, stored beside the facts (not inside them). Propagation and the journal's visibility filter are both just queries over these sets.
propagation gates
The conservative conditions for spread: proximity radius, minimum teller-knowledge age, per-tick chance, one fact per pair. Slower is recoverable; instant town-wide knowledge is not.
read model
A derived, filtered view over shared state for one consumer — the journal is a read model of the fact store (player-heard facts, grouped, conflict-flagged) that owns no data and never writes.
corroboration vs conflict
Same subject + same content from two tellers = corroboration (not flagged). Same subject + different content = conflict (both rows flagged). Exact normalized subjects make the comparison honest.

You are scaffolding the initial file structure for a planned feature.
This command bridges the gap between a plan document and actual files
on disk — creating skeletons, directories, config updates, and skill
files so the overnight session or /develop has something real to build on.

---

## STEP 1 — READ THE PLAN

```bash
# Find the plan document
ls .claude/plans/
cat .claude/plans/.md 2>/dev/null || \
  cat .claude/plans/$(echo "" | tr ' ' '-' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]').md 2>/dev/null || \
  echo "No plan found for '' — run /idea first"
```

If no plan exists, stop and tell the user to run `/idea` first.
The plan is the spec. Do not scaffold without it.

---

## STEP 2 — READ THE CODEBASE

```bash
# Understand what already exists before creating anything
find src/ lib/ app/ tests/ -type f 2>/dev/null | head -50
cat CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null | head -50 || true
git log --oneline -10
```

Use real class names, real import paths, and real conventions from
what you find — not generic placeholders.

---

## STEP 3 — DERIVE WHAT NEEDS TO BE CREATED

From the plan's "Affected Areas" and "Implementation Order" sections,
determine:

- New directories needed
- New source files (with correct imports and skeleton structure)
- New test files (matching the project's test conventions)
- Config file updates (pytest.ini, CMakeLists.txt, requirements.txt etc.)
- New skill files if the feature introduces patterns Claude needs
  to reference repeatedly (e.g. a new API, a new framework)
- Any one-time setup scripts (e.g. installing system packages)
- .gitignore additions for generated or temporary files

---

## STEP 4 — CREATE THE FILES

For each file derived in Step 3:

**Source files** — create with:
- Correct imports based on existing patterns in the project
- Class/function skeleton matching the plan's interface
- Docstrings explaining what each piece does and why
- TODO comments marking what the overnight session needs to fill in
- No placeholder names — use real names from the codebase

**Test files** — create with:
- Correct pytest conventions for this project
- One test function stub per acceptance criterion in the plan
- Each stub has a docstring explaining what it tests
- `pytest.mark.skip(reason="not implemented yet")` on each stub
  so the test suite runs clean before the feature is built

**Config updates** — update existing files rather than creating new ones
where possible. Add only what the plan requires.

**Skill files** — only if the feature introduces something Claude needs
to reference repeatedly. Write to `.claude/skills/<feature>/SKILL.md`.
Not every feature needs a skill — only ones with non-obvious APIs,
protocols, or patterns.

**Setup scripts** — only if the feature requires one-time environment
setup (installing system packages, external tools, etc.). Write to
`scripts/setup-<feature>.sh`. Make it idempotent — safe to run twice.

---

## STEP 5 — DO NOT CREATE

Things the scaffold should NOT create:

- Implementation code (that's for /develop or the overnight session)
- Golden/reference files (those are generated by running the tests)
- Database migrations (those need careful human review)
- Secrets or credentials
- Anything not mentioned in the plan

If the plan is unclear about something, leave a clear TODO comment
and note it in the summary rather than guessing.

---

## STEP 6 — UPDATE .gitignore

Add any paths that should never be committed:
```bash
# Examples based on feature type:
# Visual testing:   tests/visual/diffs/  tests/visual/actual/
# Build artifacts:  dist/  build/  *.pyc
# Generated files:  whatever the feature produces at runtime

grep -qF "<path>" .gitignore || echo "<path>" >> .gitignore
```

---

## STEP 7 — SUMMARY

After creating all files, print a clear summary:

```
Scaffold complete for: [feature name]
Plan: .claude/plans/[plan].md

Files created:
  [path]  ← [one line: what it is]
  [path]  ← [one line: what it is]

Files updated:
  [path]  ← [what was added]

Next steps:
  1. [Any one-time setup to run e.g. bash scripts/setup-x.sh]
  2. Review the scaffolded files and adjust if needed
  3. /plan-github "[feature name]" to create GitHub issues
  4. bash ~/scripts/nightly.sh to build overnight
     OR /develop [feature] to build now

Nothing is implemented yet — stubs and skeletons only.
The overnight session or /develop fills them in.
```

---

## TONE

The scaffold is a starting point, not a finished product. Be explicit
about what is a skeleton vs what is complete. Use TODO comments
liberally — they are communication to the implementer, not a sign
of incompleteness in the scaffold itself.

You are a backlog planning agent for a personal GitHub project.
Your job is to read the current project state and create well-formed
GitHub issues that the overnight session can work through autonomously.

Every issue you create must be:
- Self-contained (completable in one overnight session)
- Specific (clear acceptance criteria, not vague goals)
- Verifiable (a test to run or output to check)
- Code-economy compliant (won't produce bloated PRs)
- Labelled ready-for-ai and assigned to the repo owner

---

## STEP 1 — PREREQUISITES

```python
import os
from github import Github

# Verify auth
token = os.environ.get("GH_TOKEN")
username = os.environ.get("GITHUB_USERNAME")
if not token or not username:
    raise SystemExit(
        "Set GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_USERNAME in your shell config first."
    )

gh = Github(token)
repo = get_repo(gh)   # auto-detects from git remote
print(f"Planning issues for: {repo.full_name}")

# Read existing open issues to avoid duplicates
existing = list_issues(repo, state="open")
existing_titles = {i["title"].lower() for i in existing}
print(f"Existing open issues: {len(existing)}")
```

---

## STEP 2 — READ PROJECT CONTEXT

Read all of these before planning any issues:

**CLAUDE.md** — the project purpose, stack, rules, and current state.
This is the source of truth for what the project is trying to be.

**README.md** — user-facing description and roadmap if any.

**Current codebase:**
```bash
# What exists right now
find src/ lib/ app/ -type f 2>/dev/null | head -50 || \
  find . -name "*.py" -o -name "*.cpp" -o -name "*.ts" \
  | grep -v node_modules | grep -v build | head -50

# Where work is heading
git log --oneline -20

# Known gaps and TODOs
grep -rn "TODO\|FIXME\|HACK\|NotImplemented\|raise NotImplementedError" \
  src/ lib/ app/ 2>/dev/null | head -30

# Test coverage gaps (uncovered files)
pytest --co -q 2>/dev/null | head -30 || true
```

---

## STEP 3 — CREATE MILESTONE (GITHUB EQUIVALENT OF EPIC)

Group related issues under a milestone:

```python
def create_milestone(repo, title: str, description: str) -> int:
    """Create a GitHub milestone. Returns the milestone number."""
    milestone = repo.create_milestone(
        title=title,
        description=description
    )
    print(f"Created milestone: {milestone.title} (#{milestone.number})")
    return milestone.number
```

Create one milestone per theme of work. For "" focus, one milestone
is enough. For full project analysis, create 2-4 milestones.

Good milestone names:
- "SCPI Device Family — Oscilloscopes"
- "NPC Tier 1: Structured Output"
- "Data Pipeline — Market Data Ingestion"

---

## STEP 4 — CREATE ISSUES

For each issue, use this exact body template so the overnight session
has everything it needs:

```python
ISSUE_TEMPLATE = """## What to change
{what}

## Where it is
{where}

## How to verify it's done
{verify}

## Constraints
{constraints}

## Code economy note
{economy_note}

## Branch name
`feature/issue-{{number}}-{slug}`

## Concept for learning materials
{concept}
"""
```

The **concept** field is critical — it tells the overnight session what
to teach/drill after completing this issue. It must be:
- A technical concept, not a feature name
- Specific enough to produce a useful lesson
- Different from concepts already in docs/learning/PROGRESS.md

```python
def plan_and_create_issues(repo, milestone_number: int,
                           specs: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Create a batch of issues. Each spec is a dict with keys:
        title, what, where, verify, constraints, economy_note,
        slug, concept

    Returns list of created issue dicts with number and URL.
    """
    username = os.environ["GITHUB_USERNAME"]
    created = []

    # Ensure overnight labels exist
    create_overnight_labels(repo)

    milestone = repo.get_milestone(milestone_number)

    for spec in specs:
        # Skip if similar issue already exists
        if spec["title"].lower() in existing_titles:
            print(f"Skipping (exists): {spec['title']}")
            continue

        body = ISSUE_TEMPLATE.format(
            what=spec["what"],
            where=spec["where"],
            verify=spec["verify"],
            constraints=spec["constraints"],
            economy_note=spec["economy_note"],
            slug=spec["slug"],
            concept=spec["concept"],
            number="N"    # placeholder — updated after creation
        )

        issue = repo.create_issue(
            title=spec["title"],
            body=body,
            labels=["ready-for-ai"],
            assignees=[username],
            milestone=milestone
        )

        # Update branch name now that we have the number
        updated_body = body.replace(
            "feature/issue/N",
            f"feature/issue-{issue.number}"
        )
        issue.edit(body=updated_body)

        print(f"  Created #{issue.number}: {spec['title']}")
        print(f"  Concept: {spec['concept']}")
        created.append({
            "number":  issue.number,
            "title":   spec["title"],
            "concept": spec["concept"],
            "url":     issue.html_url
        })

    return created
```

---

## STEP 5 — ECONOMY NOTE GUIDANCE

Every issue should include an `economy_note` that pre-constrains the
implementation. This prevents the overnight session from over-building.

Good economy notes:
```
Use stdlib re for command pattern matching — no regex library needed.
Follow the existing BaseDevice pattern exactly — no new abstractions.
One new file maximum: src/devices/psu_e3631a.py plus its test file.
```

Bad economy notes (too vague):
```
Keep it simple.
Don't over-engineer.
```

The note should name the specific stdlib/pattern to use, or the
specific constraint on scope.

---

## STEP 6 — VERIFY THE QUEUE

After creating all issues:

```python
print("\n=== Tonight's ready-for-ai queue ===")
queue = list_issues(repo, label="ready-for-ai")
for issue in queue:
    print(f"  #{issue['number']:3} {issue['title']}")
    print(f"       URL: {issue['url']}")

print(f"\nTotal: {len(queue)} issues queued")
print("Run nightly-all.sh tonight to work through them.")
```

---

## STEP 7 — WRITE LOCAL PLAN SUMMARY

Save a planning summary locally (not committed):

```python
summary = f"""# Issue Planning Summary
Date: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')}
Repo: {repo.full_name}
Focus: {"" or "full project analysis"}

## Issues Created Tonight
"""
for issue in created_issues:
    summary += f"- #{issue['number']}: {issue['title']}\n"
    summary += f"  Concept: {issue['concept']}\n"
    summary += f"  URL: {issue['url']}\n\n"

summary += """
## What Was NOT Planned
[things seen in codebase not turned into issues and why]
"""

Path(".claude/memory/planning-session.md").write_text(summary)
print("\nPlan saved to .claude/memory/planning-session.md")
```

---

## CONCEPT SELECTION GUIDE

The `concept` field in each issue is what drives learning generation.
Choose well — this is what you'll study after the overnight session.

| Issue type | Good concept | Bad concept |
|------------|-------------|-------------|
| New SCPI device | "Multi-channel PSU channel selection in SCPI" | "E3631A support" |
| New Qt block | "Qt drag-and-drop hardware block pattern" | "New block" |
| Bug fix | "SCPI ErrorQueue per IEEE 488.2" | "Fixed a bug" |
| New NPC | "LLM character constraint and knowledge domain" | "Added blacksmith" |
| Backtest fix | "Lookahead bias in rolling feature windows" | "Fixed backtest" |
| Data pipeline | "Point-in-time market data and survivorship bias" | "Data ingestion" |

Before finalizing a concept, check docs/learning/PROGRESS.md to avoid
re-teaching something already well covered.

---

## RUNNING THIS COMMAND

```
/plan-github                        full project analysis
/plan-github "oscilloscope family"  focus on one area
/plan-github "phase 2"             focus on next milestone
```

Re-run after completing a milestone to plan the next set of work.
It reads existing open issues first and skips duplicates.


from there rather than starting over.

Write the session start to .claude/memory/checkpoint.md:

```
# Checkpoint
Session started: [timestamp]
Goal: Work through all ready-for-ai issues
Status: IN PROGRESS

Issues failed: []
Issues skipped: []
```

## FOR EACH ISSUE (in number order, lowest first)

### A. READ AND ASSESS

```bash
gh issue view [N] --comments
```

**Blockers that cause a SKIP:**
- Requires a design decision not documented in the issue
- Depends on another issue that isn't complete yet
- Requires credentials, API keys, or external resources not available

If blocked, label and move on — do NOT guess at intent:

### E. PLAN

### F. IMPLEMENT

Use the appropriate specialist agents for this repo (see repo-specific
section below). Follow the plan. Write complete code — no placeholders.

If you hit a problem after 2 attempts on the same sticking point, SKIP
the issue and mark it ai-blocked. Do not spiral.

### G. TEST

Run the project's test suite. The exact commands are in the repo-specific
section below. Tests MUST pass before committing.

If tests fail after 2 fix attempts: skip, mark blocked, move on.

## LEARNING CONCEPT SELECTION — GENERAL GUIDANCE

These guidelines apply to all repos unless overridden in a repo-specific
overnight-session command.

Choose a concept that:
- Is non-obvious (skip things any developer already knows)
- Will appear again in this codebase (worth learning for maintainability)
- Can be explained in one lesson without splitting into prerequisite lessons
- Has clear vocabulary (terms worth adding to the glossary)
- Produces useful recall questions in a drill

Avoid:
- Concepts named after specific model numbers or vendor names
  ("E3631A" is not a concept; "triple-channel PSU SCPI addressing" is)
- Concepts so generic they produce a useless lesson
  ("adding a class" — skip this)
- Concepts already well-covered in the existing lesson library
  (check docs/learning/PROGRESS.md first)

---

## FAILURE HANDLING POLICY

This policy applies to the entire session.

**Never stop the run because one issue failed.**
**Never silently skip — always label and comment.**
**Never attempt a risky or irreversible action without a prior commit.**

If at any point the session hits a situation that is genuinely ambiguous,
dangerous, or requires a human decision not covered by the issue:
1. Stop work on that issue
2. Label it needs-human
3. Leave a detailed comment explaining exactly what decision is needed
4. Move to the next issue

The goal is to maximize completed work, not to force through stuck issues.

knowledge checks. In overnight autonomous mode, skip the interactive
questions and put that energy into making the HTML content more thorough
instead. The HTML is the deliverable — the in-chat conversation is not.
