content:
/idea

Goal: Fix gun aim direction, add more character style variety, and replace
the character-creator preview's auto-spin with player-driven rotation that
falls back to facing the player after real inactivity.

Context:
1. Gun aim likely has the same root cause as the earlier moonwalk fix —
   aim direction is stored/updated somewhere separate from the actual
   aim target (cursor position, look vector, whatever drives it), so the
   two have drifted out of sync. Apply the same fix pattern: derive aim
   direction from the authoritative target every frame rather than storing
   it independently. Do not patch this per-weapon or per-animation-state;
   fix it at the source the same way facing was fixed.
2. More character styles — extend the existing socket/style-tag system
   (heads, eyes, hair, body, etc.) with additional style-tagged part sets.
   No new architecture needed here; this should be additive within the
   existing contract, not a parallel system.
3. Character-creator preview currently auto-spins continuously on an
   internal timer, forcing the player to wait out a full rotation to see
   details like the eyes. Replace this entirely:
   - Rotation is driven only by player drag/input while input is active.
   - A time-since-last-input counter tracks inactivity.
   - Only after a defined idle timeout (not immediately) does the model
     ease toward a fixed default orientation — facing the player/camera —
     rather than continuing any spin.
   - There should be no code path where an autonomous spin runs
     unconditionally; input and idle-fallback are the only two states.
   - If an auto-rotate "preview mode" is wanted later, that's a separate,
     explicitly opt-in third state — do not build it now, just don't
     structure the fix in a way that makes it hard to add later.

Autonomy instructions for tonight's run — this runs unattended, so:
- Do not stop to ask me clarifying questions, including any /grill-me-style
  interrogation step. Where a decision would normally prompt me, pick the
  most defensible option yourself, log the decision and reasoning in
  OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md, and keep going.
- For the aim fix, prefer the derived-value approach over a per-weapon
  patch even if the patch would look done sooner — same reasoning as the
  moonwalk fix, this prevents new weapons from reintroducing the bug.
- Pick reasonable defaults for idle timeout duration and ease speed for the
  preview rotation; log the chosen values so I can tune them later without
  re-deriving the logic.
- Follow existing CLAUDE.md agent routing.
- Draft tickets, implement, test, open a draft PR as usual. Do not merge,
  do not touch main.
- docs/learning/, OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md, .claude/memory/ stay gitignored.

=== README ===
# LLM NPC City

A small first-person 3D city where every inhabitant is a live LLM character.
Walk the streets, find the baker, the cop, the busker, the hot-dog vendor —
press `T` and talk to them about anything. Each NPC has their own personality,
their own knowledge of the city (and pointed ignorance of everything else),
and remembers your conversation.

Powered locally by [Ollama](https://ollama.com) — no cloud, no API key.

## Quick start (Windows)

1. **Install Ollama** from <https://ollama.com/download>, then pull the model:

   ```
   ollama pull qwen2.5:3b-instruct
   ```

2. **Install MSYS2** from <https://www.msys2.org> and, in the *UCRT64* shell:

   ```
   pacman -S mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-cmake
   ```

3. **Fetch the art packs** (once): `bash tools/fetch_assets.sh` — two CC0
   low-poly packs, pinned and checksummed (see `assets/LICENSES.md`).

4. **Double-click `run.bat`** (or run `./run.ps1`). It checks Ollama is up,
   builds (CMake fetches raylib automatically), and launches the game.

## Playing

- `WASD` to walk, mouse to look around.
- Walk up to anyone: `[T] Talk to <name>` appears — press `T`.
- Type, press `Enter`, and watch the reply stream in live. `Escape` to leave.
- `Escape` opens the pause menu: resume, quit, or **rebind every key with the
  mouse** (changes save instantly).

Full reference: [docs/CONTROLS.md](docs/CONTROLS.md).

## Multiplayer (2-4 friends)

One player hosts; up to three more walk the same city and talk to the same
NPCs — one shared brain per character, so the baker remembers what your
friend told her.

**Hosting:** `Escape` → **Multiplayer** → **Host on port 40605**. Your machine
runs the world and the LLM; nobody else needs Ollama. Tell your friends your
IP address (`ipconfig` / `ifconfig`, e.g. `192.168.1.20`).

**Joining:** `Escape` → **Multiplayer** → click the address field, type
`<host-ip>:40605`, press `Enter`. Connection problems show up right there —
wrong address, full session (4 players max), or mismatched game versions.

What to expect in a session:

- Everyone sees everyone walk around, plus each NPC's live position and mood.
- NPC conversations are private to read, public in effect: if your friend
  angers Officer Brooks, you'll see her scowl.
- An NPC answers one person at a time; a second question waits its turn.

`<host-ip>:40605`, press `Enter`. Connection problems show up right there —
wrong address, full session (4 players max), or mismatched game versions.

- Everyone sees everyone walk around, plus each NPC's live position and mood.

  angers Officer Brooks, you'll see her scowl.

=== raylib-visual-overhaul plan (art intent) ===
# Plan: raylib Renderer Swap + Low-Poly Visual Overhaul
Date: 2026-07-05
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: XL

## The Idea (one paragraph)
The game currently draws its city as flat-colored boxes through a hand-rolled
~570-line legacy OpenGL 2.1 renderer sitting on SFML. This plan replaces that
entire presentation layer with [raylib](https://www.raylib.com) (simple,
C-style, modern-3D-capable, actively maintained) and restyles the whole game
with professionally-made CC0 low-poly asset packs — real buildings, streets,
props, and rigged characters instead of boxes. The engine-agnostic heart of the
game (`src/core/`: LLM, NPCs, world, dialogue, multiplayer — 96 unit tests)
survives byte-for-byte untouched; only the `src/app/` shell (~1,400 lines) is
rewritten. Full feature parity before merge: dialogue with streaming text,
menus and rebinding, mood expressions, arrests, and multiplayer host/join all
work in the new renderer.

## Goal
A player launches the same game and walks a genuinely good-looking low-poly
city — modeled buildings, dressed streets, animated characters with visible
moods — with every existing feature (talking, instructing, multiplayer)
working exactly as before.

## Out of Scope (this version)
- Godot/Unreal or any full engine migration (decided: raylib library swap).
- Custom-authored art, character customization, or paid asset packs — CC0 only.
- Gameplay changes of any kind: no new NPC abilities, no new world size,
  no new multiplayer features. Same game, new body.
- Advanced rendering: no PBR, no dynamic shadows beyond raylib's basics, no
  post-processing stack in v1 (fog + tinted lighting is the v1 mood budget).
- Skeletal animation *blending*; v1 uses each model's baked idle/walk clips
  switched hard (walk when moving, idle otherwise).
- Touching `src/core/` beyond what compiles (it should not change at all).

## Decisions Already Made
- **raylib via CMake FetchContent**, pinned to a release tag — reproducible on
  macOS/Linux/Windows, no system install needed, and the sfml@2 keg-only
  headache disappears with SFML itself. (raylib replaces SFML for windowing,
  input, text, and 2D overlay too — SFML is fully removed.)
- **Asset sources (all CC0 / public domain, commercial-safe, no attribution
  required — verify license text when downloading):**
  - Kenney — *City Kit (Commercial/Suburban/Roads)*, kenney.nl
  - Kay Lousberg — *KayKit City Builder Bits + Character packs*, kaylousberg.com
  - Quaternius — *Ultimate Modular Buildings, Animated Characters*, quaternius.com
  - Format: glTF (`.glb`) preferred — raylib loads it natively with animations.
- **Moods on 3D characters**: keep the game's signature expressive faces by
  rendering the existing procedural face (brows/eyes/mouth by `NpcMood`) onto a
  small texture and mapping it to the character head's face material — the
  low-poly packs use flat face textures, so a 128×128 generated face texture
  per mood slots right in. Fallback if a pack's UVs fight us: a subtle
  floating emote billboard above the head.
- **Base branch**: this work starts *after* the multiplayer PR stack (#28-#34)
  merges — full parity includes multiplayer rendering, and both rewrite
  `src/app/main.cpp`. Merging order: multiplayer first, then this.

## Affected Areas
- `src/app/Renderer3D.{hpp,cpp}` — **deleted**, replaced by:
  - `src/app/RaylibRenderer.{hpp,cpp}` — camera, city scene, characters,
    nameplates (raylib `DrawBillboard`/`GetWorldToScreen`), sky/fog/lighting.
  - `src/app/Assets.{hpp,cpp}` — loads `.glb` models/animations + generated
    face textures once; maps building `facadeKind`/`spotId` and NPC index →
    model + tint (same stable-index trick the current renderer uses).
  - `src/app/FaceTexture.{hpp,cpp}` — ports the existing procedural
    brow/eye/mouth drawing (currently GL immediate mode) to a raylib
    `RenderTexture2D` per `NpcMood`.
- `src/app/main.cpp` — same loop and modes, but raylib window/input/timing
  replaces SFML events (`WindowShouldClose`, `IsKeyPressed`, `GetMouseDelta` —
  which also deletes the macOS cursor-disassociation workaround, raylib's
  relative mouse handles it).

# Visual Layer Inventory — LLM-NPC Town (C++/raylib)

## A. World rendering — what draws each frame

All world geometry is emitted in `RaylibRenderer::drawCity` (`src/app/RaylibRenderer.cpp:165-252`).

**Ground plane** — a single flat `DrawPlane` sized to the whole map, flat grass color (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:169`).

**Roads** — two code paths (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:177-205`):
- If the KayKit road models `road_straight`, `road_straight_crossing`, `road_junction` are loaded, streets are laid as tiled models on a 16-unit pitch, with junction art at the four crossings and zebra-crossing (`crossing`) tiles on the arms (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:180-199`). Tile draw = `drawRoadTile` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:63-75`), which pins thickness to `kRoadThickness = 0.05f` (line 68) and floats the slab at y=0.01 to avoid z-fighting (line 73).
- Fallback with no models: two flat asphalt `DrawCube` strips (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:201-204`).

**Block slabs** — 3×3 grid of flat `DrawCube` slabs (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:208-215`): center block = pale-stone plaza (`kPlaza`), the NE block is skipped to stay grass (park), all others = `kSidewalk`.

**Buildings & props** — iterate `city.buildings()`, each keyed off collision AABBs (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:223-251`):
- Fountain special-cased by id before model lookup → composite primitives (line 227-230).
- Otherwise `modelForBuilding` returns a KayKit model, scaled by SizeSpec: `Uniform` → `drawModelUniform` (line 234), `Fill` → `drawModelFittedToAABB` (line 237). Both draw with `WHITE` tint (i.e. no tint; material/vertex colors only).
- No model → fallback `DrawCube` + `DrawCubeWires`, tinted by a hash of `facadeKind` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:242-249`).

**Fountain** — fully procedural, built from `DrawCylinder`/`DrawCylinderWires` primitives (`drawFountain`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:82-115`): stone basin, mid column + bowl, finial, plus translucent water discs. Colors are hardcoded `kStone/kStoneDark/kWater` (lines 87-89). Comment at 77-81 states the KayKit pack has no fountain model, so it is composed from primitives.

**Cars, benches, traffic lights, bushes, dumpsters, trash** — these are all KayKit models routed through the same building/prop path (curated map, see section D), sized `Uniform`.

## B. Characters — two entirely separate systems

**1. Rigged glTF pack characters** — `drawCharacter` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:254-306`). Real animated glTF models (`character->model`) with clip selection (idle/walk/gesture/death, lines 267-269), CPU skinning via `UpdateModelAnimation` (line 286), uniform-scaled to 1.8 units tall (lines 291-296), drawn `WHITE` (no tint). Fallback when no pack: a single marker `DrawCylinder`+wires (lines 259-262). Mood shown as a billboarded baked face texture above the head (`DrawBillboard`, lines 301-305).

**2. Composite primitive characters** (player-created) — `drawCompositeCharacter` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:308-382`). Pure primitives assembled from the socket system: tapered `DrawCylinder` body (line 347), `DrawSphere` head (350), sphere/cylinder hair variants (352-361), sphere/cube eyes (364-369), and a generic `DrawCube` for any part without a bespoke shape (378). Colored by flat palette (skin/hair/outfit, lines 327-329) plus a hardcoded `dark{38,38,44}` (330). Procedural walk-bob via `sin` (line 334); no skeleton (header note `RaylibRenderer.hpp:73`).

These two systems coexist: NPCs/remote players use the rigged glTF path; player-created avatars use the primitive-composite path. They are visually different construction methods sharing only the 1.8-unit height contract.

**Viewmodel (first-person weapon)** — `drawViewmodel` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:384-423`): hardcoded `DrawCubeV` boxes, a table of two specs — Fist (skin cube) and Pistol (dark cube + grip cube), lines 393-396. No models.

## C. Lighting, fog, sky, post-processing

**There is no real lighting model** — no directional/ambient light, no normals-based shading. "Light" is a single scalar `lightLevel` that multiplies fragment RGB.

**Fog shader** — the only shader, defined inline as GLSL 330 string constants in `Assets.cpp`:
- Vertex: `kFogVertexShader` (`Assets.cpp:29-45`) — passes world-space position through `matModel`.
- Fragment: `kFogFragmentShader` (`Assets.cpp:47-66`). It does three things: standard `texture0 * colDiffuse * fragColor` (line 60); a **warm tint** multiply `vec3(1.06, 1.0, 0.92)` times `lightLevel` (line 61); exponential-squared distance fog `1 - exp(-d*d)` blending toward `fogColor` (lines 62-64). So day/night "lighting" is just this per-fragment brightness multiply — flat, non-directional.

Compiled via `LoadShaderFromMemory` (`Assets.cpp:78`); degrades to plain look on failure (line 95-97). Fog density hardcoded `0.006f` (`Assets.cpp:89`). The shader is assigned to every city-model material (`Assets.cpp:265-269`) and every character material (`Assets.cpp:226-230`). The renderer also wraps the whole primitive batch in `BeginShaderMode` so ground/slabs/fountain/viewmodel haze identically (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:154-160`, ended at `endFrame` 425-428).

**Day/night** — `DayNight.hpp`. Sky is four bands (night/dawn/day/dusk) with linear blends (`skyColorAt`, lines 36-49). Palette: day sky `135,190,235` (light blue), night `16,22,44` (deep navy), dusk `222,136,84` (warm orange), with warmth peaking mid-dusk (lines 25-27, 42-47). `lightLevelAt` (lines 54-65): 1.0 daylight → 0.35 night, blended across the same dawn/dusk windows. `setTimeOfDay` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:121-135`) drives sky color, `lightLevel`, and the shader's fogColor from these curves; sky and fog always share the same color. `ClearBackground(renderer.skyColor())` at `main.cpp:935`.

**Nameplates / labels / HUD** (2D, `main.cpp`, drawn after the 3D pass): projected via `worldToScreen` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:430-442`). `drawNameplate` = text with a 1px shadow offset (`main.cpp:152-158`); `drawCenteredHudText` = text on a dark bar (142-149); combat callouts (1036-1042); weapon HUD + reload bar (1072-1074); death overlay red tint + text (1080-1085); pause dim (1088); assets-missing notice (1096-1100).

# Game Feel / Juice Audit — Evidence Inventory

## Headline corrections to the premise
- **This is a FIRST-PERSON game, not top-down 3D.** Camera sits at eye height with mouse-look. `RaylibRenderer.cpp:138` places the camera at `pose.position.y + 1.7f`; `beginFrame` builds a yaw/pitch look direction (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:141-144`); `main.cpp:103-109` `applyMouseLook` consumes `GetMouseDelta`. `CameraPose`/`LocalPlayer` are explicitly "First-person pose" (`main.cpp:66`, `RaylibRenderer.hpp:18`).
- **There is no drivable car / vehicle system.** All cars (`police_car`, `sedan_a`, etc.) are static collision props authored in `City.cpp:56-60` with `facadeKind 13`. No steer/throttle/mount/enter code exists anywhere (grep of `src/` for drive|vehicle|steer|throttle returned only unrelated "drives"/"driven" prose and network "drive the loop" comments). No car-hits-NPC logic exists.

## AUDIO — DEFINITIVE: NONE
There is zero audio in the project. A full grep of `src/` for `InitAudioDevice|LoadSound|LoadMusic|LoadWave|PlaySound|PlayMusic|UpdateMusicStream|StopSound|SetSoundVolume|SetMusicVolume|raudio|miniaudio|OpenAL` returns exactly one hit, and it is a comment describing intent, not code: `CombatEvents.hpp:9` ("main.cpp iterates the returned vectors and routes LLM triggers / **audio** / screen effects"). No audio device is ever initialized, no sound/music asset is ever loaded or played, and `CMakeLists.txt` links `raylib` but never references audio. The game runs completely silent — no music, no footsteps, no gunshot, no UI clicks, no voice.

## Player movement (`main.cpp:535-547`)
- **Instant velocity, no acceleration/deceleration.** Each frame a `wish` vector is summed from the four move actions, then `normalize`d, then applied directly: `target = position + wish * (kWalkSpeed * dt)` (`main.cpp:540-545`). No velocity is stored between frames; releasing a key stops movement immediately. No sprint, no crouch, no jump.
- **Speed:** `kWalkSpeed = 7.0f` units/sec (`main.cpp:53`). Diagonal is normalized so it isn't faster.
- **Collision response feel:** `City::resolveMovement` (`City.cpp:93-104`) does axis-separated clamping — it tries the new X against obstacles, then the new Z independently, against building AABBs inflated by the player radius (`kPlayerRadius = 0.45f`, `main.cpp:54`). This produces hard wall-sliding with a full stop into corners; no bounce, no push-back, no step-up. Collision is circle-vs-AABB only (`circleIntersectsAny`, `City.cpp:85-91`).
- Movement is frozen during an arrest: `if (jailSecondsLeft <= 0.f)` gates the whole movement block (`main.cpp:538`).

## Camera
- First-person, rebuilt from scratch every frame (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:137-147`). `fovy = 70.f`, `CAMERA_PERSPECTIVE`.
- **No smoothing/lerp** — camera position/target are set raw from player pose each frame (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:138-144`).
- **No zoom** (fovy is a hard constant), **no camera shake ever**, **no roll**. Yaw/pitch come only from raw mouse delta (`main.cpp:106-107`); pitch clamped to ±75° (`kMaxPitchDeg`, `main.cpp:58`, `main.cpp:107`). Mouse sensitivity `0.12f` (`main.cpp:57`), applied with no smoothing/acceleration.
- Cursor is hard-locked via `DisableCursor()` in play, toggled to `EnableCursor()` for menu/dialogue (`main.cpp:416`, `main.cpp:536`, `main.cpp:563` etc.).

## Animation — MIXED: skeletal for NPCs, procedural for player-created characters
- **Pack NPCs / remote players: true SKELETAL glTF animation.** `drawCharacter` selects a clip index (`walk`/`idle`/`gesture`/`death`), advances a per-entity clock, computes a frame at 60 fps, and calls raylib's `UpdateModelAnimation(character->model, animation, frame)` — CPU skinning (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:267-287`). Clip choice is state-driven: `walking ? walk : idle`, gesture overrides when `gesturePhase > 0`, death overrides all (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:267-269`). Frame loop is `int(time*60) % frameCount` — **no blending/crossfade between clips**; the clock just resets to 0 on clip change (`RaylibRenderer.hpp:100-106`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:272-275`).
- **Player-created "composite" characters: PROCEDURAL only, no skeleton.** `drawCompositeCharacter` builds the figure from primitive parts and fakes a walk with a vertical bob: `bob = walking ? fabs(sin(phase*7)) * 0.05f : 0` applied via `rlTranslatef` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:334-336`). Header states it outright: "`phase` drives the procedural walk bob (no skeleton in v1)" (`RaylibRenderer.hpp:73`).
- **Walk-vs-idle trigger** is pure positional delta, not a velocity/state machine: `visual.walking = distanceXZ(npc.position(), npcLastPos[i]) > 0.01f` (`main.cpp:963`).
- **Facing/turning is instant (snap), no easing.** NPC facing is set directly by `atan2` either toward a target (`Npc::faceToward`, `Npc.cpp:102-109`) or derived from motion above a 0.5 u/s threshold (`Npc::deriveFacingFromMotion`, `Npc.cpp:208-219`). The render applies facing as a hard `DrawModelEx` rotation (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:295`). No turn interpolation anywhere.
- **Faces are billboarded flat textures**, not rigged — a mood emote floats above the head (`DrawBillboard`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:301-305`), one of six procedural `NpcFace` textures. The dead don't emote (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:301`).
- **Idle** = the model's idle glTF clip for pack NPCs; composite characters are fully static when not walking (bob = 0).

## Action feedback (what the player perceives)
- **Talk:** press-T opens a dialogue overlay; the NPC turns to face you (`npc.lookAt`, `main.cpp:574`). Reply text streams into a transcript, plus an italic "stage direction" line for tag-only actions ("waves at you.", etc.) from `stageDirection` (`main.cpp:113-126`, `main.cpp:909-916`). Mood drives the billboard face. **No sound, no particle.**
- **Attack:** LMB → `world.playerAttack` (`main.cpp:552-553`). Feedback is purely the **viewmodel thrust/recoil**: `attackAnimFraction` is slammed to `1.0` on attack (`World.cpp:20`, `World.cpp:32`) and decays over ~0.15 s (`World.cpp:145`), driving a forward push (fist) or backward recoil (pistol) of a cube prop in `drawViewmodel` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:384-423`). **No muzzle flash, no tracer render, no impact particle, no hit-stop, no screen shake, no sound.** The pistol projectile is simulated (`World.cpp:34-42`, `tickProjectiles` `World.cpp:61-101`) but is **never drawn** — it's an invisible hitscan-like bullet.
- **Knock down / kill an NPC:** the only feedback is a floating text **combat callout** above the NPC ("Ow! Help!", "You'll regret that!", or "<name> collapses!") lasting 3 s (`main.cpp:718-725`, drawn `main.cpp:1036-1045`), plus the NPC switching to the `death` clip / Fleeing / Hostile state (`Npc::takeDamage`, `Npc.cpp:221-230`). No blood, no particle, no sound, no hit-stop.
- **Get shot by an NPC:** a **red full-screen vignette flash** — `hurtFlash = 0.35f` on a landed shot (`main.cpp:727`), rendered as a fading red rectangle whose alpha scales `180 * (hurtFlash/0.35)` (`main.cpp:1094-1098`). This is the single genuine "juice" primitive in the game. Also a health-bar drop (HUD, `main.cpp:1073-1077`). No shake, no sound.
- **Get arrested:** teleport to police station + a centered HUD banner "Arrested: disturbing the peace. Released in Ns" with a countdown; movement locked for `kJailSeconds = 10.f` (`main.cpp:689-712`, banner `main.cpp:1054-1059`, `main.cpp:61`). No sound, no transition effect.
- **Death:** a dark-red full-screen overlay + "You died." text + respawn prompt (`main.cpp:1079-1086`). Static, no animation/sound.
- **Buy:** there is no purchase/economy/transaction system in the code at all.

## Frame / tick structure
- **Delta-time based, clamped, no fixed timestep, no interpolation.** `const float dt = fmin(0.03f, GetFrameTime())` (`main.cpp:520`) — dt is capped at 30 ms (≈33 fps floor) to keep physics stable on hitches. `SetTargetFPS(60)` with `FLAG_VSYNC_HINT` (`main.cpp:325-327`). Everything (movement, combat, cooldowns, world clock, gossip timer) integrates against this single `dt`. There is **no interpolation/extrapolation layer** — sim and render run in lockstep in one loop. Animation timing separately reads raylib's `GetFrameTime()`/`GetTime()` directly (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:276`, `main.cpp:975`).
- One shared world clock advances once per frame (`world.state().advanceTime(dt)`, `main.cpp:648`); menu pauses NPC sim but the comment notes the town keeps living.

## Juice primitives present vs. absent
**Present:**
- Red hurt-flash vignette with linear fade (`main.cpp:421`, `727`, `1094-1098`) — the only screen-space effect.
- Viewmodel punch/recoil tween via `attackAnimFraction` linear decay (`World.cpp:145`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:412`).
- Procedural walk-bob `fabs(sin)` for composite characters only (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:334`).
- Floating combat/name callouts with TTL fade-out logic on TTL but text alpha is constant (`main.cpp:742-745`, `1036-1045`).
- Gesture-phase timer feeding a gesture animation clip (`Npc.cpp:114-121`, `Npc.hpp:96-97`).
- dt clamping (`main.cpp:520`).

**Absent (searched, not found in `src/`):**
- **No audio of any kind** (see above).
- **No particle system** (grep `particle` → 0 code hits).
- **No easing/tween helpers** — grep `tween|easing|ease|smoothstep|EaseIn|EaseOut` → 0 hits; all fades are hand-rolled linear.
- **No screen shake / hit-stop / slow-mo / freeze-frame** — grep `shake|hitstop|freeze|slowmo` → 0 code hits.
- **No camera smoothing, no zoom, no FOV kick.**
- **No muzzle flash / bullet tracer / impact decal / blood.**
- **No movement acceleration/friction.**
- **No footstep or turn animation.**

### One notable staleness flag
`RaylibRenderer.hpp:3-5` still carries a top-of-file banner "NOT YET IN THE BUILD... TODO(implement): step 3" and several methods are annotated `TODO(implement)` (`RaylibRenderer.hpp:48`, `62`, `67`, `85`, `91`), yet `RaylibRenderer.cpp` fully implements all of them and `CMakeLists.txt:66` compiles it into the game target. The comments are out of date; the renderer is live.</result>

# Visual Layer Inventory — LLM-NPC Town (C++/raylib)

## A. World rendering — what draws each frame

All world geometry is emitted in `RaylibRenderer::drawCity` (`src/app/RaylibRenderer.cpp:165-252`).

**Ground plane** — a single flat `DrawPlane` sized to the whole map, flat grass color (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:169`).

**Roads** — two code paths (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:177-205`):
- If the KayKit road models `road_straight`, `road_straight_crossing`, `road_junction` are loaded, streets are laid as tiled models on a 16-unit pitch, with junction art at the four crossings and zebra-crossing (`crossing`) tiles on the arms (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:180-199`). Tile draw = `drawRoadTile` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:63-75`), which pins thickness to `kRoadThickness = 0.05f` (line 68) and floats the slab at y=0.01 to avoid z-fighting (line 73).
- Fallback with no models: two flat asphalt `DrawCube` strips (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:201-204`).

**Block slabs** — 3×3 grid of flat `DrawCube` slabs (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:208-215`): center block = pale-stone plaza (`kPlaza`), the NE block is skipped to stay grass (park), all others = `kSidewalk`.

**Buildings & props** — iterate `city.buildings()`, each keyed off collision AABBs (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:223-251`):
- Fountain special-cased by id before model lookup → composite primitives (line 227-230).
- Otherwise `modelForBuilding` returns a KayKit model, scaled by SizeSpec: `Uniform` → `drawModelUniform` (line 234), `Fill` → `drawModelFittedToAABB` (line 237). Both draw with `WHITE` tint (i.e. no tint; material/vertex colors only).
- No model → fallback `DrawCube` + `DrawCubeWires`, tinted by a hash of `facadeKind` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:242-249`).

**Fountain** — fully procedural, built from `DrawCylinder`/`DrawCylinderWires` primitives (`drawFountain`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:82-115`): stone basin, mid column + bowl, finial, plus translucent water discs. Colors are hardcoded `kStone/kStoneDark/kWater` (lines 87-89). Comment at 77-81 states the KayKit pack has no fountain model, so it is composed from primitives.

**Cars, benches, traffic lights, bushes, dumpsters, trash** — these are all KayKit models routed through the same building/prop path (curated map, see section D), sized `Uniform`.

## B. Characters — two entirely separate systems

**1. Rigged glTF pack characters** — `drawCharacter` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:254-306`). Real animated glTF models (`character->model`) with clip selection (idle/walk/gesture/death, lines 267-269), CPU skinning via `UpdateModelAnimation` (line 286), uniform-scaled to 1.8 units tall (lines 291-296), drawn `WHITE` (no tint). Fallback when no pack: a single marker `DrawCylinder`+wires (lines 259-262). Mood shown as a billboarded baked face texture above the head (`DrawBillboard`, lines 301-305).

**2. Composite primitive characters** (player-created) — `drawCompositeCharacter` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:308-382`). Pure primitives assembled from the socket system: tapered `DrawCylinder` body (line 347), `DrawSphere` head (350), sphere/cylinder hair variants (352-361), sphere/cube eyes (364-369), and a generic `DrawCube` for any part without a bespoke shape (378). Colored by flat palette (skin/hair/outfit, lines 327-329) plus a hardcoded `dark{38,38,44}` (330). Procedural walk-bob via `sin` (line 334); no skeleton (header note `RaylibRenderer.hpp:73`).

These two systems coexist: NPCs/remote players use the rigged glTF path; player-created avatars use the primitive-composite path. They are visually different construction methods sharing only the 1.8-unit height contract.

**Viewmodel (first-person weapon)** — `drawViewmodel` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:384-423`): hardcoded `DrawCubeV` boxes, a table of two specs — Fist (skin cube) and Pistol (dark cube + grip cube), lines 393-396. No models.

**There is no real lighting model** — no directional/ambient light, no normals-based shading. "Light" is a single scalar `lightLevel` that multiplies fragment RGB.

**Fog shader** — the only shader, defined inline as GLSL 330 string constants in `Assets.cpp`:
- Vertex: `kFogVertexShader` (`Assets.cpp:29-45`) — passes world-space position through `matModel`.
- Fragment: `kFogFragmentShader` (`Assets.cpp:47-66`). It does three things: standard `texture0 * colDiffuse * fragColor` (line 60); a **warm tint** multiply `vec3(1.06, 1.0, 0.92)` times `lightLevel` (line 61); exponential-squared distance fog `1 - exp(-d*d)` blending toward `fogColor` (lines 62-64). So day/night "lighting" is just this per-fragment brightness multiply — flat, non-directional.

Compiled via `LoadShaderFromMemory` (`Assets.cpp:78`); degrades to plain look on failure (line 95-97). Fog density hardcoded `0.006f` (`Assets.cpp:89`). The shader is assigned to every city-model material (`Assets.cpp:265-269`) and every character material (`Assets.cpp:226-230`). The renderer also wraps the whole primitive batch in `BeginShaderMode` so ground/slabs/fountain/viewmodel haze identically (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:154-160`, ended at `endFrame` 425-428).

**Day/night** — `DayNight.hpp`. Sky is four bands (night/dawn/day/dusk) with linear blends (`skyColorAt`, lines 36-49). Palette: day sky `135,190,235` (light blue), night `16,22,44` (deep navy), dusk `222,136,84` (warm orange), with warmth peaking mid-dusk (lines 25-27, 42-47). `lightLevelAt` (lines 54-65): 1.0 daylight → 0.35 night, blended across the same dawn/dusk windows. `setTimeOfDay` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:121-135`) drives sky color, `lightLevel`, and the shader's fogColor from these curves; sky and fog always share the same color. `ClearBackground(renderer.skyColor())` at `main.cpp:935`.

**Nameplates / labels / HUD** (2D, `main.cpp`, drawn after the 3D pass): projected via `worldToScreen` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:430-442`). `drawNameplate` = text with a 1px shadow offset (`main.cpp:152-158`); `drawCenteredHudText` = text on a dark bar (142-149); combat callouts (1036-1042); weapon HUD + reload bar (1072-1074); death overlay red tint + text (1080-1085); pause dim (1088); assets-missing notice (1096-1100).

**Baked face emotes** — `FaceTexture::bake` (`FaceTexture.cpp:35-100`): six moods drawn procedurally into a 128px `RenderTexture` (cream bubble, dark eyes/brows, lip mouths, blush), independent of downloads. This is the only render-to-texture; not a post-process pass.

**No post-processing** — no bloom/SSAO/tonemap/full-screen shader. Grep confirmed only `LoadRenderTexture`/`BeginTextureMode` usage is the face baking; the 2D overlays are the only screen-space effects (flat colored `DrawRectangle` tints).

## D. Assets — packs, stems, size contract, fallbacks

Loaded once at startup in `Assets::Assets` (`Assets.cpp:70-177`). Asset root is `assets/models/city` and `assets/models/characters` (lines 99-100); presence gated on `citybits_texture.png` (line 101). The pack is **KayKit** (city bits + adventurers; see character stems and `citybits_texture.png`).

Loaded from `.gltf` via `loadCityModel` (`Assets.cpp:250-272`).

**Curated landmark map** (`Assets.cpp:108-127`): bakery→building_A, police→building_E, coffee→building_B, library→building_D, hardware→building_C, office_a→building_F, tower→building_H, taxi_cab→car_taxi, plus benches, carts (box_B), traffic lights, bushes, cars, dumpster, trash. Explicit note that there is **no** `fountain` entry so the composite primitive path is taken (lines 114-117).

**Characters** (`Assets.cpp:172`): five KayKit adventurers loaded from `.glb` — `Barbarian`, `Knight`, `Mage`, `Rogue`, `Rogue_Hooded`. Knight doubles as police uniform (`knightIndex_`, lines 240, 246). Clip names resolved by string: `Idle`, `Walking_A`, `Cheer`, `Death_A_Pose` (`Assets.cpp:233-239`). Note on load-time mesh compaction to drop unskinned attachment meshes so raylib 5.5 skinning doesn't crash — meaning **held hand-props are stripped** (lines 202-221).

**SizeSpec contract** (`Assets.hpp:45-53`, table at `Assets.cpp:130-154`): `Fill` = stretch to collision AABB (default, buildings); `Uniform` = scale uniformly to a world-meter height, grounded/centered (vehicles/props/furniture, so proportions survive). Explicit heights e.g. taxi 1.5, cart 1.9, bench 0.9, fountain 2.6, traffic light 4.5, bush 1.1, cars 1.35, dumpster 1.4. Buildings unlisted → Fill (`sizeSpecFor`, `Assets.cpp:274-278`).

**Fallbacks when assets missing** (never crash — `Assets.hpp:20-21`):
- No city tree → `loaded_ = false`, `modelForBuilding` returns nullptr → renderer draws hashed-tint fallback cubes (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:240-249`).
- Missing individual stem → logged, skipped (`Assets.cpp:252-254`).
- No characters → marker cylinder (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:259-262`).
- Shader compile fail → plain (unfogged, untinted) look (`Assets.cpp:95-97`).
- Generic building filler picked by FNV-1a hash of id over `building_A..H` (`Assets.cpp:14-21`, 156-157, 280-289).

## E. Character-part composite system (`CharacterParts.*`)

Socket/composite catalog, data-driven. Categories: `Body, Head, Eyes, Hair` (`CharacterParts.hpp:14`). Attachment via `CategorySpec` parent+socket chain: Body root → Head on "head" → Eyes on "eyes" and Hair on "hair" (`CharacterParts.cpp:31-37`). Parts declare a `localSize` box (anchor bottom-center) and named sockets (`CharacterParts.hpp:32-38`).

**(1) Intentional art direction vs placeholder primitives.**
- Reads as *intentional*: the KayKit city-bits models for buildings/roads/cars/props (curated landmark silhouettes, `Assets.cpp:108-127`), the KayKit rigged adventurers with named animation clips, the four-band day/night sky+fog color story (`DayNight.hpp:25-27`), and the warm-flat ground/asphalt/plaza palette (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:20-24`, comment "warm, low-poly-friendly flats").

# Game Feel / Juice Audit — Evidence Inventory

## Headline corrections to the premise
- **This is a FIRST-PERSON game, not top-down 3D.** Camera sits at eye height with mouse-look. `RaylibRenderer.cpp:138` places the camera at `pose.position.y + 1.7f`; `beginFrame` builds a yaw/pitch look direction (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:141-144`); `main.cpp:103-109` `applyMouseLook` consumes `GetMouseDelta`. `CameraPose`/`LocalPlayer` are explicitly "First-person pose" (`main.cpp:66`, `RaylibRenderer.hpp:18`).
- **There is no drivable car / vehicle system.** All cars (`police_car`, `sedan_a`, etc.) are static collision props authored in `City.cpp:56-60` with `facadeKind 13`. No steer/throttle/mount/enter code exists anywhere (grep of `src/` for drive|vehicle|steer|throttle returned only unrelated "drives"/"driven" prose and network "drive the loop" comments). No car-hits-NPC logic exists.

## AUDIO — DEFINITIVE: NONE
There is zero audio in the project. A full grep of `src/` for `InitAudioDevice|LoadSound|LoadMusic|LoadWave|PlaySound|PlayMusic|UpdateMusicStream|StopSound|SetSoundVolume|SetMusicVolume|raudio|miniaudio|OpenAL` returns exactly one hit, and it is a comment describing intent, not code: `CombatEvents.hpp:9` ("main.cpp iterates the returned vectors and routes LLM triggers / **audio** / screen effects"). No audio device is ever initialized, no sound/music asset is ever loaded or played, and `CMakeLists.txt` links `raylib` but never references audio. The game runs completely silent — no music, no footsteps, no gunshot, no UI clicks, no voice.

## Player movement (`main.cpp:535-547`)
- **Instant velocity, no acceleration/deceleration.** Each frame a `wish` vector is summed from the four move actions, then `normalize`d, then applied directly: `target = position + wish * (kWalkSpeed * dt)` (`main.cpp:540-545`). No velocity is stored between frames; releasing a key stops movement immediately. No sprint, no crouch, no jump.
- **Speed:** `kWalkSpeed = 7.0f` units/sec (`main.cpp:53`). Diagonal is normalized so it isn't faster.
- **Collision response feel:** `City::resolveMovement` (`City.cpp:93-104`) does axis-separated clamping — it tries the new X against obstacles, then the new Z independently, against building AABBs inflated by the player radius (`kPlayerRadius = 0.45f`, `main.cpp:54`). This produces hard wall-sliding with a full stop into corners; no bounce, no push-back, no step-up. Collision is circle-vs-AABB only (`circleIntersectsAny`, `City.cpp:85-91`).
- Movement is frozen during an arrest: `if (jailSecondsLeft <= 0.f)` gates the whole movement block (`main.cpp:538`).

## Camera
- First-person, rebuilt from scratch every frame (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:137-147`). `fovy = 70.f`, `CAMERA_PERSPECTIVE`.
- **No smoothing/lerp** — camera position/target are set raw from player pose each frame (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:138-144`).
- **No zoom** (fovy is a hard constant), **no camera shake ever**, **no roll**. Yaw/pitch come only from raw mouse delta (`main.cpp:106-107`); pitch clamped to ±75° (`kMaxPitchDeg`, `main.cpp:58`, `main.cpp:107`). Mouse sensitivity `0.12f` (`main.cpp:57`), applied with no smoothing/acceleration.
- Cursor is hard-locked via `DisableCursor()` in play, toggled to `EnableCursor()` for menu/dialogue (`main.cpp:416`, `main.cpp:536`, `main.cpp:563` etc.).

## Animation — MIXED: skeletal for NPCs, procedural for player-created characters
- **Pack NPCs / remote players: true SKELETAL glTF animation.** `drawCharacter` selects a clip index (`walk`/`idle`/`gesture`/`death`), advances a per-entity clock, computes a frame at 60 fps, and calls raylib's `UpdateModelAnimation(character->model, animation, frame)` — CPU skinning (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:267-287`). Clip choice is state-driven: `walking ? walk : idle`, gesture overrides when `gesturePhase > 0`, death overrides all (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:267-269`). Frame loop is `int(time*60) % frameCount` — **no blending/crossfade between clips**; the clock just resets to 0 on clip change (`RaylibRenderer.hpp:100-106`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:272-275`).
- **Player-created "composite" characters: PROCEDURAL only, no skeleton.** `drawCompositeCharacter` builds the figure from primitive parts and fakes a walk with a vertical bob: `bob = walking ? fabs(sin(phase*7)) * 0.05f : 0` applied via `rlTranslatef` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:334-336`). Header states it outright: "`phase` drives the procedural walk bob (no skeleton in v1)" (`RaylibRenderer.hpp:73`).
- **Walk-vs-idle trigger** is pure positional delta, not a velocity/state machine: `visual.walking = distanceXZ(npc.position(), npcLastPos[i]) > 0.01f` (`main.cpp:963`).
- **Facing/turning is instant (snap), no easing.** NPC facing is set directly by `atan2` either toward a target (`Npc::faceToward`, `Npc.cpp:102-109`) or derived from motion above a 0.5 u/s threshold (`Npc::deriveFacingFromMotion`, `Npc.cpp:208-219`). The render applies facing as a hard `DrawModelEx` rotation (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:295`). No turn interpolation anywhere.
- **Faces are billboarded flat textures**, not rigged — a mood emote floats above the head (`DrawBillboard`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:301-305`), one of six procedural `NpcFace` textures. The dead don't emote (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:301`).
- **Idle** = the model's idle glTF clip for pack NPCs; composite characters are fully static when not walking (bob = 0).

## Action feedback (what the player perceives)
- **Talk:** press-T opens a dialogue overlay; the NPC turns to face you (`npc.lookAt`, `main.cpp:574`). Reply text streams into a transcript, plus an italic "stage direction" line for tag-only actions ("waves at you.", etc.) from `stageDirection` (`main.cpp:113-126`, `main.cpp:909-916`). Mood drives the billboard face. **No sound, no particle.**
- **Attack:** LMB → `world.playerAttack` (`main.cpp:552-553`). Feedback is purely the **viewmodel thrust/recoil**: `attackAnimFraction` is slammed to `1.0` on attack (`World.cpp:20`, `World.cpp:32`) and decays over ~0.15 s (`World.cpp:145`), driving a forward push (fist) or backward recoil (pistol) of a cube prop in `drawViewmodel` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:384-423`). **No muzzle flash, no tracer render, no impact particle, no hit-stop, no screen shake, no sound.** The pistol projectile is simulated (`World.cpp:34-42`, `tickProjectiles` `World.cpp:61-101`) but is **never drawn** — it's an invisible hitscan-like bullet.
- **Knock down / kill an NPC:** the only feedback is a floating text **combat callout** above the NPC ("Ow! Help!", "You'll regret that!", or "<name> collapses!") lasting 3 s (`main.cpp:718-725`, drawn `main.cpp:1036-1045`), plus the NPC switching to the `death` clip / Fleeing / Hostile state (`Npc::takeDamage`, `Npc.cpp:221-230`). No blood, no particle, no sound, no hit-stop.
- **Get shot by an NPC:** a **red full-screen vignette flash** — `hurtFlash = 0.35f` on a landed shot (`main.cpp:727`), rendered as a fading red rectangle whose alpha scales `180 * (hurtFlash/0.35)` (`main.cpp:1094-1098`). This is the single genuine "juice" primitive in the game. Also a health-bar drop (HUD, `main.cpp:1073-1077`). No shake, no sound.
- **Get arrested:** teleport to police station + a centered HUD banner "Arrested: disturbing the peace. Released in Ns" with a countdown; movement locked for `kJailSeconds = 10.f` (`main.cpp:689-712`, banner `main.cpp:1054-1059`, `main.cpp:61`). No sound, no transition effect.
- **Death:** a dark-red full-screen overlay + "You died." text + respawn prompt (`main.cpp:1079-1086`). Static, no animation/sound.
- **Buy:** there is no purchase/economy/transaction system in the code at all.

## Frame / tick structure
- **Delta-time based, clamped, no fixed timestep, no interpolation.** `const float dt = fmin(0.03f, GetFrameTime())` (`main.cpp:520`) — dt is capped at 30 ms (≈33 fps floor) to keep physics stable on hitches. `SetTargetFPS(60)` with `FLAG_VSYNC_HINT` (`main.cpp:325-327`). Everything (movement, combat, cooldowns, world clock, gossip timer) integrates against this single `dt`. There is **no interpolation/extrapolation layer** — sim and render run in lockstep in one loop. Animation timing separately reads raylib's `GetFrameTime()`/`GetTime()` directly (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:276`, `main.cpp:975`).
- One shared world clock advances once per frame (`world.state().advanceTime(dt)`, `main.cpp:648`); menu pauses NPC sim but the comment notes the town keeps living.

## Juice primitives present vs. absent
**Present:**
- Red hurt-flash vignette with linear fade (`main.cpp:421`, `727`, `1094-1098`) — the only screen-space effect.
- Viewmodel punch/recoil tween via `attackAnimFraction` linear decay (`World.cpp:145`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:412`).
- Procedural walk-bob `fabs(sin)` for composite characters only (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:334`).
- Floating combat/name callouts with TTL fade-out logic on TTL but text alpha is constant (`main.cpp:742-745`, `1036-1045`).
- Gesture-phase timer feeding a gesture animation clip (`Npc.cpp:114-121`, `Npc.hpp:96-97`).
- dt clamping (`main.cpp:520`).

**Absent (searched, not found in `src/`):**
- **No audio of any kind** (see above).
- **No particle system** (grep `particle` → 0 code hits).
- **No easing/tween helpers** — grep `tween|easing|ease|smoothstep|EaseIn|EaseOut` → 0 hits; all fades are hand-rolled linear.
- **No screen shake / hit-stop / slow-mo / freeze-frame** — grep `shake|hitstop|freeze|slowmo` → 0 code hits.
- **No camera smoothing, no zoom, no FOV kick.**
- **No muzzle flash / bullet tracer / impact decal / blood.**
- **No movement acceleration/friction.**
- **No footstep or turn animation.**

### One notable staleness flag
`RaylibRenderer.hpp:3-5` still carries a top-of-file banner "NOT YET IN THE BUILD... TODO(implement): step 3" and several methods are annotated `TODO(implement)` (`RaylibRenderer.hpp:48`, `62`, `67`, `85`, `91`), yet `RaylibRenderer.cpp` fully implements all of them and `CMakeLists.txt:66` compiles it into the game target. ## Conversation & Menu UX Audit — LLM-NPC Town Game

All citations are `file:line`. Files read in full: `Menu.hpp/.cpp`, `LlmClient.hpp/.cpp`, `Npc.hpp/.cpp`, `DialogUI.hpp/.cpp`, `DialogueSession.hpp`, plus the dialogue sections of `main.cpp`.

Note: the actual conversation interface lives in `src/app/DialogUI.cpp` (the transcript + input box) and `src/core/DialogueSession.*` (the state machine), not in `Menu.cpp`. `Menu.cpp` is the pause menu only and never touches conversation.

### 1. Starting a conversation with an NPC

- Trigger is **proximity + a key press**, not proximity alone. Each frame the nearest NPC within `kTalkRadius = 3.5` world units is computed into `nearbyNpc` (`main.cpp:841`, `world.nearestNpcWithin(...)`; constant at `main.cpp:55`).
- Affordance: while in `Playing` mode and an NPC is in range, a centered HUD prompt renders 84px above the screen bottom: `"[" + bindings.key(Action::Talk) + "] Talk to " + npc.persona().name` (`main.cpp:1048-1052`). Default Talk key is **T** (`KeyBindings.cpp:31`).
- Pressing Talk opens the chat only if the NPC is `NpcState::Idle` (not fleeing/hostile/dead) (`main.cpp:565-568`). On open: `session.open(nearbyNpc)`, the NPC turns to face the player via `npc.lookAt(player.position)` (`main.cpp:574`), the dialog is reset/enabled, and a System transcript line is seeded: `"You are talking to " + name + " (" + role + "). Enter sends, Esc leaves."` (`main.cpp:579-581`). Mode switches to `Dialogue` and the mouse cursor is enabled (`main.cpp:582-583`).
- `dialog.swallowPendingText()` (`main.cpp:578`, impl `DialogUI.cpp:109`, `71-80`) discards the frame's keystrokes so the "T" that opened the chat doesn't leak into the input box.

### 2. Typing a message

- Yes, there is an in-game single-line text input box, rendered at the bottom of the screen (`DialogUI::render`, `DialogUI.cpp:193-203`). Box rect: `{kPadding, h - kInputHeight - kPadding*0.5, w - 2*kPadding, kInputHeight}` — full width, `kInputHeight = 48` px tall (`DialogUI.cpp:12-13, 194-195`). Fill color `{30,30,36}`, border `{120,160,220}` when enabled / `{70,70,70}` when disabled (`DialogUI.cpp:196-198`).
- The line renders as `"> " + input_ + "_"` (a literal underscore cursor when enabled) at font size `kFontSize = 16` (`DialogUI.cpp:15, 200-203`). White text when enabled, gray `{120,120,120}` when disabled.
- Input handling in `pollInput()` (`DialogUI.cpp:71-93`): printable ASCII only (`ch >= 32 && ch < 127`) via `GetCharPressed()` (`DialogUI.cpp:74-79`). **No character limit** on the chat input — the input box has no length cap (contrast the Menu/Creator fields which cap at 32/160, `Menu.cpp:205`, and the join address at 64, `Menu.cpp:228`).
- Editing: backspace with key-repeat (`IsKeyPressed(KEY_BACKSPACE) || IsKeyPressedRepeat(KEY_BACKSPACE)`) pops one char (`DialogUI.cpp:83-86`). No left/right cursor movement, no mid-string editing — append/pop-from-end only.
- Submit: `KEY_ENTER` with a non-empty input returns the string and clears the box (`DialogUI.cpp:87-91`). Empty Enter does nothing. There is no send button.
- The submitted line is echoed immediately as a `Player` transcript line labeled `"You"` (`main.cpp:612`), then `npc.ask(submitted)` fires the request (`main.cpp:613`), and the input box is disabled until the reply lands (`dialog.setInputEnabled(false)`, `main.cpp:617`). Guard `!npc.waiting()` (`main.cpp:611`) prevents sending a second line while one is in flight.

### 3. How the NPC response is shown

- **Streaming, token-by-token.** On submit, `dialog.beginStreaming(npc.persona().name)` starts a live line (`main.cpp:616`, impl `DialogUI.cpp:111-115`). Each frame `client.drainDeltas()` is pumped (`main.cpp:845-850`); matching fragments call `dialog.appendStreamingDelta(delta.text)` (`main.cpp:848`), appending to `streamingText_` (`DialogUI.cpp:117-119`).
- The in-progress line renders live at the bottom of the transcript as `speaker + ": " + streamingText_ + "_"` (literal underscore cursor), colored NPC-gold `{255,230,180}` (`DialogUI.cpp:154-162`, color at `DialogUI.cpp:19-20`).
- On completion, `client.drainReplies()` routes the reply (`main.cpp:851-930`). `dialog.endStreaming()` removes the live line (`main.cpp:904`, `DialogUI.cpp:121-125`) and the finalized text is appended as a permanent `Npc` transcript line (`main.cpp:907`). If the model spoke no words but performed an action, a System stage-direction line is shown instead; if truly empty, `"(<name> says nothing.)"` (`main.cpp:909-916`). On error, a System line: `"[<name> seems distracted: <errorMessage>]"` (`main.cpp:924-926`). Then input is re-enabled (`main.cpp:928`).
- Layout/wrapping: it is a **scrolling transcript**, not a single dialogue box. Lines render newest-backward filling the vertical space from `transcriptBottom = h - kInputHeight - kPadding` upward (`DialogUI.cpp:140, 171-191`). Line height `kLineHeight = 22`, font size 16 (`DialogUI.cpp:14-15`). Word-aware wrap to `wrapChars = max(20, (w - 32)/9)` chars/line — a crude fixed-9px-per-char estimate (`DialogUI.cpp:141-142`, `wrap()` at `28-68`).
- History/log: **yes, a visible running transcript** kept in a `std::deque<TranscriptLine>` capped at `kMaxTranscriptLines = 200` (`DialogUI.hpp:58, 68`; `DialogUI.cpp:97-100`). Player lines are blue `{180,220,255}`, NPC gold, System gray (`DialogUI.cpp:17-23`). Behind it a dim overlay `{8,10,16,150}` is drawn (`main.cpp:1088`).
- **No scrollback control** — there is no mouse-wheel or page-up handling anywhere in `DialogUI` or the Dialogue input branch. Only whatever most-recent lines fit on screen are visible; older lines scroll off and cannot be recalled within a session.
- Persistence: the transcript is per-open-session; `dialog.reset()` clears it every time a new conversation opens (`main.cpp:576`, `DialogUI.cpp:127-134`). The NPC's underlying `history_` (capped `maxHistoryTurns=10`, i.e. 20 entries) persists across chats for LLM context (`Npc.hpp:32, 182`; `Npc.cpp:199-206`) but is never shown to the player.
- How long it stays / dismissal: the reply stays as long as the dialog is open; the whole dialog is dismissed by Esc (see §7). Lines are not individually timed.

### 4. Latency handling (while `busy()`)

- There is a "thinking" indicator, but it is driven by the **streaming state**, not `LlmClient::busy()` and not `setThinking()`. `LlmClient::busy()` (`LlmClient.hpp:92`) and `DialogUI::setThinking()` (`DialogUI.cpp:102-105`) both **exist but are never called** anywhere in the app (grep confirms `setThinking` has zero call sites; `busy()` is unused in `main.cpp`).
- The actual indicator: after submit, `beginStreaming` sets `streaming_ = true` with empty `streamingText_`. In `render()`, the branch `else if (thinking_ || streaming_)` fires and draws `"... <speaker> is thinking..."` in gray `{140,140,140}` (`DialogUI.cpp:163-168`). Once the first delta arrives, `streamingText_` is non-empty and it switches to the live streamed text (`DialogUI.cpp:154`). So the player sees "X is thinking..." only until the first token, then live words. It is static text — **no animated dots/spinner** (the dots are the literal string `"... "`).
- Can the player move while waiting? **No, not in the chat.** During `Dialogue` mode the input branch handles only Esc and `pollInput` (`main.cpp:585-620`); WASD movement and combat are gated behind `mode == AppMode::Playing` (`main.cpp:535-557`). The player is frozen in place, cursor visible, staring at the transcript until Esc or the reply. However, the world keeps simulating: NPC behaviors and the day/night clock keep running during dialogue (`main.cpp:648, 651-661` — "NPC behaviors keep running during dialogue, freeze in the menu"). The input box is locked (`setInputEnabled(false)`) so you also cannot queue a next message while waiting.

### 5. The pause menu — Pages, navigation, layout machinery

Opened by `Action::OpenMenu` (default **Escape**) or `KEY_ESCAPE` while in Playing mode; `menu.open()`, mode → `Menu`, cursor enabled (`main.cpp:559-564`). `menu.open()` resets to the Main page and clears edit/toast state (`Menu.cpp:102-109`).

Navigation is **mouse-click only** for buttons (keyboard is used only for text-field typing and Escape). `update()` polls `IsMouseButtonPressed(MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT)`, walks the `layout()` hit-rects, and dispatches by `Hit.id` (`Menu.cpp:253-333`). Escape backs out one page or resumes from Main (`Menu.cpp:245-251`). Clicking empty space cancels captures/edits (`Menu.cpp:328-332`).

**Layout machinery:** `Page` enum {Main, Controls, Multiplayer, Creator, Journal} (`Menu.hpp:100`). A `Hit` is a `Rectangle` + int `id` (`Menu.hpp:103-106`). `layout()` (`Menu.cpp:111-180`) recomputes hit-rects from live `GetScreenWidth/Height()` each call so `render()` and `update()` always agree; `render()` re-calls `layout()` and draws each rect with hover highlight (`Menu.cpp:488-558`). Ids are namespaced by constant blocks (`Menu.cpp:13-38`).

The five pages:
- **Main** (title "Paused", `Menu.cpp:435`): six stacked 320×52 buttons — Resume, Controls, Multiplayer, Create Character, Journal, Quit (`Menu.cpp:116-123, 498-505`). Resume→game, Quit→close (`Menu.cpp:259-260`).
- **Controls**: one chip per action (`kActionCount`) at `w*0.5+90` (`Menu.cpp:171-176`); shows action label + current key; clicking a chip arms `awaiting_` and the next key press rebinds via `applyCapture` (`Menu.cpp:189-198, 338-356`). Instructional line "Click a key, then press the new key. Esc cancels." (`Menu.cpp:483-486`). Rebinds use swap semantics and save to disk immediately (`Menu.cpp:346-355`).
- **Multiplayer**: if a session is active, a Leave button; otherwise Host (fixed port 40605), a click-to-edit join-address field (default `127.0.0.1:40605`, cap 64 chars, Enter joins), and Join (`Menu.cpp:155-169, 225-243, 409-419`). Status line from an injected hook (`Menu.cpp:477-482`).
- **Creator** ("Create a Character"): left column three text fields — Name (required, cap 32), Backstory (cap 160), Traits (cap 160) (`Menu.cpp:130-137, 201-220, 507-518`). Right column: a `[<] label [>]` cycler per body-part category (Body/Head/Eyes/Hair), a Palette cycler, Randomize, and Save & Spawn (`Menu.cpp:140-154, 519-536`). This page dims the overlay less (90 vs 170) because main.cpp renders a live in-world character preview behind it (`Menu.cpp:432`, `Menu.hpp:78-83`). `attemptCreate` validates name and fires the injected `onCreate` hook (`Menu.cpp:388-407`).
- **Journal**: title "Journal"; renders read-only rows from an injected hook, grouped by subject header, 7 rows/page (`kJournalRowsPerPage`), with Prev/Next paging and Back (`Menu.cpp:124-129, 442-475`). Conflicting entries render in orange and are tagged `[conflicting accounts]` (`Menu.cpp:463-467`). Empty state: "You haven't been told anything yet." (`Menu.cpp:446`). This is the only place a player can re-read accumulated NPC-conveyed facts, and it is fact-store data, not conversation transcripts.

Toasts: transient status messages centered at `h*0.88` in yellow, `kToastSeconds = 3` (`Menu.cpp:57, 421-424, 560-562`).

### 6. Nameplates / who-am-I-talking-to feedback

- `drawNameplate()` draws name text at font size **14** with a 1px black shadow, centered on a projected world point (`main.cpp:151-158`).
- Every NPC within `kNameplateRange = 28` units gets a floating nameplate at feet+2.15y (`main.cpp:55-56, 1007-1031`). For local NPCs the plate also appends the current schedule activity: `name + " - " + activity` e.g. "Marge - baking bread" (`main.cpp:1025-1029`; activity from `Npc::activity()`, `Npc.hpp:88`).
- Remote players get cyan nameplates (`main.cpp:1032-1034`); combat callouts float higher in orange (`main.cpp:1036-1045`).
- In-conversation "who am I talking to" feedback: the seeded System line naming the NPC and role (`main.cpp:579-581`) plus every NPC line being prefixed with the speaker name in the transcript (`DialogUI.cpp:173`). There is **no dedicated header/portrait** in the dialog box naming the current partner — you rely on the transcript prefix and the seed line, which can scroll off.

### 7. Conversation affordances (end / who's nearby / re-read)

- **End a chat:** press Esc (`main.cpp:586-597`). It closes the session, ends streaming, returns to Playing, disables the cursor. On close (solo/host) it fires `requestSummary` + `requestFacts` for that NPC (`main.cpp:590-593`) — background LLM calls that update the NPC's persisted memory and extract journal facts; these produce no visible dialog (`main.cpp:853-865`). There is no on-screen "Leave" button in the dialog; Esc is the only exit, and it is only advertised in the seed line ("Esc leaves").
- **See who's nearby:** only the single nearest in-range NPC is surfaced, via the `[T] Talk to <name>` prompt (`main.cpp:1048-1052`) and nameplates (§6). No list of nearby NPCs.
- **Re-read what was said:** within an open chat, only the transcript lines that currently fit on screen are visible; there is no scrollback (§3). Across chats, the transcript is wiped on each new open (`main.cpp:576`). The Journal page (§5) is the only persistent re-readable record, and it holds extracted facts with attribution, not verbatim dialogue.

### The core type-a-message-and-read-a-reply loop (done hundreds of times)

Per message, the mechanical loop is: click/press T to open (mouse cursor toggles on) → type into a single-line box with no length limit and append-only editing (backspace only) → press Enter → input box locks and grays out → "<name> is thinking..." static gray text until first token → tokens stream into a gold line with an `_` cursor → line finalizes into the scrolling transcript → input re-enables. Each turn:
- The player is **rooted in place** the entire time — no movement, no doing anything else while the model thinks (`main.cpp:585-620`, movement gated to Playing at `535`).
- Only **one message can be in flight**; you cannot pre-type the next line (input disabled at `main.cpp:617`, re-enabled only at `928`).
- The "thinking" feedback is **static text, no animation/spinner** (`DialogUI.cpp:163-168`), and the dedicated `busy()`/`setThinking()` plumbing that exists is dead code (never called).
- Exit is **Esc only**, surfaced solely in an easily-scrolled-away seed line.
- There is **no scrollback** to re-read earlier turns mid-conversation, and the transcript is **discarded on every new conversation** (`main.cpp:576`).
- Cursor mode flips every open/close (`EnableCursor`/`DisableCursor` at `main.cpp:583, 597`), so each conversation entails a mouse-mode context switch.</result>

The input box is locked (`setInputEnabled(false)`) so you also cannot queue a next message while waiting.

- **Main** (title "Paused", `Menu.cpp:435`): six stacked 320×52 buttons — Resume, Controls, Multiplayer, Create Character, Journal, Quit (`Menu.cpp:116-123, 498-505`). Resume→game, Quit→close (`Menu.cpp:259-260`).

- **Creator** ("Create a Character"): left column three text fields — Name (required, cap 32), Backstory (cap 160), Traits (cap 160) (`Menu.cpp:130-137, 201-220, 507-518`). Right column: a `[<] label [>]` cycler per body-part category (Body/Head/Eyes/Hair), a Palette cycler, Randomize, and Save & Spawn (`Menu.cpp:140-154, 519-536`). This page dims the overlay less (90 vs 170) because main.cpp renders a live in-world character preview behind it (`Menu.cpp:432`, `Menu.hpp:78-83`). `attemptCreate` validates name and fires the injected `onCreate` hook (`Menu.cpp:388-407`).
- **Journal**: title "Journal"; renders read-only rows from an injected hook, grouped by subject header, 7 rows/page (`kJournalRowsPerPage`), with Prev/Next paging and Back (`Menu.cpp:124-129, 442-475`). Conflicting entries render in orange and are tagged `[conflicting accounts]` (`Menu.cpp:463-467`). Empty state: "You haven't been told anything yet." (`Menu.cpp:446`). This is the only place a player can re-read accumulated NPC-conveyed facts, and it is fact-store data, not conversation transcripts.

Toasts: transient status messages centered at `h*0.88` in yellow, `kToastSeconds = 3` (`Menu.cpp:57, 421-424, 560-562`).

- `drawNameplate()` draws name text at font size **14** with a 1px black shadow, centered on a projected world point (`main.cpp:151-158`).

For local NPCs the plate also appends the current schedule activity: `name + " - " + activity` e.g. "Marge - baking bread" (`main.cpp:1025-1029`; activity from `Npc::activity()`, `Npc.hpp:88`).

There is **no dedicated header/portrait** in the dialog box naming the current partner — you rely on the transcript prefix and the seed line, which can scroll off.

On close (solo/host) it fires `requestSummary` + `requestFacts` for that NPC (`main.cpp:590-593`) — background LLM calls that update the NPC's persisted memory and extract journal facts; these produce no visible dialog (`main.cpp:853-865`). There is no on-screen "Leave" button in the dialog; Esc is the only exit, and it is only advertised in the seed line ("Esc leaves").

Per message, the mechanical loop is: click/press T to open (mouse cursor toggles on) → type into a single-line box with no length limit and append-only editing (backspace only) → press Enter → input box locks and grays out → "<name> is thinking..." static gray text until first token → tokens stream into a gold line with an `_` cursor → line finalizes into the scrolling transcript → input re-enables. - The player is **rooted in place** the entire time — no movement, no doing anything else while the model thinks (`main.cpp:585-620`, movement gated to Playing at `535`).
- Only **one message can be in flight**; you cannot pre-type the next line (input disabled at `main.cpp:617`, re-enabled only at `928`).

# Pacing & Progression Audit — LLM-NPC Town Game

Everything below is what exists in the code RIGHT NOW. Citations are `file:line`.

## The headline finding

There is **no economy, no score, no XP, no quest, no objective, no win state, and no lose state anywhere in the codebase.** A repo-wide grep for `money|cash|coin|buy|sell|price|economy|currency|pay|purchase` returns **zero source hits**, and `score|xp|level|quest|objective|goal|win|lose|victory|reward|unlock|mission` returns **zero gameplay hits** (only unrelated substrings like `EINPROGRESS`, `underscore`, `loglevel`). The "## Goal" lines in `.claude/plans/*.md` are plan-doc section headers describing each feature's *purpose*, not player goals (e.g. `player-journal.md:14` "The player opens the journal, sees what they've been told").

---

## System-by-system inventory

### Economy / money — DOES NOT EXIST
No currency, wallet, prices, shops, or transactions of any kind. The "stores" (bakery, hardware, coffee) from `README.md:73-84` are set dressing with NPCs to talk to; nothing is buyable. There is nothing to earn and nothing to spend. No reason to accumulate anything because no accumulator exists.

### Weapons / combat — EXISTS, but stakes reset instantly
- Two weapons, pure static data: Fist (15 dmg) and Pistol (35 dmg, 12 ammo), `Weapon.hpp:27-32`.
- Player attacks on left-click: melee hits nearest NPC in range, pistol spawns a projectile — `World.cpp:12-43`, wired at `main.cpp:552-556`.
- Consequence for the NPC: `Npc::takeDamage` sends unarmed NPCs to `Fleeing`, armed ones (cops) to `Hostile`, and 0 HP to `Dead` — `Npc.cpp:221-230`. Hostile cops shoot back and can drop the player — `World.cpp:113-135`.
- **No stakes that persist.** Player death just opens a "Dead" screen; pressing Enter respawns at full HP at a fixed point `Vec3{0,0,24}`, and *every surviving NPC is reset to Idle* via `calmDown()` — `main.cpp:621-630`, `Npc.hpp:156-159`. A killed NPC stays dead only until… see "persistence" below (it does NOT persist).
- **Ammo is finite and never replenished.** The pistol starts with 12 (`Player.hpp:31-34`); there is no reload, pickup, or refill anywhere (grep for `reload|pickup|refill` finds nothing). Once spent, the pistol is permanently unusable for the session — `playerSwitchWeapon` even refuses to equip it at 0 ammo (`World.cpp:45-50`). This is a slow depletion, the opposite of progression.

### Law / police / jail — EXISTS, penalty is a 10-second timeout with zero memory
- Trigger: an NPC's LLM reply emits `[ACTION: arrest]` (police) or `[ACTION: call_police]` (civilians route the summons) — `NpcAction.hpp:46-55`, `Npc.cpp:68-100`. A civilian's `CallPolice` makes main order every police NPC to `commandArrest()` — `main.cpp:918-921`.
- A cop with `Arrest` behavior chases and "catches" the player within 1.6 units — `Npc.cpp:143-152`.
- Penalty: on catch, `jailSecondsLeft = kJailSeconds` (**10 seconds**, `main.cpp:61,694`), player is teleported beside the police station (`main.cpp:695-698`), movement and combat are frozen while jailed (`main.cpp:538,551`), and a HUD line counts down "Released in N" (`main.cpp:1054-1057`).
- **No long-term effect.** No criminal record, no fine, no wanted level, no escalation, nothing stored. After 10 s you walk free identical to before. The cop just `commandReturnHome()` (`main.cpp:699`).

### NPC memory — EXISTS and persists across sessions (the one real persistence)
- On leaving a conversation, the NPC's own model summarizes it; the summary is saved and injected into future prompts — `main.cpp:590-593,860`, plan `npc-memory-and-model.md`.
- Persisted to SQLite `saves/conversations.sqlite3`, one row per NPC (`ConversationStore.hpp:20-45`), loaded at startup and re-injected — `main.cpp:243-246`. So the baker genuinely remembers you next launch. This is real continuity — but it is *narrative* memory, not a *progression* mechanic: it unlocks no capability, tracks no number, gates nothing.

### Gossip / facts — EXISTS, spreads NPC-to-NPC, minimal player payoff
- On conversation close a second LLM call proposes 0–2 structured facts; validated all-or-nothing and committed to the shared `WorldState` bus — `Gossip.cpp:38-81`, `main.cpp:879-882`.
- Facts spread between NPCs who are physically near each other every 15 s, gated by proximity (≤6 units), age (>30 game-min) and a 35% roll — `Gossip.cpp:83-116`, tick at `main.cpp:667-686`.
- Persisted to `saves/facts.sqlite3` (`FactStore.hpp:11-38`), loaded at startup (`main.cpp:257-258`).
- **Player-facing payoff = essentially just the journal (below).** Gossip an NPC has heard is injected into that NPC's prompt (`Npc.hpp:139-141`, `main.cpp:269`), so NPCs may reference things — but nothing rewards the player for spreading or gathering facts; there's no objective tied to it.

### Journal — EXISTS, pure read-only viewer
- A pause-menu page listing facts the player was personally told (`knows("player",…)` AND `source != "player"`), grouped by subject, timestamped, flagging two facts with the same subject but different content as "conflicting accounts" — `Journal.hpp:25-49`.
- It "writes nothing, owns no data" (`player-journal.md:11-12`). It is an information display, not a quest log — no checkboxes, no tasks, no completion. Its own out-of-scope note explicitly excludes "quest hooks" — `player-journal.md:42-43`.

### World clock / schedules / day-night — EXISTS, purely cosmetic, no pressure/reward
- One shared clock: 1 real second = 1 game minute, a 24-real-minute day, starts 09:00 — `WorldState.hpp:57-60`. Advanced each frame at `main.cpp:648`.
- NPCs follow authored `.persona` schedules (walk to a spot, show an activity per time band) — `Schedule.hpp:13-33`, `Npc.cpp:174-190`. The activity is shown on the nameplate only (per `OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md:118-120`, "not yet injected into the LLM prompt").
- Day/night shifts sky/fog/light colors — `DayNight.hpp`, `main.cpp:934`.
- **Nothing is time-gated, timed, or rewarded.** No shop hours that matter, no curfew, no deadline, no event that fires at a given hour. Time changes only the scenery and where NPCs stand.
- **The clock does NOT persist** — `WorldState`'s constructor always resets to `kStartHour = 9.0` (`WorldState.cpp:11-13`); nothing saves `world_time_seconds` (FactStore never touches it). Every launch starts at 09:00. `OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md:116-118` confirms "Time doesn't persist across restarts."

### NPC behaviors — EXISTS, player influences them only transiently
- NPCs can Follow, Stop, Face, RaiseHand, Wave, Arrest, ReturnHome via LLM action tags — `NpcAction.hpp:14-24`, `Npc.cpp:111-197`. The player influences these by talking (e.g. "follow me").
- **No wandering, crowds, or moving traffic.** Grep for `wander|crowd|pedestrian|traffic` finds only static `trafficlight_*` props (`City.cpp:42-45`) — they are collision boxes, not vehicles. NPCs are otherwise stationary except when following a schedule or a conversation command.
- All player influence is transient: behaviors reset (arrest → ReturnHome, combat → calmDown on respawn). Nothing an NPC does under player influence is recorded.

---

## The four key questions

**(1) Any explicit goal, quest, objective, win/lose, or numeric progression?**
**None.** No quest/objective/score/XP/level system exists (repo-wide grep confirms). The only win/lose-adjacent state is the "Dead" screen (`main.cpp:621-630,1079-1081`) and the 10-second jail (`main.cpp:694`) — both fully self-reversing with no record kept. The only player-facing numbers are HP (`Player.hpp:16-17`) and pistol ammo (`Player.hpp:28`), and both only ever move *downward* toward a reset, never accumulate.

**(2) What can you do in minute 11 that you couldn't in minute 1?**
Mechanically, **nothing new.** No ability, weapon, area, or option unlocks over time. The only thing that changes is *fiction*: NPCs may now recall what you told them earlier (memory, `main.cpp:245-246`) and may repeat facts that have spread through town (gossip, `main.cpp:667-686`), and your journal may list a few more overheard facts (`Journal.hpp:25`). Your capabilities in minute 11 equal your capabilities in minute 1 — arguably reduced, since spent pistol ammo never comes back (`World.cpp:45-50`).

**(3) What persists across sessions vs resets?**

| Persists (SQLite in `saves/`) | Resets every launch |
|---|---|
| NPC conversation memory — `conversations.sqlite3`, `main.cpp:243-246` | Clock → always 09:00 — `WorldState.cpp:11-13` |
| Gossip facts + who-knows-what — `facts.sqlite3`, `main.cpp:257-258` | Player HP/ammo/position — `Player.hpp:16,31-34` |
| Player-created characters (persona + look) — `characters.sqlite3`, `main.cpp:222-224` | NPC deaths (Dead NPCs load alive; no death table) |
| | Arrest/jail state — no record stored |
| | Combat/behavior state — reset via `calmDown()` `main.cpp:627` |

**(4) Does anything the player does have lasting consequence in the world?**
**Only conversational/informational consequence, never structural.** Two things carry forward: (a) what you *say* to an NPC — it summarizes and remembers it (`main.cpp:860`, `ConversationStore`); (b) facts you introduce — they persist and can propagate to other NPCs (`Gossip.cpp:69-116`, `FactStore`). That's the extent of it. **Violence, arrest, death, money, and time leave no permanent mark**: killing an NPC is undone next launch (no death persistence), jail leaves no record, and there is no world state a player can permanently change, improve, deplete, or "beat." The world remembers your *words*, not your *deeds*.</result>
