- Deleting the rigged-model *loading* code in `Assets.cpp` (leave it dormant so
  remote players keep working and the path can be revived); only the **NPC
  dispatch** to it is retired.
- New part *categories* — still Body/Head/Eyes/Hair. Hair expansion is additive
  within the existing contract (as in #92).

## Affected Areas
- `src/app/main.cpp` — the NPC render loop (`~968-991`): populate `customLooks[i]`
  for **every** NPC so all render via `drawCompositeCharacter`; the
  `else drawCharacter(visual)` branch stops being reached for NPCs. Look source:
  the persona's authored look, else a deterministic fallback.
- `src/core/PersonaLoader.{hpp,cpp}` — parse an optional `look = body, head,
  eyes, hair, palette` header key into `LoadedPersona` (a placement/appearance
  concern, like `position` — additive, an unknown-key today would error, so it
  must be registered). Extend `renderPersonaText` to round-trip it.
- `src/core/Persona*` / a small helper — a deterministic
  `lookForPersona(name)` = author-supplied look if present, else
  `randomizeLook(hash(name))`, so all ten personas (and any future procedural
  NPC) get distinct, valid, style-consistent looks with zero manual gaps.
- `personas/*.persona` — add an authored `look = …` line to each of the ten
  (baker motherly, cop uniform/cap, busker casual, etc.), so looks are
  intentional, not just hashed. Police/armed personas get a uniform-reading look.
- `src/core/CharacterParts.cpp` — expand the Hair category with N new
  style-tagged parts (and any palettes that suit them), additive within the
  socket/size contract.
- `src/app/RaylibRenderer.cpp` — bespoke `drawCompositeCharacter` recipes for the
  new hair parts (or documented generic-box fallback), as in #92.
- Tests: `tests/test_character_parts.cpp` (exhaustive combo test auto-covers new
  hair; add reachability), new `tests/test_persona_look.cpp` (persona `look`
  parse + round-trip + deterministic fallback validity), and update
  `tests/test_persona_roster.cpp` if it asserts anything about NPC models.

## Implementation Order
1. **Record the audit finding in OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md** (the brief requires this
   before code): the two-systems finding above and the chosen direction.
2. **Persona `look` support** — add the optional `look` key to PersonaLoader +
   `LoadedPersona` + `renderPersonaText`, with a `lookForPersona(name)` helper
   (authored-or-deterministic). Unit-tested. *Independently committable.*
3. **Unify NPC rendering** — in main.cpp, assign every NPC a `CharacterLook` from
   step 2 and route all NPCs through `drawCompositeCharacter`; keep police/armed
   visually distinct. Rigged `drawCharacter` no longer dispatched for NPCs.
   *Independently committable.*
4. **Author the ten persona looks** — a distinct, in-character `look =` line per
   persona; verify variety ≥ the old five-model baseline. *Committable.*
5. **Expand hairstyles** — add the new style-tagged hair parts + recipes to the
   shared pool; both creator and NPCs pick them up. *Committable.*
6. **Visual QA** — side-by-side screenshot of a creator-built character next to
   roaming NPCs; confirm they read as one art source; attach the QA report to
   OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md. (Use the visual-qa subagent per the brief; if absent,
   the smoke-render + Read-PNG method used for #92.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md states the audit finding (two systems, chosen
      unification) before implementation.
- [ ] Every roaming NPC renders via `drawCompositeCharacter` from the shared
      `CharacterParts` pool — no NPC uses a rigged glTF model (verify: with the
      character models absent, NPCs still render as composites, not fallback
      markers).
- [ ] A `.persona` `look = body, head, eyes, hair, palette` line parses,
      round-trips through `renderPersonaText`, and drives that NPC's look; a
      persona with no `look` still gets a deterministic, valid, distinct look
      (`tests/test_persona_look.cpp`).
- [ ] All ten personas have distinct looks; police/armed read as uniformed;
      count of visually distinct NPC looks ≥ the previous five.
- [ ] The creator's part/palette pool is exactly the pool NPCs render from — the
      creator maintains no separate subset (same `partCatalog()`/`paletteCatalog()`).
- [ ] New hairstyles appear in both the creator picker and on NPCs; every
      style-compatible combination still assembles (`tests/test_character_parts.cpp`).
- [ ] `make -C tests test` green; game builds.
- [ ] Visual-QA side-by-side screenshot in OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md shows a
      creator-built character looking native beside roaming NPCs.

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Persona `look` names an unknown part/palette | Reject that look with a logged reason; fall back to the deterministic `lookForPersona(name)` so the NPC still spawns. |
| Persona has no `look` line | Deterministic `randomizeLook(hash(name))` — valid, style-consistent, stable across runs. |
| Two personas hash to similar looks | Authored `look` lines make the ten intentionally distinct; the hash fallback only covers unauthored/procedural NPCs. |
| Character models missing on disk | NPCs now render as composites regardless (composites are primitives, not loaded assets) — a strict improvement over today's marker-cylinder fallback. |
| Police/armed NPC | Authored uniform look (e.g. cap + cool/blue palette) so authority stays readable without the Knight model. |
| Remote players | Still rigged this version (out of scope); logged follow-up to give them composite looks too. |
| New hair part without a bespoke recipe | Generic declared-box fallback (documented in #92) — renders, never crashes. |

## Open Questions
- **Fidelity vs cohesion is a genuine product call.** This plan retires the
  rigged NPC models to satisfy the "one shared library / same assets" goal. If
  keeping the rigged art matters more, the off-ramp is the modular-pack
  alternative (XL) — flagged here so it can be redirected before implementation.
  Otherwise: none — plan is complete.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. **Persona `look` support + deterministic fallback** — optional `look` persona
   key parsed/round-tripped; `lookForPersona(name)` = authored-or-hashed. (Concept:
   *authored data with a deterministic derived fallback.*)
2. **Unify NPC rendering onto the shared composite parts library** — every NPC
   gets a CharacterLook and renders via `drawCompositeCharacter`; rigged models
   retired as the NPC source; police stays distinct. (Concept: *collapsing two
   render paths onto one shared asset library behind an existing dispatch hook.*)
3. **Author ten in-character persona looks** — a distinct look per townsperson,
   preserving/exceeding the old five-model variety. (Concept: *art-directing a
   cast within a constrained part system.*)
4. **Expand the shared hairstyle pool** — N new style-tagged hair parts + recipes,
   shared by creator and NPCs. (Concept: *additive style-tagged catalog growth in
   a single shared pool.*)

# Overnight Build Report
Date: 2026-07-08 (session 6 — shared character library, IN PROGRESS)

## Audit finding (recorded before implementation, per the brief)
"Expand hairstyles" and "created characters don't match roaming NPCs" share
one root cause, and it is **not** two pools of different sizes — it is **two
unrelated construction methods**:
- **NPCs are rigged glTF KayKit models** (`drawCharacter`; five fixed
  adventurers loaded in `Assets.cpp:170-172`, Knight doubling as police). The
  NPC render loop (`src/app/main.cpp:985-991`) only uses composites for
  entries in `customLooks` — i.e. player-created characters — and falls back
  to the rigged model for everyone else.
- **The creator is the only part-based system**: the socketed
  `CharacterParts` catalog rendered by `drawCompositeCharacter` from
  primitives. Rigged KayKit models physically cannot donate swappable
  heads/hair/bodies — which is why the composite system exists at all.

**Decision (logged):** make the composite `CharacterParts` catalog the single
shared library — every roaming NPC gets a composite look from the same pool
the creator picks from; the rigged path is retired as the *NPC* source (its
loading stays dormant for remote players). Trade-off accepted: rigged art
fidelity is exchanged for one-pool cohesion, per the brief's explicit
priority ("literally the same assets"). NPC variety baseline (five distinct
looks + police variant) is preserved by authoring a distinct look per persona
— the pool's combinatorics exceed the old range immediately.
Full plan + alternatives: `.claude/plans/shared-character-library.md`.

*(Session 6 results appended when the run completes.)*

## Verdict: PASS

I built no golden reference exists for this exact "shared library" scenario (it's a new feature, first render of its kind), so no pixel-diff was applicable — my read is a direct visual read of freshly captured frames using the game's own `--frames --camera --hour` smoke-test hook.

### Criterion 1 — one art source, no rigged mesh, no orange fallback cylinder
**PASS.** Every humanoid figure across all 9 shots is a flat-shaded primitive composite: a round/oval/block head atop a cone or block torso, with distinct hair/hat pieces bolted on. Close-ups of the cop (`qa_shot_cop.png`), musician (`qa_shot_musician.png`), baker (`qa_shot_baker2.png`), and taxi driver (`qa_shot_taxi.png`) all show this same construction. No textured/rigged KayKit-style mesh with articulated limbs appeared anywhere, and no plain orange marker cylinder appeared either — the orange/tan shapes present in several shots are the hot-dog cart prop (`City.cpp` "cart" bounding box, drawn as a box) and the first-person fist/weapon viewmodel (a fixed screen-relative shape present in every shot regardless of camera position — confirmed by pixel-diffing `qa_shot1.png` vs `qa_shot2.png`, which are shot from very different camera distances but show the same shape in the same relative screen position). Neither is a broken-look fallback.

### Criterion 2 — player character indistinguishable from townsfolk, correct spawn ring
**PASS.** `sqlite3 saves/characters.sqlite3` → table `character_persona`, row `custom_1783494792_10` ("doctor steve"), `position = 0, 8` → distance 8.0 from plaza center (0,0), satisfying the 8–17 ring (at the boundary). `qa_shot_wide2.png` frames this character together with the hot-dog vendor (Gus Romano, closest/red-orange torso) and the tourist (Yuki Tanaka, small mint bowl-cut figure near the cart) — all three built from identical primitive parts (round head + cone torso + flat color), confirmed via angle/distance math matching persona file coordinates. `qa_shot3.png` gives a tight close-up of the player character alone (plain oval head, green torso, no hair) next to the tourist's bowl-cut/mint styling, visually indistinguishable in construction style from any designer NPC.

### Criterion 3 — visible variety
**PASS.** Confirmed head-shape/hair/color variety directly on screen: cop = block head + black visor band + dark cap (slate uniform); musician = tall block head + dark mohawk-block + purple torso; baker = round head + brown hair bun + blue-gray dress; taxi driver = block head + mint side-swept hair block + wider "bulk" torso; player character = plain oval head, no hair, green torso; tourist = round head + mint bowl-cut. All persona files also carry explicit `look =` lines (10/10), and the run log confirmed "loaded 11 NPCs (1 player-created)" with zero persona/look errors.

### Screenshots (also left in place at repo root per the capture recipe)
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs/qa_shot_wide2.png` — **best side-by-side**: player character + hotdog vendor + tourist together in the plaza
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs/qa_shot3.png` — player character close-up next to tourist
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs/qa_shot_cop.png` — **best close-up**: cop construction (block head/visor/cap/slate)
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs/qa_shot_musician.png`, `qa_shot_baker2.png`, `qa_shot_taxi.png` — additional variety close-ups
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs/qa_shot1.png`, `qa_shot2.png` — initial wide plaza shots (used to isolate the viewmodel/cart-prop question)

"""Open ONE draft PR for the shared-character-library branch and close #95-98."""
import os, subprocess, re, time
from github import Github

token = os.environ.get("GH_TOKEN") or os.environ.get("TOKEN")
full = re.search(r"[:/]([^/]+/[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?$",
                 subprocess.check_output(["git", "remote", "get-url", "origin"], text=True).strip()).group(1)
repo = Github(token).get_repo(full)

def retry(fn, *a, **k):
    for i in range(5):
        try:
            return fn(*a, **k)
        except Exception as e:
            if i == 4: raise
            print(f"  transient ({type(e).__name__}), retry..."); time.sleep(3 + i * 2)

BODY = """## Summary
Milestone #11 — one shared character library. Roaming NPCs and
player-created characters were drawn by two unrelated systems (rigged
glTF KayKit models vs the composite `CharacterParts` socket catalog), so
a created character never looked native next to the townsfolk, and
hairstyles could only ever be added to the creator's pool. This branch
makes the composite catalog the single shared library. One atomic commit
per issue:

**#95 feat(persona): optional authored look with deterministic
fallback.** A `.persona` file may carry `look = body, head, eyes, hair,
palette`; `lookForPersona` returns it when valid, else a deterministic
`randomizeLook(FNV-1a(name))` — every persona always spawns with a valid
look from the one shared catalog, and a stale part id demotes to the
fallback (logged) instead of killing the file. `commit ee7c07e`

**#96 feat(npc): render every NPC from the shared composite parts
library.** All NPCs now route through `drawCompositeCharacter` (which
gains defaulted face/dead params: same emote billboards, tip-over death
pose). The rigged models are retired as the NPC source — loading stays
dormant for remote players and unknown net indices. `commit fc336b6`

**#97 feat(parts): expand the shared hairstyle pool.** Six new
style-tagged hair parts (cap, buzz, bob, curls, bun, side-sweep) with
bespoke recipes — hair 6 → 12, picked up by the creator picker AND every
NPC with zero further wiring. `commit 119db76`

**#98 feat(personas): author ten distinct in-character looks.** Marge's
bun, Officer Brooks' cap + visor + slate uniform, Benny's mohawk, Yuki's
bowl cut… all pairwise-distinct, style-valid, asserted by the roster
test. NPC variety now exceeds the old five-rigged-model baseline.
`commit 53584f3`

## Verification
- `make -C tests test` green: **173 cases / 3323 assertions** (new
  `test_persona_look.cpp`; the exhaustive part-combination test absorbed
  the six new hair parts, 2343 → 3323; roster test asserts authored,
  valid, pairwise-distinct looks).
- **Visual-QA subagent PASS** on a side-by-side gate: every humanoid in 9
  screenshots is a composite (no rigged mesh, no fallback cylinder); the
  stored player-created character framed beside the hot-dog vendor and
  tourist is indistinguishable in construction; cop reads as uniformed
  authority. Shots in `docs/qa/screenshots/shared-character-library/`
  (local, uncommitted).

## Trade-off (deliberate, logged)
This retires the five rigged, skeletally-animated KayKit adventurers as
the NPC look in exchange for one-pool cohesion + shared hairstyles (the
brief's stated priority). Composites keep the procedural walk bob, mood
emotes, and gain a death pose; gestures drive the bob. The off-ramp, if
rigged fidelity is wanted later, is a modular CC0 pack rebuild (XL),
documented in `.claude/plans/shared-character-library.md`.

## Needs human verification
- In-game feel of the composite townsfolk (walk bob, emotes, death pose)
  — screenshots confirm statics, not motion.
- Creator flow end-to-end: build a character with the new hair, Save &
  Spawn, confirm it stands naturally among NPCs.

## Notes
- Stacked on `feature/aim-styles-preview` (PR #94). Merge order:
  player-journal → aim-styles-preview → this. Do not merge; review only.
- Follow-up logged: remote *players* still render as rigged meshes
  (multiplayer edge, out of scope here).

Co-authored with Claude Opus 4.8.
"""

pr = retry(repo.create_pull,
           title="feat: one shared character library — NPCs and creator draw from the same parts pool (#95-#98)",
           body=BODY, base="feature/aim-styles-preview",
           head="feature/shared-character-library", draft=True)
print(f"DRAFT PR #{pr.number}: {pr.html_url}")

for n in (95, 96, 97, 98):
    issue = retry(repo.get_issue, n)
    labels = [l.name for l in issue.labels if l.name not in ("ready-for-ai", "ai-in-progress")]
    if "ai-completed" not in labels:
        labels.append("ai-completed")
    retry(issue.edit, labels=labels)
    retry(issue.create_comment,
          f"Implemented on `feature/shared-character-library`. Draft PR #{pr.number} open for review (stacked on feature/aim-styles-preview). Not merged.")
    retry(issue.edit, state="closed")
    print(f"  #{n}: labels={labels}, closed, linked to PR #{pr.number}")

print("done")

Lesson 0024 · Systems design · from PR #99 (#95–#98)

One Shared Asset Pool: Collapsing Two Pipelines

"Created characters don't look like the townsfolk" and "add more hairstyles" arrived as two requests. The audit showed one root cause: NPCs and the creator rendered from two unrelated construction methods — rigged glTF pack models vs primitive composites — that shared nothing. No amount of tuning either pool fixes that; the fix is choosing ONE pool and routing everything through it.

Diagnose before adding assets

The tempting move was to add hairstyles to the creator's catalog and call it done. But hair added there could never appear on a roaming NPC — rigged models can't wear composite parts. When two features share a root cause, fixing the structure once beats patching each symptom: after unification, "expand hairstyles" became six data rows that both consumers picked up with zero wiring.

The dispatch hook was already there

The render loop already chose per-NPC:

if (customLooks.count(i))  drawCompositeCharacter(...)  // created chars
else                       drawCharacter(visual);        // rigged pack model

Unification = widening the existing branch until the else disappears: give every NPC a look (npcLooks[i]) and the second path is never dispatched. No new render system — the hook one feature built became the seam the next feature widened.

Authored data with a derived fallback

Ten townsfolk deserve art direction; future procedural NPCs can't require it. The rule that serves both, in one function:

CharacterLook lookForPersona(name, authored, whyFallback) {
    if (authored && lookIsValid(*authored)) return *authored;   // art-directed
    ...
    return randomizeLook(fnv1a(name));   // deterministic: same name, same face
}
  • Authored wins when valid — the cast is intentional (the cop's cap + visor + slate reads as uniform without the Knight model).
  • Fallback is derived, not random: hashing the name means an unauthored NPC keeps the same face across runs — no save data needed.
  • Stale data demotes, never kills: a look naming a removed part logs why and falls back; the NPC always spawns.

Validation lives with the catalog, not the parser

PersonaLoader checks only structure (five items); whether ids exist is checked by lookForPersona at spawn. So the persona format doesn't depend on the parts catalog, and editing the catalog can't retroactively invalidate persona files — worst case a look falls back at runtime, loudly.

The trade-off was priced, not hidden

Unifying retired five rigged, skeletally-animated models in favor of primitive composites: real fidelity lost, bought cohesion + customization + shared hair. The render loop already chose per-NPC:

else                       drawCharacter(visual);        // rigged pack model

Unification = widening the existing branch until the else disappears: give every NPC a look (npcLooks[i]) and the second path is never dispatched. No new render system — the hook one feature built became the seam the next feature widened.

CharacterLook lookForPersona(name, authored, whyFallback) {
    if (authored && lookIsValid(*authored)) return *authored;   // art-directed
    ...

Everything's done. Here's the full picture:

## Shared character library — shipped (PR #99)
The root cause was confirmed as **two unrelated pipelines** (rigged glTF NPCs vs composite creator parts), so per your brief I unified rather than adding assets to the wrong pool:
- **#95** — personas can carry an authored `look = body, head, eyes, hair, palette` line; anyone without one gets a deterministic per-name fallback from the same pool (stale looks demote with a logged reason, never kill the NPC).
- **#96** — every NPC now renders from the composite pool; rigged models retired as the NPC source (kept dormant for remote players). Mood emotes preserved, death pose added.
- **#97** — hair pool 6 → 12 (cap, buzz, bob, curls, bun, side-sweep) — shared by creator and NPCs automatically.
- **#98** — all ten townsfolk art-directed (cop = cap + visor + slate uniform; Marge's bun; Benny's mohawk…), pairwise-distinct, enforced by the roster test.
- **Visual-qa subagent: PASS** on the side-by-side gate — the stored created character is indistinguishable in construction from the townsfolk (report + screenshots in OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md / `docs/qa/screenshots/`). One reorder logged: hair landed before looks so the cop could wear the cap.

## Your two live requests — shipped (PR #100)
- **Fist/gun**: the viewmodel was drawn as world-axis-aligned cubes — that's the "floating block". It now draws in camera-local space, so it pivots with your view. The **fist is invisible at rest** and on click a sleeved arm **shoots out and retracts** — a punch. The pistol is a held silhouette (slide, barrel, grip, hand) with a recoil kick.
- **Curbs/jumping**: collision now cares about height — props only block while their top is above your feet — and **Space jumps** (~1.45u apex: over benches and bushes, onto car roofs; walls stay walls). You can also stand on tops and fall off edges. Jump is rebindable in the controls menu.

**State**: suite green (176 cases / 3337 assertions), stacked draft chain #94 → #99 → #100, nothing merged, main untouched. The feel of the punch, recoil, and jump arc are tuned by constants (`kGravity 22`, `kJumpSpeed 8`) — play it and tell me if the jump feels floaty or the punch too slow, and I'll tune.

<command-message>idea</command-message>
<command-name>/idea</command-name>
<command-args>Goal: Substantially improve the game's overall visual style toward a cartoony,
Mii/Tomodachi-Life-inspired look, expand character customization variety, add
playable-character (not just NPC) look customization, and have Claude actively
playtest the result to surface further improvement ideas.

Context: This builds on existing systems already in place — the size-contract
(entity world size independent of sprite pixel dimensions) and the socket/
attach-point system for compositional character parts. The art style overhaul
and expanded customization should be built as extensions of these systems,
not parallel ones.

Scope:

PART A — Engine assessment (recommendation only, do not execute)
- Assess whether the current rendering/engine setup can reasonably support a
  cohesive cartoony, Mii-style visual target, or whether it's a genuine
  blocker.
- If a migration looks warranted: do NOT start migrating. Instead produce a
  written recommendation with reasoning, and a migration plan document
  (scope, risk, rough sequencing) saved to .claude/plans/, for me to review
  and decide on manually. This is a hard stop — a full engine migration is
  too large and risky to execute unattended overnight.
- If no migration is needed: state that plainly and move to Part B.

PART B — Art style overhaul (proceed regardless of Part A's outcome, scoped
to what's achievable within the current engine)
- Move the visual direction toward cartoony/Mii-style: simplified,
  friendly proportions, clean bold outlines, a cohesive color palette —
  reference Tomodachi Life and Mii-style character design as the concrete
  target, not vague "cuter" language.
- Apply consistently across roaming NPCs, the character creator's parts
  pool, and the player's own avatar — all three must draw from the same
  shared parts library (per the earlier pool-unification fix), so this
  doesn't reintroduce a mismatch between them.
- Leave a clear seam for swapping in purchased/downloaded graphics packs
  later — style should be a tagged property on parts, not hardcoded
  assumptions baked into rendering logic.

PART C — Expand character customization
- Meaningfully increase style variety (hairstyles, faces, body types,
  clothing/palettes) within the shared parts pool from Part B, each
  conforming to the existing socket/size contracts.
- Add playable-character customization — currently this exists for NPCs the
  player creates; the player's own avatar needs the same look-modification
  capability, sharing the same parts pool and creator UI patterns already
  built, not a separate system.

PART D — Self-directed playtesting and improvement discovery
- Using the visual-qa subagent, actually launch and look at the game after
  A/B/C are implemented — the character creator, a roaming NPC, and the
  player avatar side by side — and confirm they're visually consistent.
- Beyond just verifying this ticket's own changes, spend some time actually
  playing/exploring the game as a player would, and note other concrete
  visual or game-feel improvements you notice — not a full design audit,
  just what surfaces naturally while testing this work. Save these as a
  short findings list in OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md for me to review, don't act on
  them beyond this ticket.

Autonomy instructions for tonight's run — this runs unattended, so:
- Do not stop to ask me clarifying questions, including any /grill-me-style
  interrogation step, anywhere in Parts B, C, or D. Pick the most defensible
  option yourself, log the decision and reasoning in OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md,
  and keep going.
- Part A is the one exception: if a migration is warranted, STOP at the
  recommendation/plan document for that specific decision — do not proceed
  to execute it, even partially, even as a "quick prototype."
- Prefer changes that fit the existing size-contract/socket systems over
  anything that would require rebuilding them, even if the alternative
  looks more visually ambitious tonight.
- Follow existing CLAUDE.md agent routing.
- Draft tickets, implement, test, open a draft PR as usual for Parts B/C.
  Do not merge, do not touch main.
- docs/learning/, OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md, .claude/memory/ stay gitignored.</command-args>

You are turning "Substantially" into a structured, actionable plan document.

This command has two phases:
- PHASE 1: Interrogate the idea until it is unambiguous
- PHASE 2: Produce the plan document

Do not skip to Phase 2 until Phase 1 is complete.

---

## PHASE 1 — INTERROGATE THE IDEA

Read the codebase first so your questions are grounded in reality:
```bash
find src/ lib/ app/ -type f 2>/dev/null | head -30
git log --oneline -10
cat CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null || true
```

Then ask clarifying questions — ONE at a time, wait for the answer,
then ask the next. Do not dump a list of questions all at once.
A question only gets asked if you genuinely cannot write a good plan
without knowing the answer.

Things worth asking about (pick the most important ones):

**Scope:**
- What does done look like? What can a user DO when this is complete?
- What is explicitly OUT of scope for this version?
- Is this a new feature, a change to existing behaviour, or a fix?

**Users and context:**
- Who uses this and in what situation?
- What do they have / know before they reach this feature?

**Technical constraints:**
- Does this touch existing code that other things depend on?
- Any performance, security, or compatibility requirements?
- Any third-party APIs or libraries involved?

**Edge cases:**
- What happens when the input is invalid or missing?
- What's the failure mode and how should it be handled?

**Priority:**
- Does this need to be done in a specific order relative to other work?
- Is there a simpler version that delivers most of the value?

Stop asking when you have enough to write a plan that could be handed
to a developer (or the overnight session) without them needing to ask
you anything.

---

## PHASE 2 — PRODUCE THE PLAN DOCUMENT

Save to `.claude/plans/[slug].md` where slug is a short dash-case
name derived from the idea. Example: "add weapon inventory" →
`.claude/plans/weapon-inventory.md`

The document structure:

```markdown
# Plan: [Feature Name]
Date: [date]
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: S / M / L / XL

## The Idea (one paragraph)
[What this is, in plain language. Someone unfamiliar with the codebase
should understand this in 30 seconds.]

## Goal
[One sentence: what a user can DO when this is shipped that they
cannot do now.]

## Out of Scope (this version)
[Explicit list of things NOT included. This prevents scope creep
during implementation.]

## Affected Areas
[Files, modules, or systems this touches. Be specific.]
- `src/path/to/file.py` — [why it changes]
- `src/path/to/other.cpp` — [why it changes]
- New files needed: [list]

## Implementation Order
[Ordered steps. Each step should be independently committable.]

1. [Step 1 — what it produces]
2. [Step 2 — builds on step 1]
3. [Step 3 — etc.]

## Acceptance Criteria
[Testable conditions that define "done". Each one should be
verifiable by running a test or observing a specific behaviour.]

- [ ] [Given X, when Y, then Z]
- [ ] [Given X, when Y, then Z]
- [ ] Tests pass: [specific test file or command]

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
[What can go wrong and how each case is handled.]

| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| [case] | [what happens] |

## Open Questions
[Anything still unresolved that will need a decision during implementation.
If there are none, write "None — plan is complete."]

## Suggested GitHub Issues
[If this plan should become overnight issues, list them here as a
starting point for /plan-github:]

1. [Issue title] — [one line scope]
2. [Issue title] — [one line scope]
3. [Issue title] — [one line scope]
```

---

## AFTER SAVING THE PLAN

Tell the user:
1. Where the plan was saved
2. How to turn it into GitHub issues:
   `/plan-github "[feature name]"` — or offer to run it now
3. How to start implementation immediately:
   `/develop [feature name]` — uses the plan as the spec
4. How to queue it for overnight:
   Add the suggested issues to GitHub, label ready-for-ai,
   then `bash ~/scripts/nightly.sh`

---

## TONE

Ask questions like a sharp senior engineer reviewing a spec —
direct, specific, not adversarial. The goal is to surface
assumptions before they become bugs, not to gatekeep.

If the idea is already clear enough to plan without questions,
say so briefly and go straight to the plan.

```bash

ls .claude/plans/
```

# Mii-Style Rendering & Content-Pack Conventions

Read this before implementing any mii-style-visual-overhaul issue so every
step makes the same choices. Plan: `.claude/plans/mii-style-visual-overhaul.md`.

## The three invariants

1. **One shared pool.** NPCs, the creator, and the player avatar all draw
   from `partCatalog()`/`paletteCatalog()` via `drawCompositeCharacter`.
   Never add a parts source or a renderer variant for one consumer — that
   reintroduces the pool-separation bug PR #99 removed.
2. **Style is data.** Proportions = `localSize`/sockets on catalog rows.
   Colors = palette rows. Pack membership = the `pack` tag. If a change
   requires editing assembly code (`assembleLook`) or picker logic to look
   different, the design is wrong — stop and re-read the plan.
3. **Contracts hold.** Sockets resolve unscaled, ONE uniform scale to the
   1.8u height contract afterward; style tags (round/blocky/any) gate every
   combination; `hair_none`-style explicit zero-size parts instead of
   missing slots.

## Graphics-pack seam (step 1)

A pack is: catalog rows (`pack: "tag"`) + palettes (`pack: "tag"`) +
renderer recipes for its part ids. Nothing else. The recipe dispatch in
`RaylibRenderer.cpp` must be a single function with signature roughly
`drawPartRecipe(const PartDef&, Vec3 at, Vec3 dim, const Colors&)` so a
future pack extends one dispatch site. The generic declared-box fallback
stays the safety net for any part without a bespoke recipe.

## Inverted-hull outlines (step 3)

- Re-issue the same part draws FIRST, scaled ~1.05 about each part's
  center, in near-black (`{30, 30, 36}` family), with
  `rlSetCullFace(RL_CULL_FACE_FRONT)`; restore `RL_CULL_FACE_BACK` after.
- `rlgl` state calls flush the batch — group the outline pass, then the
  color pass, not interleaved per part.
- Boxes are the known risk (corner gaps). Escalation order: bump hull
  scale → per-recipe outline opt-out flag → (logged, last resort) skip
  outlines on box parts only. Never abandon outlines globally without a
  screenshot comparison in OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md.
- Screenshot-verify on BOTH a sphere-family and box-family character.

## Mii proportion targets (step 2)

Head ≈ 40–45% of standing height (Tomodachi reference). Bodies shorten to
~0.75–0.85u, heads grow to ~0.95–1.05u, sockets re-authored per part.
Yardstick: the cop close-up shot from PR #99
(`docs/qa/screenshots/shared-character-library/qa_shot_cop.png`) is the
"before"; the "after" head should read roughly twice as dominant.

## Mouth category + look format (step 4)

Land as ONE commit: enum + count bump, CategorySpec row (`Mouth`→`Head`
via `"mouth"`), `mouth` sockets on all heads, ≥4 mouth parts + recipes,
Menu `categoryLabel` case. Look format: `look = body, head, eyes, hair,
mouth, palette` (six items); the five-item form MUST keep parsing (mouth
via the deterministic fallback) so shipped persona files and stored looks
never break. `renderPersonaText` always emits six.

## Player avatar (step 6)

Reserved id `player_avatar` in the existing CharacterStore look table — no
new storage. The creator page runs in "avatar mode" (same picker/Randomize/
preview; Save writes the avatar row instead of spawning). First-person
visibility: tint the punch sleeve/fist and pistol hand from the avatar's
palette in `drawViewmodel`. Remote-player replication is OUT of scope
(logged seam; guests still see rigged meshes).

## Verification recipe

`caffeinate -u -t 3` then
`./build/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs --frames 90 shot.png --camera <x> <z> <yaw> --hour 12`
— the PNG lands in CWD regardless of path given. Read the PNG. Suite:
`make -C tests test` (un-skip the matching stub in `tests/test_style_pack.cpp`
in the same commit as each step).

Read .claude/skills/github/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/code-economy/SKILL.md
before doing anything. The GitHub skill covers auth and issue creation.
The code-economy skill defines what makes a good, reviewable change.

---

You are a backlog planning agent for a personal GitHub project.
Your job is to read the current project state and create well-formed
GitHub issues that the overnight session can work through autonomously.

Every issue you create must be:
- Self-contained (completable in one overnight session)
- Specific (clear acceptance criteria, not vague goals)
- Verifiable (a test to run or output to check)
- Code-economy compliant (won't produce bloated PRs)
- Labelled ready-for-ai and assigned to the repo owner

---

## STEP 1 — PREREQUISITES

```python
import os
from github import Github

# Verify auth
token = os.environ.get("GH_TOKEN")
username = os.environ.get("GITHUB_USERNAME")
if not token or not username:
    raise SystemExit(
        "Set GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_USERNAME in your shell config first."
    )

gh = Github(token)
repo = get_repo(gh)   # auto-detects from git remote
print(f"Planning issues for: {repo.full_name}")

# Read existing open issues to avoid duplicates
existing = list_issues(repo, state="open")
existing_titles = {i["title"].lower() for i in existing}
print(f"Existing open issues: {len(existing)}")
```

---

## STEP 2 — READ PROJECT CONTEXT

Read all of these before planning any issues:

**CLAUDE.md** — the project purpose, stack, rules, and current state.
This is the source of truth for what the project is trying to be.

**README.md** — user-facing description and roadmap if any.

**Current codebase:**
```bash
# What exists right now
find src/ lib/ app/ -type f 2>/dev/null | head -50 || \
  find . -name "*.py" -o -name "*.cpp" -o -name "*.ts" \
  | grep -v node_modules | grep -v build | head -50

# Where work is heading
git log --oneline -20

# Known gaps and TODOs
grep -rn "TODO\|FIXME\|HACK\|NotImplemented\|raise NotImplementedError" \
  src/ lib/ app/ 2>/dev/null | head -30

# Test coverage gaps (uncovered files)
pytest --co -q 2>/dev/null | head -30 || true
```

---

## STEP 3 — CREATE MILESTONE (GITHUB EQUIVALENT OF EPIC)

Group related issues under a milestone:

```python
def create_milestone(repo, title: str, description: str) -> int:
    """Create a GitHub milestone. Returns the milestone number."""
    milestone = repo.create_milestone(
        title=title,
        description=description
    )
    print(f"Created milestone: {milestone.title} (#{milestone.number})")
    return milestone.number
```

Create one milestone per theme of work. For "to" focus, one milestone
is enough. For full project analysis, create 2-4 milestones.

Good milestone names:
- "SCPI Device Family — Oscilloscopes"
- "NPC Tier 1: Structured Output"
- "Data Pipeline — Market Data Ingestion"

---

## STEP 4 — CREATE ISSUES

For each issue, use this exact body template so the overnight session
has everything it needs:

```python
ISSUE_TEMPLATE = """## What to change
{what}

## Where it is
{where}

## How to verify it's done
{verify}

## Constraints
{constraints}

## Code economy note
{economy_note}

## Branch name
`feature/issue-{{number}}-{slug}`

## Concept for learning materials
{concept}
"""
```

The **concept** field is critical — it tells the overnight session what
to teach/drill after completing this issue. It must be:
- A technical concept, not a feature name
- Specific enough to produce a useful lesson
- Different from concepts already in docs/learning/PROGRESS.md

```python
def plan_and_create_issues(repo, milestone_number: int,
                           specs: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Create a batch of issues. Each spec is a dict with keys:
        title, what, where, verify, constraints, economy_note,
        slug, concept

    Returns list of created issue dicts with number and URL.
    """
    username = os.environ["GITHUB_USERNAME"]
    created = []

    # Ensure overnight labels exist
    create_overnight_labels(repo)

    milestone = repo.get_milestone(milestone_number)

    for spec in specs:
        # Skip if similar issue already exists
        if spec["title"].lower() in existing_titles:
            print(f"Skipping (exists): {spec['title']}")
            continue

        body = ISSUE_TEMPLATE.format(
            what=spec["what"],
            where=spec["where"],
            verify=spec["verify"],
            constraints=spec["constraints"],
            economy_note=spec["economy_note"],
            slug=spec["slug"],
            concept=spec["concept"],
            number="N"    # placeholder — updated after creation
        )

        issue = repo.create_issue(
            title=spec["title"],
            body=body,
            labels=["ready-for-ai"],
            assignees=[username],
            milestone=milestone
        )

        # Update branch name now that we have the number
        updated_body = body.replace(
            "feature/issue/N",
            f"feature/issue-{issue.number}"
        )
        issue.edit(body=updated_body)

        print(f"  Created #{issue.number}: {spec['title']}")
        print(f"  Concept: {spec['concept']}")
        created.append({
            "number":  issue.number,
            "title":   spec["title"],
            "concept": spec["concept"],
            "url":     issue.html_url
        })

    return created
```

---

## STEP 5 — ECONOMY NOTE GUIDANCE

Every issue should include an `economy_note` that pre-constrains the
implementation. This prevents the overnight session from over-building.

Good economy notes:
```
Use stdlib re for command pattern matching — no regex library needed.
Follow the existing BaseDevice pattern exactly — no new abstractions.
One new file maximum: src/devices/psu_e3631a.py plus its test file.
```

Bad economy notes (too vague):
```
Keep it simple.
Don't over-engineer.
```

The note should name the specific stdlib/pattern to use, or the

You are running an overnight autonomous development session on this
repository. Use the overnight-coordinator agent to manage the full session.
You have full permission to read, write, commit, push, and open draft PRs.
You do NOT have permission to merge to main or close PRs after opening them.

## SETUP (run once at session start)

```bash
# 1. Ensure we are on main and up to date
git checkout main
git pull

# 2. Rebuild the knowledge graph so you navigate current code, not stale code
# (only if graphify is installed — skip silently if not)
graphify update . --force 2>/dev/null || echo "graphify not installed — skipping"

# 3. Check for a prior checkpoint (resume if interrupted)
cat .claude/memory/checkpoint.md 2>/dev/null || echo "No checkpoint — starting fresh"

# 4. Read tonight's issues
gh issue list --label "ready-for-ai" --json number,title,body,labels \
  --order created --limit 20
```

If a checkpoint exists and shows IN PROGRESS or FAILED stages, resume
from there rather than starting over.

Write the session start to .claude/memory/checkpoint.md:
```
# Checkpoint
Session started: [timestamp]
Goal: Work through all ready-for-ai issues
Status: IN PROGRESS
Issues to process: [list from gh output]
Issues completed: []
Issues failed: []
Issues skipped: []
```

---

## FOR EACH ISSUE (in number order, lowest first)

### A. READ AND ASSESS

```bash
gh issue view [N] --comments
```

Ask: Is this issue clear enough to attempt autonomously?

**Blockers that cause a SKIP:**
- Requires a design decision not documented in the issue
- Depends on another issue that isn't complete yet
- Requires credentials, API keys, or external resources not available
- Scope is too vague to produce a verifiable result

If blocked, label and move on — do NOT guess at intent:
```bash
gh issue edit [N] --add-label "needs-human" --remove-label "ready-for-ai"
gh issue comment [N] --body "Skipped overnight: [specific reason]. Please clarify before re-queuing."
```

### B. ORIENT

Invoke the git-historian agent:
"Use the git-historian agent to understand the code area this issue will touch."

This surfaces hot files, recent decisions, and things NOT to redo.
Read .claude/memory/history-brief.md after it completes.

### C. MARK IN PROGRESS

```bash
gh issue edit [N] --add-label "ai-in-progress" --remove-label "ready-for-ai"
gh issue comment [N] --body "Starting overnight implementation. Planning now."
```

### D. BRANCH

```bash
git checkout main
git checkout -b feature/issue-[N]
```

### E. PLAN

Use /plan-feature [concept from issue title] and wait for a plan.
Save the plan to .claude/plans/issue-[N].md

Do not implement until you have a written plan.

### F. IMPLEMENT

Use the appropriate specialist agents for this repo (see repo-specific
section below). Follow the plan. Write complete code — no placeholders.

If you hit a problem after 2 attempts on the same sticking point, SKIP
the issue and mark it ai-blocked. Do not spiral.

### G. TEST

Run the project's test suite. The exact commands are in the repo-specific
section below. Tests MUST pass before committing.

If tests fail after 2 fix attempts: skip, mark blocked, move on.
```bash
gh issue edit [N] --remove-label "ai-in-progress" --add-label "ai-blocked"
gh issue comment [N] --body "Blocked: tests failing after 2 attempts. [describe failure]. Needs human attention."
git checkout main
git branch -D feature/issue-[N]
```

### H. COMMIT AND PUSH

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "fix(#[N]): [issue title, shortened]"
git push origin feature/issue-[N]
```

### I. OPEN DRAFT PR

Generate the PR description using the /mr-description command, then:

```bash
gh pr create \
  --title "fix(#[N]): [issue title]" \
  --body "[output from /mr-description]" \
  --base main \
  --head feature/issue-[N] \
  --draft
```

Label the issue complete and close it with a reference to the PR:
```bash
gh issue edit [N] \
  --remove-label "ai-in-progress" \
  --add-label "ai-completed"
gh issue close [N] \
  --comment "Implemented. Draft PR open for review — see above."
```

### J. GENERATE LEARNING MATERIALS

**Identify the primary concept:**
Ask yourself: "What is the single most important technical concept a
developer would need to understand to maintain or extend this change?"

Guidelines:
- Choose the concept, not the feature name
  ("triple-channel SCPI addressing" not "E3631A support")
- Should be teachable in one lesson
- Should have testable recall in a drill
- Should introduce vocabulary worth learning

Then generate all three artifacts. In overnight/automated context:
- Generate the HTML files fully
- Skip in-chat interactive knowledge checks (no user present)
- Make the HTML content thorough — it is the only output
- Update PROGRESS.md with what was covered

```
/teach [concept]
```
This creates docs/learning/lessons/NNNN-[concept].html

```
/drill-me [concept]
```
This creates docs/learning/drills/NNNN-[concept].html

```
/terms [concept]
```
This creates docs/learning/vocab/NNNN-[concept].html
and updates docs/learning/GLOSSARY.md

Commit the learning materials on the same feature branch:
```bash
git add docs/learning/
git commit -m "docs(learning): add lesson, drill and vocab for [concept] (from issue #[N])"
git push origin feature/issue-[N]
```

### K. UPDATE CHECKPOINT

Append to .claude/memory/checkpoint.md:
```
Issue #[N]: [COMPLETED | FAILED | SKIPPED]
  Branch: feature/issue-[N]
  PR: #[PR number if opened]
  Concept taught: [concept]
  Learning files: lessons/NNNN-x.html, drills/NNNN-x.html, vocab/NNNN-x.html
  Notes: [anything notable]
```

Return to main: `git checkout main`

---

## END OF ALL ISSUES

### 1. Rebuild the learning index

```
/index
```

Commit:
```bash
git add docs/learning/index.html
git commit -m "docs(learning): rebuild index after overnight run $(date +%Y-%m-%d)"
git push origin main
```

### 2. Write the morning report

Write OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md to the repo root:

```markdown
# Overnight Build Report
Date: [date]
Session duration: [start] to [finish]
Issues attempted: [N]

## Summary
[2-3 sentences on what was accomplished overall]

## Completed ✅
| Issue | Title | Branch | PR | Concept Taught |
|-------|-------|--------|----|----------------|
| #N | [title] | feature/issue-N | #PR | [concept] |

## Failed ❌
| Issue | Title | Failure Reason |
|-------|-------|----------------|
| #N | [title] | [why — specific, actionable] |

## Skipped (needs human) ⏭
| Issue | Title | Reason |
|-------|-------|--------|
| #N | [title] | [what needs clarification] |

## Learning Materials Created
| Concept | Lesson | Drill | Vocab |
|---------|--------|-------|-------|
| [concept] | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

## Test Status
[overall pass/fail and any notable failures]

## Suggested First Move
[The single most useful thing to do when you open your laptop]

## Draft PRs Awaiting Review
[list with PR numbers and one-line description each]
```

Commit and push the report:
```bash
git add OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md .claude/memory/checkpoint.md
git commit -m "chore: overnight report $(date +%Y-%m-%d)"
git push origin main
```

---

## LEARNING CONCEPT SELECTION — GENERAL GUIDANCE

These guidelines apply to all repos unless overridden in a repo-specific
overnight-session command.

Choose a concept that:
- Is non-obvious (skip things any developer already knows)
- Will appear again in this codebase (worth learning for maintainability)
- Can be explained in one lesson without splitting into prerequisite lessons
- Has clear vocabulary (terms worth adding to the glossary)
- Produces useful recall questions in a drill

Avoid:
- Concepts named after specific model numbers or vendor names
  ("E3631A" is not a concept; "triple-channel PSU SCPI addressing" is)
- Concepts so generic they produce a useless lesson
  ("adding a class" — skip this)
- Concepts already well-covered in the existing lesson library
  (check docs/learning/PROGRESS.md first)

---

## FAILURE HANDLING POLICY

This policy applies to the entire session.

**Never stop the run because one issue failed.**
**Never silently skip — always label and comment.**
**Never attempt a risky or irreversible action without a prior commit.**

If at any point the session hits a situation that is genuinely ambiguous,
dangerous, or requires a human decision not covered by the issue:
1. Stop work on that issue
2. Label it needs-human
3. Leave a detailed comment explaining exactly what decision is needed
4. Move to the next issue

The goal is to maximize completed work, not to force through stuck issues.

---

## NOTE ON AUTOMATED LEARNING GENERATION

In a live session, /teach, /drill-me, and /terms end with in-chat
knowledge checks. In overnight autonomous mode, skip the interactive
questions and put that energy into making the HTML content more thorough
instead. The HTML is the deliverable — the in-chat conversation is not.

lines: +// Palette colors resolved once per character and handed to every recipe.
+// The ONE place part ids map to shapes — the graphics-pack seam (issue
+// #101). A content pack is exactly: catalog rows (PartDef/PartPalette
+// with their `pack` tag) + recipe branches HERE. Nothing else — not the
+// assembly, not the picker, not the render loop — changes when a pack is
+// added. `at` is the part's anchor (bottom-center) and `dim` its declared
+// size, both already in world units (contract scale applied); a part
+// without a bespoke branch falls through to the generic declared-box
+// recipe at the bottom, so new catalog rows always render.
+void drawPartRecipe(const PartDef& part, const Vec3& at, const Vec3& dim,
+    const float cy = at.y + dim.y * 0.5f;  // box center height
+        // Tapered trunk: narrow shoulders over a wider base.
+        DrawSphere({at.x, at.y + dim.y * 0.3f, at.z}, dim.x * 0.5f, c.hair);
+        // Oversized cap sunk into the head reads as a bowl cut.
+        DrawSphere({at.x, at.y - dim.y * 0.55f, at.z}, dim.x * 0.5f, c.hair);
+        // Vertically stretched sphere reads as a longer, oval face.
+        // A rounded cap plus a small tail behind the head.
+        DrawSphere({at.x, at.y + dim.y * 0.30f, at.z}, dim.x * 0.5f, c.hair);
+        // A single tall narrow crest running front-to-back.
+        DrawCube({at.x, cy, at.z}, dim.x * 0.5f, dim.y, dim.z, c.hair);
+        // A flat crown sunk onto the head plus a forward brim (+z is
+        // the character's front, same as the eye sockets).
+        // A tight crop: one thin disc hugging the scalp.
+        // A sunken crown with side spheres reaching down over the ears.
+        DrawSphere({at.x, at.y - dim.y * 0.35f, at.z}, dim.x * 0.50f, c.hair);
+        // A cluster of small spheres: a lower row of three, two on top.
+        // A rounded cap with a bun perched top-back.
+        DrawSphere({at.x, at.y - dim.y * 0.25f, at.z}, dim.x * 0.52f, c.hair);
+        // A slab swept to one side, with a longer fall down that side.
+        DrawCube({at.x - dim.x * 0.12f, cy, at.z}, dim.x * 0.76f, dim.y,

exhaustive combo test gains the fifth axis (3423 -> 8437 assertions);

Two jobs in the repo at /Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs (branch feature/mii-style-visual-overhaul, built at ./build/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs).

CONTEXT: This milestone restyled all characters toward a cartoony Mii/Tomodachi-Life look, all through ONE shared parts library used by roaming NPCs, the character creator, and the player avatar. Changes: Mii proportions (head ≈ half the body+head silhouette), inverted-hull dark outlines on every character, a cohesive pastel palette set, a new Mouth category (smile/open/neutral/o), expanded hair/eyes/bodies, and ten art-directed townsfolk (cop = cap + visor + slate + neutral mouth; baker = pear body + bun + smile; librarian = glasses + bob; musician = mohawk + wink; tourist = bowl cut + o-mouth + sky palette...).

JOB 1 — CONSISTENCY GATE (verdict required):
Judge across several screenshots whether every character on screen reads as ONE cohesive cartoon art source:
- Mii proportions everywhere (oversized head, small body) — no old-proportioned figure anywhere.
- Dark outline rims on every character (spheres AND boxes), no glaring hull artifacts (double edges, gaps, flicker bands).
- Mouths visible on faces at close range.
- Pastel palette cohesion — no character that looks like it belongs to another game.
- The one player-created character in saves (position: query saves/characters.sqlite3 table character_persona for its "position = x, z" line) must be indistinguishable in construction from townsfolk.
NOTE: the creator-preview and first-person avatar arm cannot be captured headlessly (menu/attack input needed) — do NOT try; they're flagged for human verification separately.

JOB 2 — FREE PLAYTEST SWEEP (observations only):
Explore like a player would, via screenshots from varied vantages and hours, and note CONCRETE visual/game-feel observations beyond this milestone's own changes — things that look off, feel dead, or could be better (e.g. environment vs character style mismatch, lighting, street life, prop scale, emptiness, sky, whatever surfaces).   caffeinate -u -t 3

content.text:
All screenshots are saved. Here is my full QA report.

## JOB 1 — Consistency Gate

**Verdict: PASS WITH CAVEATS**

- **Mii proportions everywhere** — PASS. Verified via both code (`CategorySpec`/socket math in `src/core/CharacterParts.cpp`: head fraction of total assembled height computes to ~49% for `body_block`+`head_block`, similarly generous for round bodies) and direct pixel measurement on `baker_closeup.png` (head ~60% of figure), `player_char_closeup.png` (head ~65%), and `musician_closeup4.png` (head ~60%, box family). No old-proportioned figure found anywhere.
- **Dark outline rims on every character, spheres and boxes, no glaring hull artifacts** — PASS for the actual composite geometry. Zoomed crops of round heads (baker, player character) and box heads/bodies (musician, cop's real head+torso once separated from the emote overlay — see caveat) all show a single, crisp, unbroken black rim with clean corners; no double edges, no gaps, no flicker bands. **CAVEAT:** a pre-existing, non-Mii legacy system — the per-mood "emote billboard" (`RaylibRenderer.cpp` ~line 582, `DrawBillboard(... faceTexture(face) ...)` at fixed height 2.45) — draws a flat, un-outlined circular face floating above the composite head whenever `mood != Neutral`. It visually reads as a second, disconnected head with none of the new outline/style treatment. Because the documented capture recipe requires `--frames N`, which sets `smokeRun = true` and forces `face = i % 6` (main.cpp line 1064), **5 of every 6 NPCs will show this artifact in any screenshot taken the documented way** — confirmed on `cop_closeup2.png`/`cop_fullbody.png` (Angry emote) vs. `musician_closeup4.png` (index lands on Neutral, no emote, clean head visible). This also fires in normal gameplay whenever an NPC's mood shifts, not just in scripted runs.
- **Mouths visible on faces at close range** — PASS. Confirmed on baker (flat neutral-ish bar), player character (smile bar+dots), musician (bar+dots), all legible at close range.
- **Pastel palette cohesion** — PASS. Every screenshot (plaza, street, park, night, morning) shows the same warm-peach-skin / muted-hair / saturated-pastel-outfit family; nothing reads as an asset from another game.
- **Player-created character indistinguishable from townsfolk** — PASS. `custom_1783494792_10` (position 0, 8) uses `body_round/head_oval/eyes_happy/hair_none/mint`, same catalog, sockets, scale contract, and outline pass as authored NPCs (side-by-side with a bystander NPC in `player_char_closeup.png`). Its stored `look_json` predates the Mouth category and has no `"mouth"` key; the documented fallback (`mouth_smile` default in `CharacterLook::fromJson`) resolves this correctly and it visually reads as an intentional smile.

## JOB 2 — Free Playtest Sweep

1. Date: 2026-07-10 (session 7 — Mii-style visual overhaul, milestone #12)

**Verdict: NO migration. raylib is not a blocker for the Mii/Tomodachi
target.** The look is low-poly rounded shapes + flat color + dark outlines:
flat-shaded palette primitives were already the baseline; inverted-hull
outlines need only the rlgl calls the composite renderer already uses;
proportions/palette are catalog data. A migration (Unity/Godot) would strand
the C++ core, 182 tests, and the PR chain to buy rendering features a toon
style doesn't use. No migration plan document produced because none is
recommended. (Full reasoning: .claude/plans/mii-style-visual-overhaul.md.)

## Session 7 summary — issues #101-#107, one branch, PR below
| Issue | What landed | Commit |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| #101 | pack tags + recipes isolated behind ONE dispatch (graphics-pack seam); pixel-identical | 98e04a9 |
| #102 | Mii proportions (head ≈ half the body+head silhouette) + cohesive pastel palettes — pure data | 56df349 |
| #103 | inverted-hull outlines (1.06x, front-cull, batch-drained; grouped passes) | 4b4f4a8 |
| #104 | Mouth as fifth category + six-item look, five-item/no-key back-compat | 8b0c70d |
| #105 | catalog floors: hair 18, eyes 10, bodies 6, mouths 4, palettes 12; 7 persona looks refreshed | c8188d6 |
| #106 | player avatar: same creator page in avatar mode, reserved store row, viewmodel tint | f487dd1 |
| #107 | visual gate + free playtest (below) | — |

## Decisions logged (autonomy brief)
- **Proportion metric refined** from the scaffold stub: hair height varies
  per look, so the pinned measure is head.y/(headSocket.y+head.y) in
  0.48-0.60 — lands the plan's "~40-45% of standing height" once hair joins.
- **Five-item look lines and pre-Mouth stored JSON default to mouth_smile**
  (not a per-name hash for the one slot): preserves each character's
  authored identity, simpler, and Tomodachi mouths are mostly smiles.
- **eyes_star and body_broad deliberately use the generic recipes** (big
  pupils / declared box) — the fallback path is a feature, exercised.
- **Avatar lives in the existing CharacterStore look table** under reserved
  id `player_avatar`; look-only rows never spawn (loadAll needs both
  records) — pinned by test.
- **Emote-billboard style clash NOT fixed** (gate passed; it's finding #1
  below and the brief says observations are not acted on).

## Visual-QA gate (subagent): PASS with caveats
- Mii proportions everywhere (measured ~60% head on close-ups) ✓
- Single crisp outline rim on sphere AND box families, no artifacts ✓
- Mouths legible at close range ✓; pastel cohesion across all shots ✓
- Player-created character indistinguishable (its pre-Mouth stored look
  correctly resolved to the default smile) ✓
- **Caveat:** the legacy mood-emote billboard (un-outlined flat face
  floating at 2.45u) clashes with the new style; smoke runs (--frames)
  force emotes on 5/6 NPCs so screenshots overstate it, but it also shows
  in normal play on mood shifts. Recorded as finding #1.
- Shots: docs/qa/screenshots/mii-style/ (best: musician_closeup4,
  baker_closeup, player_char_closeup).

## Playtest findings (observations ONLY — not acted on, per the brief)
1. Mood-emote billboard is now the biggest cohesion breaker (no outline,
   disconnected second face) — retire for composites or restyle to match;
   composite heads have real mouths now.
2. Night (h23) has no lit windows or streetlamp glow — reads as "day with a
   dark filter", not a night city.
3. Dusk (h20) tints the whole frame one flat rust-orange — reads dust-storm,
   not sunset; check the grading curve at that hour.
4. Plaza is a huge flat beige plane with 2-3 NPCs and no props; park is
   fountain+bench+two plants — neither reads lived-in or distinct.
5. Street clutter (box, lone shrub) floats in open ground with no
   relationship to storefronts.
6. Building facades repeat one window-grid module palette-swapped.
7. Roads are 6+ lanes wide vs pedestrian-scale shops and 0-2 cars — streets
   feel oversized and empty.
8. NPCs idle in open space; nobody uses benches/doorways/conversation poses
   — "figures parked in a lot", not street life.
9. mouth_smile reads as "bar with two dots" at distance; a slight upward
   curve would sell the smile better.
10. Street-furniture variety is thin (plants + traffic lights); 1-2 more
    prop types would help.

## Test status
Green at every commit; final: **182 cases / 31,730 assertions, 0 failed,
1 skipped** (llm_live). The exhaustive combo test now sweeps 17,280
part combinations. Game builds clean.

## Needs human verification (not headlessly capturable)
- Creator page in avatar mode (menu + typing input): open "Edit My Avatar",
  restyle, Save; restart and confirm persistence.
- First-person avatar tint: punch and pistol hand should wear your palette.
- Outline stability in MOTION (hull flicker only shows when moving).

## Suggested first move
Play 5 minutes: walk the plaza (the townsfolk are transformed), open
Edit My Avatar, pick a palette, then punch — your arm wears it.

Lesson 0025 · Rendering · from PR #108 (#103, milestone #12)

Inverted-Hull Outlines in an Immediate-Mode Renderer

The Mii-style pass needed every character wrapped in a clean dark line — the single strongest "this is a cartoon" signal. There was no shader pipeline for it, and none was needed: the classic inverted hull does it with the same draw calls the character already uses.

The trick in one paragraph

Draw the object twice. First a slightly enlarged copy in the outline color with front faces culled — so the camera sees only the far, inside-out side of the inflated shell. Then draw the real object normally on top. The real geometry covers the shell everywhere except a thin rim around the silhouette: that rim is the outline, and it follows the silhouette from every angle for free.

Ours, concretely (RaylibRenderer.cpp)

rlDrawRenderBatchActive();                 // flush what came before
rlSetCullFace(RL_CULL_FACE_FRONT);         // show only back faces
for (const PlacedPart& placed : assembled.parts) {
    rlPushMatrix();                        // inflate about the PART's center
    rlTranslatef(at.x, cy, at.z);
    rlScalef(1.06f, 1.06f, 1.06f);
    rlTranslatef(-at.x, -cy, -at.z);
    drawPartRecipe(*placed.part, at, dim, outlineColors);  // all near-black
    rlPopMatrix();
}
rlDrawRenderBatchActive();                 // flush the outline pass
rlSetCullFace(RL_CULL_FACE_BACK);          // restore
// ...then the normal color pass, unchanged.
  • Same recipes, different colors. Because #101 isolated every part shape behind drawPartRecipe, the outline pass is the SAME function with an all-black palette — new parts get outlines for free, including future graphics packs.
  • Inflate about the part's center, not the figure's feet: scaling about the origin would push high parts (hair) outward more than low parts and the rim thickness would vary up the body.
  • Uniform screen-ish thickness comes from the fixed 1.06 factor at roughly uniform character size (everyone is contract-scaled to 1.8u, so 6% is ~5cm of rim everywhere).

Why the batch drains matter

raylib's immediate shapes don't hit the GPU per call — they accumulate in an rlgl batch that flushes later. A GL state change like rlSetCullFace takes effect when the batch is drawn, so without an explicit rlDrawRenderBatchActive() before each switch, the cull mode could apply to geometry queued earlier (or the outline pass could render with the wrong culling entirely). That is also why the two passes are grouped per character instead of interleaved per part: two drains per character instead of two per part.

Where inverted hull is weak

  • Hard-edged meshes (boxes). The technique assumes the enlarged shell stays "outside" the original; at sharp corners the shell's faces move apart and can gap. At our small 1.06 factor and chunky proportions the box rims stayed clean — the escalation path (bigger scale → per-recipe opt-out) was authored in the skill file but never needed.
  • Non-uniform scale in recipes (head_oval's squashed sphere) inherits the hull scale fine because the hull wraps the same matrix stack — but a recipe that drew in world space would escape the inflation. Recipes must stay in the character's local frame.
  • Billboards/sprites don't participate — the mood emote billboard has no hull, which is exactly why it now reads as a style clash (playtest finding #1).
The general shape. When a style effect can be expressed as "draw the same thing again with different state" (outlines, drop shadows, glow shells), reuse the exact draw path with different parameters instead of building a parallel one — one recipe function, two passes, and every current and future asset inherits the effect by construction.
State changes in batched renderers. Any time you touch GL state around immediate-mode draws (cull face, blend mode, depth), flush the batch first — invisible reordering bugs otherwise land on whatever happened to share the batch.

Drill 0025 · pairs with lesson 0025

Drill: Inverted-Hull Outlines

1. Why does the rim appear at the silhouette?

The outline copy is drawn with front faces culled. Walk through why the camera ends up seeing a rim only around the object's edge.

Answer

With front faces culled, only the far (inside-out) side of the inflated shell renders. The real object, drawn after, covers that shell everywhere their screen projections overlap — which is everywhere except the band where the 6%-larger shell extends past the real silhouette. That uncovered band is the outline, and it tracks the silhouette from any viewpoint.

2. Inflate about what point — and why not the feet?

Answer

About each PART's own center (translate to center, scale, translate back). Scaling about the figure's feet would displace high parts (hair, head) outward more than low parts — the rim would grow thicker up the body and hair could visibly detach from the head.

3. The missing flush

Someone removes the rlDrawRenderBatchActive() calls around rlSetCullFace. Nothing crashes. What actually goes wrong?

Answer

raylib batches immediate geometry; GL state applies when the batch FLUSHES, not when the call is made. Without draining first, the cull-mode switch can apply to earlier queued geometry (or not yet apply to the outline pass) — outlines silently render with the wrong culling, or unrelated scene geometry drawn in the same batch gets front-culled. Classic invisible reordering bug.

4. Why grouped passes instead of outline+color per part?

Answer

Each cull-face switch forces a batch drain. Interleaving would drain the batch twice per PART (~2×5 per character); grouping the outline pass then the color pass drains twice per CHARACTER. Same image, a fraction of the flushes.

5. One function, two passes

The outline pass required almost no new drawing code. What earlier decision made that true, and what does it buy future graphics packs?

Answer

#101 isolated every part shape behind drawPartRecipe(part, at, dim, colors). The outline pass is the same dispatch called with an all-black color set inside an inflation matrix — so every part, including ones added by future packs, inherits outlines with zero extra work.

6. Where the technique fails

Name two kinds of geometry in this game that inverted hull handles poorly or not at all, and what the mitigation was.

Answer

(1) Hard-edged boxes: at sharp corners the inflated shell can gap; kept the scale small (1.06) and authored an escalation path (bigger scale → per-recipe outline opt-out) — not needed in practice. (2) Billboards (the mood emote): camera-facing sprites have no hull at all — it renders un-outlined and now clashes with the style, recorded as playtest finding #1 rather than fixed (observations-only brief).

7. Transfer it

You want a soft glow behind pickups rendered with the same immediate-mode primitives. Apply the lesson's general shape.

Answer

Same skeleton: re-issue the pickup's existing draw path scaled up, tinted glow-color (maybe additive blend), state changes wrapped in explicit batch flushes, passes grouped. No parallel "glow mesh" pipeline — the one draw path serves both, so every new pickup glows by construction.

The outline pass required almost no new drawing code. What earlier decision made that true, and what does it buy future graphics packs?

Answer

#101 isolated every part shape behind drawPartRecipe(part, at, dim, colors). The outline pass is the same dispatch called with an all-black color set inside an inflation matrix — so every part, including ones added by future packs, inherits outlines with zero extra work.

6. Where the technique fails

Name two kinds of geometry in this game that inverted hull handles poorly or not at all, and what the mitigation was.

Answer

(1) Hard-edged boxes: at sharp corners the inflated shell can gap; kept the scale small (1.06) and authored an escalation path (bigger scale → per-recipe outline opt-out) — not needed in practice. (2) Billboards (the mood emote): camera-facing sprites have no hull at all — it renders un-outlined and now clashes with the style, recorded as playtest finding #1 rather than fixed (observations-only brief).

7. Transfer it

You want a soft glow behind pickups rendered with the same immediate-mode primitives. Apply the lesson's general shape.

Answer

Same skeleton: re-issue the pickup's existing draw path scaled up, tinted glow-color (maybe additive blend), state changes wrapped in explicit batch flushes, passes grouped. No parallel "glow mesh" pipeline — the one draw path serves both, so every new pickup glows by construction.

input.content:
Vocab 0024 · pairs with lesson 0025

Vocab: Inverted-Hull Outlines

inverted hull
An enlarged copy of an object drawn in the outline color with front faces culled, so only a silhouette-hugging rim of it survives behind the real object. The zero-shader cartoon outline.
face culling
Skipping triangles by winding order. BACK culling (normal) hides the far side; FRONT culling (rlSetCullFace(RL_CULL_FACE_FRONT)) hides the near side — the hull trick's key ingredient.
render batch
rlgl's accumulation buffer for immediate-mode shapes: draw calls queue geometry, the GPU sees it at flush time. GL state changes bind at the FLUSH, not the call.
batch drain
rlDrawRenderBatchActive() — an explicit flush. Mandatory before any state change (cull, blend) that must not leak onto geometry already queued.
hull scale
The inflation factor (ours: 1.06 about each part's center). Sets rim thickness; uniform because every character is contract-scaled to the same 1.8u height.
grouped passes
Outline pass for ALL parts, then color pass for all parts — two drains per character instead of two per part. Never interleave state switches per primitive in a batched renderer.
corner gap
The hull failure mode on hard edges: inflated flat faces separate at sharp corners, opening holes in the rim. Mitigations: small scale, per-recipe opt-out, or (elsewhere) post-process outlines.
silhouette rim
The visible band where the hull extends past the real object on screen — the outline itself, which follows the object's edge from every camera angle without any per-view work.

## Milestone #12: Mii-style visual overhaul — done, draft PR #108

**Part A verdict (the one hard-stop check): NO engine migration.** raylib handles the Mii/Tomodachi target natively — the look is flat color + rounded low-poly + dark outlines, and the outline pass needed only rlgl calls already in use. Reasoning recorded in the plan and report; zero migration code written.

**What changed, per issue (one atomic commit each):**
| # | Delivered |
|---|-----------|
| #101 | Graphics-pack seam: `pack` tags + all shape recipes behind one dispatch — a future purchased pack is data + recipes, nothing else. Pixel-identical extraction. |
| #102 | Mii proportions (heads ≈ half the silhouette, pinned by test) + one cohesive pastel palette set. Pure catalog data. |
| #103 | Inverted-hull cartoon outlines on every character — clean rims on spheres *and* boxes. |
| #104 | **Mouths.** Fifth part category, landed exactly along the category-spec extension path; six-item `look =` format with full back-compat (old files/saves default to a smile). |
| #105 | Catalog: hair 18, eyes 10 (glasses, wink…), bodies 6, palettes 12 — floors pinned by test; combo test now sweeps 17,280 combinations. |
| #106 | **Your avatar**: "Edit My Avatar" in the menu reuses the creator page; persists across restarts; your punch arm and pistol hand wear your palette. |
| #107 | Visual-qa gate **PASS** + a 10-item free-playtest findings list in OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md (observations only, untouched per your brief). |

**State:** suite 182 cases / 31,730 assertions green; chain #94 → #99 → #100 → **#108**, nothing merged, main untouched; issues #101–#107 closed `ai-completed`.

**Worth your eyes first:**
1. **Play it** — the townsfolk are transformed (big heads, outlines, expressions). Then Edit My Avatar → pick a palette → punch.
2. **Finding #1** from the playtest is the one real style straggler: the mood-emote billboard (the floating face) has no outline and now reads as off-style. It's the natural next `/idea` — along with the night-lighting and plaza-emptiness observations (all 10 are in OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md).
3. Three things need human verification that headless runs can't reach: the avatar flow end-to-end, the creator page's new fifth row, and outline stability while characters move.

| Who | Where at 09:00 |
|---|---|
| Gus (hot-dog) | plaza center (6, 0) |
| Tourist Yuki + your created character | plaza (-8, 10) / (0, 8) |

- Is there a simpler version that delivers most of the value?

to a developer (or the overnight session) without them needing to ask
you anything.

```markdown
Date: [date]
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: S / M / L / XL

should understand this in 30 seconds.]

cannot do now.]

[Explicit list of things NOT included. This prevents scope creep
during implementation.]

[Files, modules, or systems this touches. Be specific.]
- `src/path/to/file.py` — [why it changes]
- `src/path/to/other.cpp` — [why it changes]
- New files needed: [list]

[Ordered steps. Each step should be independently committable.]

1. [Step 1 — what it produces]
2. [Step 2 — builds on step 1]
3. [Step 3 — etc.]

[Testable conditions that define "done". Each one should be
verifiable by running a test or observing a specific behaviour.]

- [ ] [Given X, when Y, then Z]
- [ ] [Given X, when Y, then Z]
- [ ] Tests pass: [specific test file or command]

[What can go wrong and how each case is handled.]

| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| [case] | [what happens] |

[Anything still unresolved that will need a decision during implementation.

[If this plan should become overnight issues, list them here as a
```

Goal: A trait system for NPC personalities — traits are data (behavior
rules + example lines) composed into the persona prompt — plus a lightweight
rating loop so I can mark good/bad responses and have that shape future
behavior. No model training in this ticket.

Context: This is prompt-conditioning, deliberately not fine-tuning. Traits
work through the existing persona-in-prompt pipeline. The rating loop's job
is to grow each trait's few-shot example set from responses I actually
liked, and record rules from ones I didn't.

Scope:
1. Trait data model — {name, behavior_rules[], example_exchanges[]},
   attachable to any character (premade or created). Multiple traits
   compose into one persona prompt in a defined order (backstory, traits,
   examples, memory summary).
2. Character creator integration — pick traits when creating a character;
   also editable on existing characters.
3. Rating capture — an unobtrusive in-conversation way to mark a response
   good/bad. Good → stored as a candidate example line for the active
   trait(s); bad → logged with the response for my later review. Candidates
   go to a review file, NOT auto-promoted into prompts — I curate.
4. Prompt-order check — ensure trait rules are asserted after the memory
   summary in assembly order, so long-conversation drift doesn't dilute
   traits.
5. Document (do not implement) the escalation path: what data this system
   accumulates that a future LoRA fine-tune could use if conditioning
   demonstrably fails.

Goal: NPCs can talk to each other, and the player can form a small group —
ask an NPC to follow you, walk to another NPC, and have a three-way (or
N-way) conversation instead of strictly one-on-one.

Context: Builds on the shared world-fact bus and per-NPC memory. Group
conversation is turn-based over the same structured-JSON dialogue pipeline:
each turn, one participant's persona prompt is assembled (their persona +
traits + their view of relevant facts + the conversation so far) and they
respond. NPC-to-NPC exchanges write facts to the world bus like any other
conversation.

Scope:
1. Follow mechanic — ask an NPC (subject to affinity/persona willingness)
   to follow; simple follow movement.
2. Group conversation state — a participant list instead of a single NPC;
   speaking order resolved simply (round-robin or addressed-by-name);
   player messages can address the group or a named participant.
3. NPC-to-NPC turns — when it's an NPC's turn responding to another NPC,
   same pipeline, with the other NPC's last line as input. Cap consecutive
   NPC-to-NPC turns (e.g. 2–3) before returning to the player so
   conversations don't run away without them.

   falls out naturally from the group mechanism; otherwise list as
   follow-up, don't force it.

   the world bus attributed to whoever said them.
